title: The Impact of The Gig Economy on The Vietnamese Labor Market
abstract: The gig economy, also referred to as the contract economy or freelance economy, represents an economic model in which individuals typically engage in part-time, temporary, or contract-based work rather than full-time employment with a single company. While the concept is not new globally, it remains relatively novel in Vietnam. With its inherent flexibility and advantages, the gig economy in Vietnam has been exerting multifaceted impacts on the labor market. This paper examines both the positive and negative effects of the gig economy on Vietnam’s labor market and proposes policy recommendations to enhance labor regulations and worker protection mechanisms. The study employs qualitative methods, using secondary data from official statistics and reputable surveys, supplemented by a questionnaire survey of 490 workers in major cities. Findings reveal that while the gig economy expands labor supply, increases flexibility, and creates new opportunities, it also poses challenges related to job stability, social protection, and skill development.

title: Rising market power and its political discontents
abstract: Abstract How does market power affect the political behavior of small business owners? As the growing market power of large multinational firms has fundamentally changed the opportunity structure for small businesses and their beneficiaries, we try to understand how those economic developments influence European democracies. We argue that growing market power lowers small business owners’ trust in key democratic institutions and the functioning of markets, driving them to reject incumbents and shift their support to radical right parties. We employ firm-level, individual-level, and regional-level data on fourteen European countries to test this argument. Our findings indicate that rising market power, measured by combining mergers and increases in market concentration, is associated with the declining economic performance of micro-firms. In turn, mergers and the declining economic share of these firms are robust predictors of anti-incumbent and increased radical right voting both at the individual and constituency levels. This article provides the first analysis of the effect of market concentration on rich democracies and, in doing so, offers a novel explanation for the surprising radical right support among small business owners in Europe.

title: Emotion Regulation and Prosocial Behavior among Eleventh-Grade Students at SMA Negeri 1 Talamau, Indonesia
abstract: Emotion regulation is widely assumed to support adolescents’ prosocial behavior, yet evidence from Indonesian senior high schools remains inconsistent, particularly in rural settings. This study described emotion regulation and prosocial behavior among eleventh-grade students at SMA Negeri 1 Talamau, West Pasaman, Indonesia, and examined the relationship between these variables. A quantitative correlational design involved 65 students selected from a population of 187 through proportionate random sampling. Data were collected using Likert-type emotion regulation and prosocial behavior scales comprising 37 items (α = .918) and 38 items (α = .937), respectively. Descriptive percentage analysis and Pearson product-moment correlation were conducted following normality and linearity testing. Most students exhibited high emotion regulation (61.54%), while nearly half demonstrated very high prosocial behavior (49.23%). No students were classified in the low or very low categories. The correlation was positive but very weak and statistically nonsignificant (r = .185, p = .141). These findings provide no evidence of a statistically significant linear association within this sample and caution against assuming that higher emotion regulation necessarily corresponds to greater prosocial behavior in this school context. The study contributes contextual evidence to research on adolescent soc…

title: Corporate Transparency and Disclosure Obligations in India
abstract: Efficient disclosure methods ensure that investors obtain precise, prompt and thorough information about the financial status, governance framework and operational activities of companies. In India, corporate transparency and disclosure obligations secure accountability through mandatory reporting under the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. These rules promote investor trust by requiring timely financial statements, annual reporting, a governance framework and ESG disclosures. This paper examines the legal provisions governing corporate disclosure in India under the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and assesses the role of the Securities and Exchange Board of India in promoting transparency and safeguarding investors. It offers an examination of investor protection, corporate responsibility and transparency in the Indian capital markets, analyses the extent to which corporate disclosure practices protect investors' interests and enhance market transparency, and identifies issues and gaps in the existing disclosure system. The research also examines the effects of insufficient disclosure on investor trust.
venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Analytics and AI in Management
abstract: The modern business world is changing rapidly with the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics. Earlier, businesses depended mainly on past data to understand what had already happened. Today, AI and analytics help organizations predict future situations and make better decisions based on available data. This change has given rise to the idea of “augmented intelligence”, in which AI works together with people to support their decisions instead of replacing them. This paper studies how the use of AI and predictive analytics is affecting businesses and the way managers make decisions. It focuses on the use of AI in daily work, the automation of routine tasks, access to analytical tools and the changing role of human judgment in decision-making. A survey of 35 management professionals (N = 35) was conducted to understand their practical experience of AI and analytics in the workplace. The results show that AI is already being used in many professional roles: about 88.6% of respondents said that their work involves both AI and analytics, and 82.9% said that AI has significantly reduced their workload.

title: Unlocking Human Capital Development through Technopreneurship Education: Evidence on the Moderating Influence of Entrepreneurial Mindset from Niger State, Nigeria
abstract: Purpose: Graduate unemployment remains a persistent challenge in Niger State, Nigeria, despite growing investments in entrepreneurial education. This study examines the moderating effect of entrepreneurial mindset (EMS) on the relationship between technopreneurship education and human capital development (HCD) among tertiary institution students. Methodology: A quantitative research design was adopted using data from 500 students selected from a population of 9,135 students across tertiary institutions in Niger State through purposive sampling. The study assessed key dimensions of technopreneurship education—Business and Financial Literacy (BFL), Entrepreneurial Skills (ES), Innovation and Creativity (IC), and Technological Competence (TC). Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), with EMS specified as a moderating variable. Results: The findings indicate that BFL (β = 0.194, p = 0.002), ES (β = 0.218, p = 0.001), IC (β = 0.146, p = 0.004), and TC (β = 0.224, p = 0.000) exert significant positive effects on HCD. Although EMS shows only a marginal direct effect on HCD (β = 0.092, p = 0.054), it significantly strengthens the relationships between TC and HCD (p = 0.000) and between BFL and HCD (p = 0.006). Novelty and contribution: The study advances technopreneurship literature by demonstrating that entrepreneurial mindset enhances t…

title: Clinical management of metachromatic leukodystrophy cases identified in the German and Austrian Newborn screening pilots
abstract: Abstract Background Metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) is a rapidly progressive leukodystrophy that leads to severe disability and early death if untreated. Autologous hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell gene therapy (HSPC-GT, atidarsagene autotemcel, arsa-cel) for early onset subtypes and allogenic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for late onset disease substantially alters disease progression for early onset disease when administered before symptom onset, creating a strong rationale for newborn screening (NBS). At the same time, NBS technique for MLD in dried blood spots has recently been demonstrated to be robust and highly accurate. The aim was to give real-world results from the world’s first NBS pilots for clinical management and treatment of identified children. Methods Between September 2021 and July 2025, 359,282 newborns underwent NBS for MLD in two different laboratories in Germany and Austria using a three-tier algorithm integrating sulfatide quantification, arylsulfatase A (ARSA) activity measurement, and ARSA sequencing. Screen-positive infants underwent a predefined care pathway including standardized confirmatory diagnostics, genotype-based and biochemical prediction of disease onset, clinical assessment and management guiding early treatment and surveillance at the qualified treatment center (QTC) in Tübingen. Judicial Trends on Marital Agreements: Scope for Recognizing Prenuptial Contracts in India
abstract: Prenuptial agreements occupy an ambiguous position in Indian law. No specific legislation governs their formation, validity or enforcement, and their status must be determined by reference to Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which renders void agreements whose object or consideration is opposed to public policy. Early cases such as Tekait Mon Mohini Jemadai v. Basanta Kumar Singh and Krishna Aiyar v. Balammal reflect a near-complete judicial refusal to enforce agreements that interfered with cohabitation or conjugal rights, or that facilitated separation, because these were treated as core incidents of marriage that could not be recast by anticipatory bargain. Indian courts have nonetheless been more accommodating towards postnuptial settlements, mediated financial arrangements and transparent financial planning, suggesting that the judicial stance is one of differentiated, rather than absolute, non-recognition. This paper submits that provisions on property division, maintenance and the relinquishment of future rights should be assessed under both contract law and matrimonial law, and that a blanket waiver of maintenance should not take precedence over the court’s statutory oversight. It advances a fairness-based model of limited recognition grounded in free consent, independent legal advice, full financial disclosure and judicial review at the stage of enforcement…

title: Fluid–substrate coupled controls on mineral‑phase selection in the Kunlun hydrothermal system
abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation at submarine hydrothermal vents transfers redox‑sensitive elements from the lithosphere to the ocean. However, conventional plume and sediment‑trap sampling poorly preserves particle‑scale signatures generated at reactive interfaces, hindering robust interpretation of near‑vent mineralization. Here, we deployed open‑cell Fe, Ni, Cu, and Fe–Ni foams within diffuse low‑temperature alkaline fluids of the serpentinization‑driven Kunlun hydrothermal field. The results reveal that the hydrothermal system mainly favoured goethite‑dominated Fe‑oxyhydroxide coatings, while ambient seawater promoted lepidocrocite precipitation. Substrate chemistry further modulated mineral‑phase selection: NiO precipitated on Ni‑bearing substrates, hematite occurred exclusively on Fe–Ni foam, and maghemite formed on Cu foam. The Fe foam yielded the thickest Fe‑rich deposits, fed both by hydrothermal Fe supply and anodic dissolution of the metallic substrate. For serpentinization‑related hydrothermal systems, naturally occurring reactive mineral surfaces—Fe–Ni alloys such as awaruite—behave as geochemically active interfaces that steer mineralization, rather than as passive particle collectors. Such interfacial effects can improve reconstructions of mineral assemblages and improve reconstructions of lithosphere‑to‑ocean element fluxes in serpentinization‑driven systems.

title: Underground Coal Mine Fires in Dhanbad, Jharkhand: A Need for Comprehensive State Legislation to Protect the Right to Life and Environment
abstract: The underground coal mine fires in the Jharia Coalfield of Dhanbad, Jharkhand, constitute one of India’s longest-running environmental and humanitarian crises. Burning continuously for over a century, these fires have caused extensive environmental degradation, air pollution, land subsidence, destruction of valuable coal reserves, and widespread displacement of local communities. Continuous exposure to toxic gases and particulate matter has resulted in serious public health concerns, including respiratory diseases, cardiovascular disorders, and other chronic illnesses, thereby threatening the fundamental right to life and a healthy environment guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. Although several central enactments, including the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Mines Act, 1952, provide a general framework for environmental protection and mining regulation, they do not adequately address the unique challenges posed by underground coal mine fires. This article critically examines the constitutional and statutory obligations of the Union and the State Governments in preventing mine fires, protecting public health, ensuring environmental restoration, and rehabilitating affected communities. It argues that the absence of a comprehensive…

title: The Influence of Price, Promotion, and Location on Meat Purchase Decisions at Toko Daging Indonesia in Selincah, Jambi City
abstract: Meat purchase decisions may be shaped by pricing, promotional communication, and convenient store access. This study examined the individual and joint associations of price, promotion, and location with meat purchase decisions at Toko Daging Indonesia in Selincah, Jambi City. A quantitative associative approach with a survey design involved 97 consumers selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through multiple linear regression in IBM SPSS Statistics 25. Price (β = .375, p < .001), promotion (β = .342, p < .001), and location (β = .533, p < .001) were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions. The regression model was statistically significant (F = 34.142, p < .001), with the three predictors jointly explaining 50.9% of the variation in purchase decisions. Location had the largest standardized coefficient among the predictors. These findings indicate that pricing, promotion, and location are relevant to consumer purchase decisions in this retail setting. The study provides contextual evidence to inform meat retail marketing strategies and highlights the importance of integrating competitive pricing, relevant promotional communication, and convenient store access.

title: Bridging the Farm-to-Input Gap: Opportunity Recognition and Design Thinking in a Philippine Animal Agri-Products Trading Company
abstract: Animal agri-products trading companies occupy a critical but under-examined position in the Philippine livestock value chain, connecting farmers, veterinarians, and feed mills to veterinary, breeding, nutritional, and biosecurity inputs. Despite the sector's importance to food security and rural livelihoods, limited research examines how such companies recognize market opportunities and build viable, trusted enterprises. This study, conducted on a start-up Philippine animal agri-products trading company (pseudonym "AgriVet Co."), determined the extent to which the company practices opportunity recognition, creativity and ideation, design thinking application, trust-building and relationship management, and feasibility validation; examined the relationships among these five domains; explored, through the founder's and staff's experiences, how the company's market opportunity was recognized, creatively explored, and validated; and proposed evidence-informed strategies to strengthen these areas. A mixed-method case study combined a five-point Likert-scale survey of 14 respondents with key informant interviews of the founder and three senior staff, covering all 18 direct-hire personnel. Weighted means assessed each practice's extent, and thematic analysis examined the qualitative data; reliability was excellent (Cronbach's alpha = 0.89). The company practiced the examined behaviors…

Sheep-feeding practices and factors associated with fodder-tree integration in Northern Benin (West Africa)
abstract: Abstract Feed availability remains a major factor limiting animal productivity in sheep production systems in West Africa, especially during the dry season. This study analyzed sheep-feeding practices and examined factors associated with herders’ integration of fodder trees into sheep feeding in northern Benin. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 240 herders from six villages across three municipalities of the Borgou Department: N’Dali, Parakou, and Tchaourou. Data were analyzed using descriptive and comparative statistics, complemented by a binary logistic regression model. Results revealed marked seasonal complementarity in feeding practices: natural pastures were used by more than 93% of herders during the rainy season. Fodder-tree integration was reported by 123 of the 240 herders (51.3%) and differed significantly between municipalities. All herders classified as fodder-tree users reported using these resources during the dry season. The hot dry season was the most frequently reported period of forage shortage. Among fodder-tree users, the most commonly used species were Ficus nymphaeifolia, Mangifera indica, Khaya senegalensis, and Afzelia africana , mainly harvested through pruning and cutting. title: Household Solar Adoption in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal: Affordability, Energy Security and Policy Pathways for Sustainable Development
abstract: Nepal’s scattered settlements, difficult topography and fuel-import dependence make a strong case for decentralized household solar energy, but adoption depends on affordability, operational performance and policy support. This study examines the financial viability of household solar systems in Kathmandu Valley and their implications for rural energy access and sustainable development. A mixed-method design combined a structured survey of 110 households across Kathmandu, Bhaktapur and Lalitpur, open-ended interviews with 10 energy-sector experts, and a review of relevant policy and literature. Internal consistency of the 12-item instrument was high (Cronbach’s α = 0.941). Most respondents reported annual solar generation of 2,001–4,000 kWh, system efficiency of 60–80%, expected lifespan of 10–20 years and annual energy cost savings of NPR 10,001–20,000. Annual savings were positively associated with annual generation (r = 0.533), energy efficiency (r = 0.573), reliability (r = 0.642), maintenance-interval coding (r = 0.727) and expected operational lifespan (r = 0.714), all p < 0.001. An exploratory regression using the composite financial variable to predict financial feasibility yielded R = 0.489, R2 = 0.239, F(1, 108) = 33.984, p < 0.001, explaining approximately 23.9% of the variance in financial feasibility. Expert evidence identified cost, awareness, storage and policy b…

Tuning structural, optical, charge storage, and electronic transport properties of graphene oxide through functional group engineering
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effect of oxidation temperature on the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties of graphene oxide (GO) synthesized at 75, 95, and 115 °C. Increasing the oxidation temperature resulted in a reduction in crystallite size from 9.95 ± 1.24 to 8.05 ± 0.49 nm and a decrease in the interlayer spacing, accompanied by partial reorganization of the sp² carbon domains. The electrical properties were significantly improved, with enhanced carrier transport at higher oxidation temperatures. The optical band gap decreased from 4.11 to 3.69 eV, while the Urbach energy increased from 285 to 625 meV, indicating enhanced energetic disorder and band-tail formation. Electrochemical analysis revealed improved charge-transfer kinetics, with the charge-transfer resistance decreasing from 911 to 598 Ω and the relaxation time decreasing from 0.842 to 0.671 ms. The electrochemical response also showed a predominantly diffusion-controlled charge-storage contribution, while the apparent diffusion coefficient decreased from 2.094 × 10⁻⁷ to 5.792 × 10⁻⁸ cm²/s with increasing oxidation temperature. In contrast, the specific capacitance decreased from 668 to 328 F/g, which is attributed to the reduction of oxygen-containing redox-active sites and restricted ion accessibility. title: Environmental strategy and digital transformation: pathways to green innovation and sustainable performance in Vietnamese manufacturing firms
abstract: Abstract Manufacturing firms in emerging economies face dual pressures to improve both environmental performance and digital technology adoption. Both themes have attracted extensive research attention on their own, yet few studies ask whether—and through what mechanisms—a proactive environmental strategy is associated with a stronger orientation toward both digital transformation and green innovation as parallel routes to sustainable performance. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study develops and tests an integrated model in which proactive environmental strategy is examined as an organisational-level antecedent associated with digital transformation and green innovation among Vietnamese manufacturing firms. Data from 602 manufacturing enterprises were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Proactive environmental strategy is positively associated with both digital transformation and green innovation, and each of these, in turn, is positively associated with sustainable performance—a pattern consistent with partial mediation. Four antecedents predict proactive environmental strategy: organisational support, dynamic environment, green transformational leadership, and stakeholder pressure. title: Resultados Internacionales de Aprendizaje 2025 y Propuesta de Mejora para una Zona Escolar Rural de Puebla, México
abstract: La novena aplicación del principal programa internacional de evaluación de estudiantes de quince años, difundida en 2026, situó a México muy por debajo del promedio internacional en las tres áreas evaluadas y registró un retroceso significativo en matemáticas. El problema abordado es la distancia entre la disponibilidad de evidencia comparada y su uso efectivo en la escala donde se deciden las prácticas de enseñanza. El objetivo fue analizar críticamente esos resultados y traducirlos en una propuesta de mejora operable para una zona escolar de telesecundarias rurales de la Sierra Norte de Puebla, alineada con la meta 4.1 de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo con diseño de revisión documental descriptivo-interpretativa. De cuarenta y ocho documentos identificados se incluyeron veinte, seleccionados por pertinencia, verificabilidad contra la fuente institucional, vigencia y accesibilidad pública. El análisis de contenido se organizó en cuatro categorías. Los hallazgos mostraron que siete de cada diez estudiantes no alcanzaron el umbral mínimo de competencia en matemáticas, que uno de cada doscientos llegó a los niveles altos, que cuatro de cada diez quedaron por debajo del umbral en las tres áreas simultáneamente y que la brecha por condición socioeconómica permaneció estancada durante una década. title: User Perceptions of the Lentera Learning Platform: Reanalysis of a Custom Usability Questionnaire
abstract: This study re-examines user perceptions of the Lentera learning platform using the 30-response, ten-item questionnaire dataset embedded in the source manuscript. The original report applied the alternating System Usability Scale (SUS) scoring rule and obtained 49.16, although all ten administered statements are positively worded and therefore do not match the directionally alternating SUS instrument. Recalculation reproduces the original arithmetic as 49.1667 but confirms that the value cannot be interpreted as a valid SUS score. Direct analysis of the 300 original responses yields an overall mean of 3.40 on the five-point scale, a respondent-level median of 3.45, and an exploratory Cronbach's alpha of 0.944. Item means range from 3.10 for the usefulness of error messages to 3.60 for perceived search efficiency. The strongest corrected item-total relationship is observed for overall satisfaction, while error handling remains the clearest descriptive area for follow-up. These results support a moderate, generally favorable perception of the platform in this sample, but they do not establish task effectiveness, objective efficiency, or a standardized usability grade. The paper therefore distinguishes custom-survey evidence from SUS benchmarking and outlines a more defensible evaluation design for future Lentera studies.

title: Transformasi Digital dalam Akuntansi Keuangan: Systematic Literature Review Menggunakan Pendekatan PRISMA
abstract: Aim: This study aims to analyze the development of digital transformation in financial accounting, identify dominant technologies and research themes, and explore research gaps in the field of digital transformation in financial accounting. Method: This study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. The data consist of scientific articles obtained from Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. A total of 18 articles published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using content analysis with a thematic analysis approach. Results: The findings indicate that blockchain is the most dominant technology in the transformation of financial accounting due to its contribution to transparency, accountability, financial reporting quality, and fraud mitigation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation also play important roles in improving the efficiency of accounting and auditing processes and supporting data-driven decision-making. However, existing research remains largely dominated by conceptual and literature-based studies, while empirical research examining the implementation of digital technologies in accounting practices remains relatively limited. title: Underrated deep-water scleractinian species: an ecological study along the Italian coasts (Mediterranean Sea)
abstract: Abstract Scleractinians are key components of Mediterranean mesophotic and bathyal benthic ecosystems, comprising 30 species known to occur below 40 m. A large ROV dataset, including 625 dives, each corresponding to a distinct geographical site, conducted between 40 and 1825 m across the Italian seas, was used to assess the diversity of this taxon, focusing on the distribution, habitat preferences, and population density of four Data Deficient, yet well-represented species: solitary Caryophyllia cyathus , Paracyathus pulchellus , and Javania cailleti , and colonial Thalamophyllia gasti . The study recorded 18 scleractinian species (representing 60% of the known deep ones) and analysed almost 2600 records of the four target species. Caryophyllia cyathus , Paracyathus pulchellus, and Thalamophyllia gasti were the most common, occurring between 80 and 150 m on inclined outcropping rocks encrusted with coralline algae along the continental platform, with major hotspots in the Tyrrhenian Sea and average densities ranging between 2.4 and 36 individuals or colonies m −2 . Thalamophyllia gasti was observed for the first time in a cave habitat in Southwest Sardinia, forming large colonies. Javania cailleti was recorded at only 4% of the investigated sites, mainly along the Northeast Sardinian canyons, Corse Channel, Dohrn Canyon, and on seamounts between 400 and 550 m. Sistem Kendali LED RGB Berbasis ESP32 Dual-Core dan FreeRTOS dengan Sinkronisasi Multi-Platform
abstract: Sistem pencahayaan cerdas umumnya bergantung pada konektivitas internet sehingga fungsionalitasnya menjadi terbatas ketika akses jaringan tidak tersedia. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengimplementasikan sistem kendali pencahayaan cerdas berbasis mikrokontroler ESP32 dual-core yang mengintegrasikan beberapa platform kendali, yaitu dashboard web React.js, Telegram Bot, dan mechanical switch sebagai kendali lokal. Sistem memanfaatkan Firebase Realtime Database sebagai layanan sinkronisasi berbasis cloud serta dilengkapi fitur adaptive brightness menggunakan sensor LDR untuk menyesuaikan tingkat kecerahan LED secara otomatis berdasarkan kondisi pencahayaan lingkungan. Untuk meningkatkan pengelolaan tugas, FreeRTOS digunakan untuk memisahkan proses komunikasi jaringan dan rendering LED pada inti prosesor yang berbeda. Evaluasi sistem dilakukan melalui pengujian fungsional, latensi, dan penanganan konflik data. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh fungsi sistem berjalan sesuai state machine yang dirancang dengan tingkat keberhasilan operasional 100% (18/18 skenario). Pengujian latensi menghasilkan rata-rata waktu respons 645 ms pada kendali lokal tekan singkat, 1202 ms pada kendali lokal tekan lama, 1844 ms pada dashboard web, 2018 ms pada Telegram Bot, dan 334 ms pada pembaruan telemetri sensor LDR. title: Between scripture and dharma: James Legge’s translation of Record of Buddhist Kingdoms and the transmission of Buddhist thought in Victorian Britain
abstract: Abstract This study examines James Legge’s 1886 English translation of Faxian’s Record of Buddhist Kingdoms (Foguo ji 佛國記), analysing how a Scottish missionary-scholar and Oxford Sinologist became a pivotal mediator of Buddhist thought to Victorian Britain. Through close textual analysis and historical contextualization, the research investigates the productive tension between Legge’s Congregationalist background and his evolving scholarly approach to Buddhist texts during a formative period in Anglophone understanding of Eastern religions. Drawing on recent developments in translation studies, the study situates Legge’s rendering within the broader landscape of nineteenth-century Buddhist translation in both English and French, demonstrating how his methods differed from those of contemporaries such as Samuel Beal and Stanislas Julien. The analysis reveals how Legge’s translation choices, terminological decisions, structural organization, and extensive footnotes, negotiated religious difference with a sophistication unusual for the period, though not without limitations in his handling of Mahayana philosophical concepts. By situating the work within the British Sinological tradition and the emerging field of comparative religion, this research illuminates how Legge’s Record of Buddhist Kingdoms functioned not merely as linguistic rendering but as cultural mediation that both a…

title: Design and Fabrication of Automated Guided Vehicle
abstract: With the advancements of robotic technologies, the industrial environments are adopting more and more aspects of automation to enhance product quality and accuracy and to reduce product cost. One of these aspects is the use of Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) which is gaining importance in industrial logistics and transportation systems. Automated Guided Vehicles are the essential parts of all automated factories.. No human intervention is required for its normal functioning during task-execution stage. In this paper, automated guided vehicle is interfaced with Programmable logic control, which is a new concept in the field of automation and replacement of traditional electro-mechanical control system. In steel plants, a lot of transporting is required inside the plant to help in production, such as, steel coils are transported from one location to another. For this purpose automated guided vehicle systems are very useful. Keywords— guided vehicle,AGV,line follower,smart trolley

title: Food supplement safety and market entry in Germany, Bulgaria, North Macedonia and China
abstract: Objective: To compare market entry controls for food supplements in Germany, Bulgaria, and North Macedonia with the health food framework of mainland China, and assess their relationship to scientific safety evaluation. Methods: A functional comparative legal review of legislation, judgments, and regulatory guidance was combined with a targeted medical literature review. Sources were checked through September 24, 2026. Vitamin B6, green tea extracts, and red yeast rice illustrate dose related toxicity and regulatory responses. Results: Germany uses notification, Bulgaria requires prior registration, and North Macedonia uses a compliance opinion followed by registration. China distinguishes registration involving assessment of safety, health function, and quality controllability from catalog-based filing supported by technical documentation. Chinese health foods and European food supplements are not identical legal categories. The examples demonstrate the importance of total exposure, preparation specific toxicity, and continued reassessment after market entry. An administrative status or regulatory dose ceiling cannot establish universal safety or therapeutic efficacy. Conclusion: Good practice combines transparent classification, proportionate evidence requirements, prominent warnings, controlled product changes, and post-market surveillance. title: Botulinum Neurotoxins in dermatology and interdisciplinary medicine: pharmacology, European regulation, clinical applications, and future directions
abstract: Background: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) has evolved from a cause of foodborne paralysis into a precisely dosed biologic used in aesthetic medicine and multiple therapeutic specialties. Objective: To review its pharmacology, European regulatory landscape, established clinical uses, emerging applications, immunogenicity, health economic concepts, and contemporary procedural epidemiology. Methods: A structured narrative review was updated through 24 September 2026. The original manuscript was used as the conceptual starting point; scientific claims were checked against PubMed indexed reviews and systematic reviews, regulatory claims against European Medicines Agency documents, and procedural statistics against the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery (ISAPS) Global Survey 2024. Results: BoNT inhibits neurotransmitter release through serotype-specific proteolysis of SNARE proteins. European products include both centrally and nationally authorised formulations, and their units are not interchangeable. Established uses include focal hyperhidrosis and several neurological and urological indications. Evidence for temporomandibular disorders, rosacea, scar modulation, chronic pruritus, and psychiatric applications is promising but heterogeneous and generally off-label or investigational. ISAPS reported 7,887,955 botulinum toxin procedures in 2024, 17.4% fewer than in 2023…

title: Clinical and patient reported improvement after metabolic optimization and autologous platelet based facial rejuvenation: a case report
abstract: Response to autologous platelet-based facial rejuvenation is variable, and patient related factors may contribute to this heterogeneity. In this paper is reported a caase of a patient with repeated poor response to previous platelet rich plasma (PRP) procedures which improved after correction of selected nutritional and metabolic abnormalities and subsequent multimodal platelet based treatment. A 61 year old postmenopausal woman, smoker, with arterial hypertension and a history of breast cancer, had undergone five PRP procedures and several chemical peels without satisfactory benefit. Examination showed xerotic, atrophic, photoaged facial skin with solar elastosis, dermal laxity and rhytides. Laboratory assessment revealed borderline thrombocytopenia, low ferritin, vitamin D, vitamin B12, zinc and albumin, with elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone and C-reactive protein. After six weeks of supportive correction, two sessions combining injectable platelet rich fibrin, PRP, microneedling and albumin PRF were performed. At three months, clinical improvement was accompanied by FACE-Q score increases for Satisfaction with Skin (42–81), Satisfaction with Facial Appearance (48–79), Psychological Function (55–76) and Social Function (68–80). Clinical and patient reported improvement followed correction of identified abnormalities and multimodal autologous platelet treatment. Because se…

title: Penerapan Model Transformers untuk Analisis Sentimen pada Survei Tahunan di Aplikasi Market Visit pada PT ASDFE
abstract: PT ASDFE menggunakan survei tahunan untuk mengevaluasi kinerja perusahaan berdasarkan masukan dari mitracabang dan distributor. Seiring dengan peningkatan jumlah responden survei tahunan dari berdampak padalamanya proses analisis data survei tahunan secara manual. volume data yang terus bertambah berdampak waktuyang dibutuhkan untuk mengekstrak opini dan mengevaluasi kinerja perusahaan menjadi tidak efisien. Penelitianini mengembangkan sistem analisis sentimen otomatis berbasis web menggunakan model Transformer, denganmemanfaatkan model pra-latih IndoBERT untuk data berbahasa Indonesia dan RoBERTa untuk data berbahasaInggris. Dataset yang digunakan berasal dari survei tahun 2021–2023 yang telah diberi label untuk proses fine-tuning pada masing-masing model. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan metrik AUC-ROC dengan hasil 0,99untuk IndoBERT dan 1,00 untuk RoBERTa menggunakan 10% dari total dataset, serta pengujian User AcceptanceTest (UAT). Hasil implementasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu mengurangi waktu analisis dari 360 menitmenjadi 35 menit dan mencapai tingkat kepuasan pengguna sebesar 98%. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa modelTransformer efektif dalam mengotomatisasi analisis sentimen dengan tingkat akurasi yang tinggi.

title: Evaluating Virtual Reality Tourism from Tourism Businesses’ Perspectives: Evidence from an Emerging Market and Implications for Strategic Adoption
abstract: Abstract Virtual reality (VR) tourism has emerged as a promising digital innovation capable of transforming tourism experiences and business practices. However, limited empirical research has examined how tourism enterprises evaluate the opportunities and constraints of this technology, particularly in emerging tourism markets. This study investigates tourism businesses’ perceptions of virtual reality tourism in Ho Chi Minh City and proposes a strategic framework for its practical application. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining a questionnaire survey of 260 tourism enterprise representatives with fifteen in-depth interviews with senior managers. The findings indicate that tourism businesses recognize several advantages of VR tourism, including its ability to expand tourism accessibility, enhance destination marketing, and support sustainable tourism by reducing environmental pressure on destinations. At the same time, enterprises identify significant limitations, such as the lack of sensory authenticity, limited social interaction, high technological investment costs, rapid technological obsolescence, and shortages of specialized human resources. Based on these findings, the study proposes a strategic application framework that positions VR tourism as a complementary tool supporting marketing innovation, inclusive tourism development, heritage interpretation, and s…

Organizing Livestock Markets in Kenya's Drylands: Evolution, Institutional Arrangements, Business Models and a Framework for Sustainable Market Coordination
abstract: Abstract: Livestock production is central to the livelihoods and economies of pastoral and agro-pastoral communities in Kenya’s drylands, yet its commercial potential is constrained by fragmented production and marketing systems, weak institutional coordination, inadequate infrastructure, information asymmetries, insecurity, climatic shocks and unequal bargaining power. This study examined the evolution, institutional arrangements and business models underpinning livestock-market organization in Kenya’s drylands and developed a framework for sustainable market coordination. A qualitative-dominant multiple-case study design was employed, focusing on four models: the Organized Livestock Marketing Model, Livestock Marketing Associations (LMAs) and Co-management Model, Meat and Livestock Assembly Model, and Livestock Market-Yard Management Model. Turkana County constituted the principal empirical case, supplemented by evidence from Marsabit, Isiolo, Samburu, Baringo and Tana River. Data were collected through 45 semi-structured key-informant interviews, 10 focus group discussions, documentary review and direct market observation, and analyzed using thematic, historical, within-case and cross-case approaches. Findings show that the four models represent complementary dimensions of livestock-market development. The Organized Livestock Marketing Model provides market architecture by c…

title: Capital Market Opening-up and High-Quality Innovation of Enterprises
abstract: At present, China’s innovation field is facing the structural dilemma of quantity priority and insufficient quality. In the critical window period when the economy turns to high-quality development, the improvement of enterprise innovation level has become an important issue. Based on the quasi-natural experimental scenario of capital market opening, this paper constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to test the effect of capital market opening on the quality of enterprise innovation. Both theoretical deduction and empirical test show that capital market opening helps to improve the quality of enterprise innovation, and this effect is more significant in state-owned enterprises and enterprises with overseas business income. From the perspective of mechanism, on the one hand, the opening of capital market promotes the improvement of innovation quality by improving corporate governance and alleviating financing bottlenecks ; on the other hand, due to the increase of stock liquidity, the quality of innovation is suppressed. Overall, the positive effect is dominant. This paper not only expands the theoretical analysis of the relationship between capital market opening and enterprise innovation, but also provides a useful reference for policy practice.

Heart rate response and clinical determinants of Glittre activities of daily living test performance in pediatrics with cystic fibrosis
abstract: Abstract The Pediatric Glittre Activities of Daily Living Test (TGlittre-P) is a field test designed to assess the functional performance of activities of daily living (ADL) in pediatric patients with cystic fibrosis (CF). However, the effects of TGlittre-P on heart rate response and the clinical determinants of test performance in this population remain insufficiently understood. To compare the heart rate response elicited by the TGlittre-P and the six-minute walk test (6MWT), and to identify pulmonary and extrapulmonary factors associated with TGlittre-P performance in pediatric patients with CF. Fifty-four pediatric patients with CF (mean age = 14.46 ± 2.16 years, 31 females and 23 males) were included in this cross-sectional study. ADL performance was assessed using the TGlittre-P, and functional capacity was assessed using the 6MWT. Pulmonary function, including forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁) and forced vital capacity (FVC), maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressure (MIP and MEP, respectively), handgrip strength (HGS %) and quadriceps muscle strength (QMS %) were measured. A multiple linear regression analysis model was used to determine independent predictors of TGlittre-P performance. The mean TGlittre-P duration was 2.00 ± 0.53 min. title: Response to Global Refugee Crisis: In Search of Best Practices for the States
abstract: The global refugee crisis has become a critical concern in international law. Despite the presence of an international refugee law regime, the refugee hosting countries have resorted to different approaches in responding to the issue. In most cases, responding countries take a defensive approach towards the refugees, and the international refugee law regime itself is not enough to ensure their protection due to its weak enforcement mechanism. However, there are some exceptions. Some countries have set benchmarks in responding to the refugee crises by going beyond their legal obligations. This paper has analyzed the international legal framework on refugee protection, explored the responses by Germany, Turkey, Uganda, and Columbia, and attempted to identify their good practices that can be role models for other refugee hosting states. While comparing the approaches of the four states, the study found that, inter alia, the economic condition of a refugee hosting country is not a barrier to ensuring the rights of the refugees, the conventional humanitarian approach is evolving into an integration strategy, and the willingness of the hosting state is more significant than its legal obligation. Based on the findings, the paper has made recommendations that can be guidelines for the refugee hosting states in responding to the refugee crisis.

title: Evaluation of the non-specific effects of a two-dose BCG vaccination scheme on immune response and milk production in dairy cows
abstract: Abstract Bovine tuberculosis (bTB) is a chronic disease primarily caused by Mycobacterium bovis , a zoonotic pathogen with worldwide distribution that causes economic losses in milk and meat production systems. In dairy cattle from central Chile, disease prevalence remains high, and the national control and eradication program has faced the reluctance of producers to implement the test-and-slaughter strategy due to the lack of compensation. Within this epidemiological context, vaccination with the M. bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) strain has proven to be a useful tool for disease prevention and control and has shown non-specific effects in humans and animals. The objective of this study was to assess non-specific immunological responses of peripheral blood monocytes and the impact on dairy production traits following vaccination with the BCG Russia strain administered in a two-dose scheme, in a commercial dairy farm with a free bTB status. A total of 198 12-month-old heifers were vaccinated via the subcutaneous route with the equivalent of 1 human dose of BCG. Ninety-six of them were revaccinated with a similar dose during first 30 d of their lactation period. In addition, 39 control animals were not vaccinated and received saline. Pro-inflammatory cytokine responses to ex-vivo homologous (PPD-B) and heterologous (LPS) stimulation was evaluated in peripheral CD14 + monocy…

Using Limestone to Assess the Impacts of Passivation and Ca-Silicate Formation on Lime Carbonation Efficiency for Looping Technology
abstract: Abstract Maximizing process efficiency in the lime looping process for direct air capture (DAC) is essential for reducing costs and energy demands to scale up this carbon dioxide (CO2) removal (CDR) technology. Here, we investigated two inefficiencies in the lime looping process: (i) surface passivation in relation to the particle size of the initial limestone powder and (ii) the presence of silicate impurities and their thermal reaction with CaCO3 during calcination. Passivation-limited carbonation to <68% completion for coarser (>25 μm) lime particles compared to ∼88% for finer (<25 μm) particles, emphasizing the need to pulverize limestone to very fine particle sizes to optimize efficiency. Limestones naturally contain unreactive impurities that will reduce CDR efficiency. For instance, the presence of 7.5 wt.% non-carbonates in the limestone used in this study reduced CO2 capture efficiency by an equal percentage. Additionally, formation of relatively inert Ca-silicates from the reaction of silicates (primarily quartz) with CaO during calcination (900 °C) further reduced efficiency by lowering CaO availability and potentially passivating reactive surfaces. The Effects of Recruitment, Selection, and Job Placement on Ship Crew Performance at PT Pelayaran Guntur Line
abstract: This study investigates the effects of recruitment, selection, and job placement on ship crew performance at PT Pelayaran Guntur Line. The research was prompted by increases in minor incidents, safety nonconformities, and suboptimal performance evaluations between 2023 and 2025. An associative quantitative design was applied to 100 active crew members selected through convenience sampling from a population of 133. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4. Recruitment had a significant positive effect on performance (β = 0.269; p = 0.009), whereas selection had no statistically significant effect (β = −0.230; p = 0.062). Job placement produced the strongest positive effect (β = 0.889; p < 0.001). The final model explained 79.6% of the variance in crew performance. These findings indicate that candidate information obtained during recruitment and selection should be integrated into competency-based placement decisions and systematic post-assignment evaluations

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Improving the Performance of Contemporary Political Systems: An Analytical Study in Governance and Decision-Making
abstract: Government digital transformation is an ever-expanding part of modern governance. Governments increasingly implement digital platforms, big-data analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, digital identity systems and integrated information infrastructures. These developments can affect the delivery of public services as well as institutional coordination, citizen–government interaction, policy formulation and decision-making. This paper explores how digital transformation affects the performance of contemporary political systems, particularly in governance and governmental decision-making. It examines the potential of digital technologies to enhance administrative efficiency, institutional responsiveness, transparency, accountability, citizen engagement and evidence-based policy-making, together with the problems of cybersecurity, privacy, digital exclusion, algorithmic bias, institutional capacity and over-reliance on technology. The study is qualitative and analytical: it reviews and synthesizes the academic literature and the reports of international organizations. Digital transformation is not simply the conversion of traditional administrative procedures into electronic processes; it is institutional change in its own right. Current studies suggest that it requires organizational transformation, sound data governance, interoperability, an adequate legal framework…

title: HIP OSTEOARTHRITIS IN PRIMARY HEALTH CARE: CONSERVATIVE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES, CURRENT EVIDENCE, AND CHALLENGES IN CHILE
abstract: Introduction: Hip osteoarthritis is a common degenerative disease that can cause pain, functional limitation, and deterioration in quality of life. Primary Health Care plays a fundamental role in its initial diagnosis, conservative treatment, and follow-up. Objective: To review the current evidence on the main conservative management strategies for hip osteoarthritis in Primary Health Care and to analyze the main challenges associated with their implementation in the Chilean context. Methodology: A narrative review of the literature was conducted through searches in PubMed/MEDLINE and SciELO, complemented by official documents from the Chilean Ministry of Health. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and relevant studies addressing diagnosis, therapeutic exercise, education, weight control, pharmacological treatment, injections, and the organization of primary care were prioritized. Results: The evidence supports a multimodal management approach based primarily on therapeutic exercise, self-management education, and modification of risk factors, including weight control when appropriate. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs may contribute to symptomatic control in selected patients, while intra-articular corticosteroid injections may provide short-term relief. In Chile, the integration of rehabilitation services into Primary Health Care represents a relevant strat…

abstract: The field of digital communication in politics is of interest for research, since the development of any social system is closely linked to competent political decision-making. The need for sustainable and high-quality information transfer must have an appropriate level of attention to its tools in order to ensure the effectiveness of all necessary processes. Digital means of communication are able to reach their potential precisely in this environment, since their prerogative is effective communication between subjects. It is necessary to understand how important it is for citizens to be able to quickly and easily communicate their public opinion, file a complaint or a proposal, and solve their widespread problems without making lengthy entries to the necessary government structure. And civil servants will find out about them faster and respond promptly. In recent years, there has been relatively intensive scientific work in the field of thesis defense on the topic of political and network communications. However, it should be recognized that most of them explore the Internet either from the point of view of sociology, psychology, journalism, or are related to other areas of political communication theory. abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis perlakuan PPN (PPN) pada transaksi retur penjualan berdasarkan Peraturan Menteri Keuangan (PMK) Nomor 81 Tahun 2024 di PT Kimia Farma Trading & Distribution Manado. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa proses retur penjualan didukung oleh prosedur administrasi dan dokumentasi yang melibatkan beberapa fungsi internal perusahaan. title: Overtourism governance and resident wellbeing. A social exchange framework for understanding community support under visitor management measures
abstract: Overtourism has moved destination scholarship from the description of visitor pressure to the design of measures that contain it. Caps, timed entry, tourist taxes, short-term rental controls, cruise berth limits and dispersal schemes are now common, yet the field still explains community reactions with a model built for a different question. Social exchange theory has long framed resident support as a judgement about the benefits and costs of tourism itself. This article argues that visitor management changes the object of that judgement. Once an authority intervenes, residents evaluate two linked exchanges, one with visitors and the tourism economy, and one with the body that governs it. The article develops a dual-exchange framework in which the governance relation has its own currencies, its own fairness criteria and its own temporal profile, and in which resident wellbeing is the medium through which both exchanges are experienced. Fourteen propositions specify how anticipated and experienced justice, institutional trust, dependence and the internal incidence of regulatory costs shape support for measures and for tourism. A typology classifies instruments by whose behaviour they restrict and where their costs fall inside the host community, and it is used to argue that effectiveness and diffuseness of cost may trade off against one another. AI-MEDIATED PLATFORM WORK: MEANINGFULNESS UNDER ALGORITHMIC MANAGEMENT
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates how platform work is matched, monitored, evaluated and performed. This conceptual paper develops a meaningfulness-based framework for AI-mediated platform work. Gig and platform work provide the bounded empirical setting because automated coordination, opaque evaluation, fluctuating demand, dependence on ratings and limited possibilities for contestation make the relevant tensions especially visible. The scientific problem is the under-specification of how co-occurring substitution and augmentation within a task bundle interact with platform-level control and governance to shape the significance workers attribute to a focal work episode. The purpose is to specify that relationship. The object isthe AI-mediated platform-work episode, operationalized through itstask bundle; the subject isthe relationship among task-level AI effects, platform-level control and governance, meaningfulness pathways and worker context. Drawing on theory synthesis and abductive model development, the article integrates research on gig work, algorithmic management, task-based labour economics and meaningful work. Contextual evidence from the OECD, the European Union and the World Bank establishes the scale and relevance of the setting but does not test the proposed relationships. Substitution and augmentation are treated as non-exclusive task-level effects, …

title: Design of an IoT-Based Waste Management System for Biogas Production as a Renewable Energy Source
abstract: The increasing volume of organic waste presents serious environmental challenges while the demand for renewable energy continues to rise. This study proposes the design and implementation of an Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart biodigester system for converting organic waste into biogas as a renewable energy source. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller with DHT22 temperature, MPX5700 pressure, and MQ-4 methane gas sensors for real-time monitoring of fermentation parameters. A K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) regression algorithm is embedded to predict methane pressure and enable automated system control. Experimental results indicate that the optimal model configuration at k = 4 achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.18 and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.21, demonstrating high predictive accuracy. The developed prototype improves methane production stability and enhances overall energy conversion efficiency. This research contributes to sustainable organic waste management and decentralized renewable energy systems.

title: Development and validation of objective performance metrics for robot-assisted basic surgical skills in a simulated anastomosis task using a single-port robotic system
abstract: Abstract Introduction The chicken anastomosis task is a widely adopted model for training robotic suturing and knot-tying. Aim of this study was to develop and validate objective performance metrics for this task on the Single-Port (SP) robotic platform and to establish a proficiency benchmark for training and assessment. Methods Seven experts in robotic surgery training and Proficiency Based Progression (PBP) developed the metrics for the SP chicken anastomosis task. The proposed metrics were refined among a panel of n = 14 participants with significant experience in PBP and/or robotics and/or the SP system, through a modified Delphi process. Construct validity was assessed by comparing recorded performances of n = 12 expert ( ≥100 SP RARPs) and n = 12 novice surgeons, blindly scored by two reviewers. abstract: The green transformation promoted by the European Union (EU) affects not only infrastructure, but also managerial work organization decisions. By 2050, the EU has set a goal to decarbonize the environment and use only clean technologies for energy production. Changing legal regulations encourage investment development, which affects the work of both business entities and other organizations. The need for management skills and the change of competencies is becoming one of the most serious challenges in implementing important infrastructure projects. When it comes to the municipal energy production sector, not only the need to evaluate investment decisions, but also aspects of ensuring security of supply are highlighted. The article presents an example of the transformation of the municipal heating sector at the municipal level in Lithuania, while emphasizing the need for management changes. The possibilities of replacing worn-out heat production infrastructure are assessed, considering the goals set by the EU. Both traditional investment payback methods and innovative approaches, such as Response Surface Methodology, were employed for this purpose. The research conducted in the article showed that investments in new-generation infrastructure are inseparable from a comprehensive assessment, taking into account the future prospects of the region. PROJECT INTEGRATION GOVERNANCE FOR MANAGING FRAGMENTATION IN HYBRID ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: Contemporary project environments increasingly combine specialized digital platforms, decentralized teams, hybrid project-management methods and multi-level governance arrangements. Although such heterogeneity can strengthen flexibility and local adaptation, it also increases the need for integration. Existing project-management research examines complexity, hybrid methodologies, information overload, knowledge transfer and governance, but these streams provide only a partial explanation of the cumulative coordination problem created when tools, information, methods, knowledge and decision rights are insufficiently connected. The purpose of this study is to conceptualize project management fragmentation (PMF) as a multidimensional integration problem and to propose a Project Integration Governance framework for limiting its dysfunctional effects while preserving useful flexibility. An exploratory qualitative expert survey was administered during April–May 2026. The analytical sample comprised 12 experienced projectmanagement professionals with 7–18 years of experience, predominantly from service-intensive sectors. Open-text responses were analyzed through deductive-inductive thematic coding and cross-case comparison. Five recurring dimensions of PMF were identified: tool and system fragmentation, data and information fragmentation, methodological fragmentation, knowledge fragme…

title: Social Commerce Risk Management for Business Sustainability: A Qualitative Study of Batik SMEs in Lampung, Indonesia
abstract: Batik SMEs in Lampung utilize social commerce to expand their markets and reach customers beyond the local region. However, the exposure of batik motifs and digital content creates risks to creative assets and brand identity. This study aims to identify the risks arising from social commerce use and analyze their management in supporting business sustainability. A qualitative approach was employed through in-depth interviews, digital observation, and documentation involving Batik SMEs that use social commerce for marketing and sales. Data were analyzed thematically to identify risk forms and management responses. The findings reveal three main risks: theft of batik motif ideas, imitation of batik motifs, and imitation of digital content. These risks challenge SMEs in maintaining product uniqueness and brand identity. Risk management strategies include continuous motif development, strengthening brand identity, using watermarks on digital content, monitoring digital activities, and developing new content concepts and designs. The findings indicate that social commerce risk management is not limited to preventing losses but also forms part of an adaptation and learning process to maintain competitiveness and support the sustainability of Batik SMEs.

abstract: At present, the invasive species red imported fire ants have become a major threat to local ecosystems and the daily lives of people in China. Long-term reliance on chemical control has led to the development of resistance in red imported fire ants, resulting in unsatisfactory control effectiveness. To address this issue, this paper, from a biomathematical perspective, for the first time introduces mathematical modeling into the population control of red imported fire ants. Numerical simulations are finally presented to demonstrate the validity and practical effectiveness of the proposed control strategies. title: Combating Cyberbullying and Child Online Exploitation in Nigeria: Legal Strategies and Enforcement Realities
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies and internet access has transformed communication, education, and social interaction globally. This digital revolution, however, has also exposed children to increasing risks of cyberbullying, online grooming, sextortion, child sexual abuse materials (CSAM), and other forms of technology-facilitated exploitation. In Nigeria, the growing number of young internet users, coupled with limited digital literacy and inadequate online safeguards, has heightened children's vulnerability to cyber-related harms. This paper examines the legal and institutional strategies adopted to combat cyberbullying and child online exploitation in Nigeria, with particular emphasis on enforcement realities. Using a doctrinal and comparative legal research methodology, the study analyzes relevant legal frameworks, including the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015, the Child Rights Act 2003, constitutional provisions, and data protection regulations. It further evaluates the roles of key enforcement institutions such as the Nigeria Police Force, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, the Nigerian Communications Commission, and other agencies. The paper identifies significant enforcement challenges, including inadequate technical capacity, weak inter-agency coordination, low reporting rates, societal stigmatization of victims, judicial lim…

title: When Consumers Cross Borders: The Extraterritorial Limits of Article 9's Perfection Rules
abstract: Consumer credit has become mobile in ways that Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code did not anticipate. Article 9’s choice-of-law rules for perfecting a security interest assume that a debtor has one stable, easily identifiable location, ordinarily the debtor’s principal residence, an assumption that dual-resident, remote-working, and expatriate consumers do not always satisfy. This article examines how UCC §§ 9-301, 9-307, and 9-316 apply to cross-border consumer-credit transactions, such as auto-secured installment credit, against the backdrop of a buy-now-pay-later market that is growing quickly and moving toward longer-term installment structures, and identifies a doctrinal gap: because individual cross-border consumer disputes are too small in dollar value to justify litigation, the choice-of-law problems created by consumer mobility have been absorbed quietly as a cost of doing business rather than resolved through case law or statutory reform. Drawing on recent Federal Reserve research on buy-now-pay-later growth, a bankruptcy decision applying the petition-date freeze rule to a lapsed Article 9 financing statement, and New York’s rollout of the 2022 UCC amendments, the article argues that this gap will not stay latent as cross-border consumer lending scales. It concludes with practical compliance recommendations for lenders and counsel: treating a debtor’s location …

title: SEO as a tool for managing the company's digital presence
abstract: This article explores the role of search engine optimization (SEO) as a strategic management tool for a company's digital presence. Using a comparative analysis of industry data, it examines the dynamics of the global SEO software market and the bipolar structure of the Russian search market: Yandex relies on behavioral factors, while Google prioritizes content quality and reputation. This divergence requires Russian companies to pursue two coordinated, yet distinct, optimization strategies. The ROI of digital channels is analyzed: SEO delivers the highest long-term returns, although the payback period ranges from nine to sixteen months. The impact of AI Overviews blocks is also examined: their proliferation has led to a significant drop in organic click-through rates and has brought GEO (Generative Response Evaluation) to the forefront: a strategy aimed at reaching cited sources of generative responses. The results are intended for digital marketing and corporate management professionals.

title: Price and Physical Evidence on Consumer Decisions Regarding Damri Executive Class Bus Services
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether price perceptions and physical evidence are associated with consumer decisions among users of DAMRI Executive Class bus services on the Pontianak-Sintang corridor. Research Method: A quantitative associative design used questionnaire data from 100 purposively selected users aged 17 years or older with direct experience of the service. Price, physical evidence, and consumer decisions were measured using five-point Likert scales and analyzed with instrument checks, descriptive statistics, multiple linear regression, partial tests, and a simultaneous model test. Results and Discussion: More favorable evaluations of price and physical evidence were each positively associated with consumer decisions, and the two predictors were jointly related to the outcome. Implications: The cross-sectional, single-corridor, purposive-sample design and two-predictor model limit generalization. The findings support managerial attention to fare-value alignment and consistent maintenance of cleanliness, comfort, vehicle condition, and supporting facilities. Originality: The study provides route-specific evidence on how monetary and tangible service attributes jointly relate to executive intercity bus choice.

abstract: Berlangganan saat ini merupakan salah satu bisnis ekonomi digital yang bergerak di berbagai sektor industri seperti layanan telekomunikasi. Perubahan ini mempengaruhi industri untuk memprediksi dan mencegah pelanggan berhenti berlangganan (churn), ini dipengaruhi oleh biaya untuk akuisisi pelanggan baru mencapai 5 hingga 25 kali lebih tinggi daripada retensi. Fitur yang di gunakan dalam model ini mencakup skor sentiment, kendala jaringan, permasalahan penagihan. Data latih sebanyak 11.388 entri di seimbangkan menggunakan SMOTE untuk memastikan representasi yang adil antara kelas pelanggan setia dan pelanggan yang churn. Pengujian dilakukan dengan menerapkan ambang batas probabilitas (threshold) sebesar 0,4 untuk meningkatkan sensitivitas deteksi. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa model mencapai akurasi sebesar 0.89, dengan tingkat Precision sebesar 0.98 dan Recall sebesar 0.90. Nilai ROC AUC sebesar 0.893 mengonfirmasi kemampuan model dalam membedakan karakteristik pelanggan secara efektif. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa kombinasi XGBoost dan SMOTE …

abstract: Law enforcement activity requires officers to maintain effective professional functioning in situations characterised by uncertainty, interpersonal conflict, emotional pressure, responsibility and potential threat. These conditions make emotional self- regulation and adaptive coping important psychological resources for maintaining professional stability. The purpose of this paper is to analyse the role of emotional regulation and coping strategies in the psychological adaptation of law enforcement officers. Particular attention is paid to the ability to recognise and regulate emotional reactions, select adaptive responses to stressful situations, maintain cognitive control under pressure and recover psychological resources after demanding professional experiences.

Gut dysbiosis, blood pressure regulation, and cardiometabolic risk in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)
abstract: Abstract Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a common endocrine-metabolic disorder associated with increased hypertension and cardiometabolic risk. Gut dysbiosis is also frequently reported in affected women, raising the question of whether microbiome-linked pathways contribute to blood pressure elevation or vascular risk in this syndrome. To evaluate and synthesize the available evidence linking gut dysbiosis, gut microbial function, and microbiome-related mechanisms to hypertension, blood pressure regulation, and cardiovascular risk in women with PMOS, we conducted a narrative review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and citation tracking. Search terms included PCOS, PMOS, gut microbiota, gut dysbiosis, hypertension, blood pressure, cardiovascular risk, microbial metabolites, bile acids, intestinal permeability, inflammation, renin-angiotensin signaling, renal sodium handling, and autonomic regulation. Human studies, animal models, interventional studies, and mechanistic investigations relevant to PMOS and hypertension were reviewed according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Eligible publications were preclinical studies, human studies, English language, adult females, and peer-reviewed original or review articles. Clarifying whether gut dysbiosis contributes …

title: The nursing workforce crisis in Bulgaria: Workforce imbalance , educational capacity, and urgent health policy reform
abstract: Bulgaria faces a structural nursing workforce crisis that threatens the accessibility, safety, and continuity of health and social care. This review analyzes the scale and age structure of the nursing shortage, the imbalance between nurses and physicians, the educational pipeline, and policy options for rapid and sustainable workforce recovery. A structured narrative review and secondary analysis of official data from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Bulgarian National Statistical Institute, Ministry of Health, Sofia Municipality, European Union legislation, professional organizations, and peer-reviewed workforce studies were conducted, using information available through 24 September 2026. In 2025, Bulgaria had 28,357 practicing nurses and 30,409 physicians under a main employment contract, corresponding to only 0.93 nurses per physician. More than 76% of nurses were aged 45 years or older and 18.4% were aged 65 years or older. OECD data show 4.4 nurses per 1,000 population in Bulgaria versus 9.1 on average across OECD countries, while the nursing graduate rate was 7.6 per 100,000 population versus 45.7 across the OECD. Increasing university admission alone cannot correct the shortage within the necessary time horizon. Bulgaria requires an integrated policy combining workforce forecasting, educational reform, student support, safe staffing, re…

abstract: Abstract The transition to a carbon–neutral electricity system depends on the widespread integration of distributed and inverter-based renewable resources. The U.S. Department of Energy and the North American Electric Reliability Corporation have identified these resources as increasing the grid's cybersecurity attack surface faster than current oversight can manage. Federal reviews have also found that guidance for assessing grid cybersecurity risk remains incomplete. In response, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission has introduced a mandatory internal network monitoring standard and, for the first time, a voluntary financial incentive for cybersecurity investment beyond compliance requirements. However, neither these measures nor the academic literature on security economics and infrastructure capital budgeting provides a clear method for allocating cybersecurity capital as distributed and renewable generation continues to expand. This paper develops a four-component investment appraisal framework that combines the compliance floor established by NERC's Critical Infrastructure Protection standards, the loss-based investment benchmark implied by the Gordon-Loeb model, the timing flexibility provided by real options analysis, and the rate-recovery incentive created by FERC Order No. 893. abstract: Abstract Colloidal activated carbon (CAC) barriers have been widely adopted for in situ groundwater remediation of legacy and emerging contaminants. The design and installation of CAC barriers require an understanding of CAC transport and deposition as a function of site geochemistry, particularly for coastal sites where spatial variations in salinities are high and CAC placement with or without in situ flocculation by CaCl2 may be complex. Our column study has explored this complexity over a wide range of salinities (0.1–0.7 M) and relevant CaCl2 concentrations (0.0125–0.23 M) by considering individual and combined effects of Na+ and Ca2+ at pH 3 and 7. For the first time, retention profiles (RPs) and SEM-EDX images of CAC retained on sand are presented alongside breakthrough curves (BTCs) to elucidate CAC transport and retention behaviors. The presence of Ca2+ increased CAC retention in sand, likely through cation bridging at pH 7 and electrostatic interactions at pH 3. For Na+, CAC retention increased significantly at pH 3 only, owing to Na+-driven double-layer compression. In Na+-Ca2+ systems, CAC retention decreased linearly with increasing Na+:Ca2+ ratio with an inflection point at 0.83, below which CAC retention was driven by Ca2+ interaction with pH and above it by Na+ interaction with pH. Research on the Impact of Green Finance on Regional Low-carbon Transformation: An Analysis of the Mediating Effect Based on Green Innovation
abstract: Under the background of "double carbon" goal, green finance is an important institutional arrangement to promote green and low-carbon economic transformation. Based on China's provincial panel data from 2006 to 2023, this paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index of green finance, and uses panel fixed effect model, mediating effect model and instrumental variable method to test the impact of green finance on regional carbon emission intensity. The results show that the development of green finance significantly reduces regional carbon emission intensity, and the conclusion is still valid after robustness test. Green finance reduces carbon emission intensity by increasing the output of green patents, and green innovation plays a complete intermediary role; Heterogeneity analysis shows that the promotion effect of green finance is more obvious in areas with low economic level and after the low-carbon policy node in 2015. This paper provides empirical evidence for improving the green finance policy system and promoting regional differentiated low-carbon development.
