title: Administrative Leadership's Strategic Planning for AI Integration in Public Secondary Schools: A Qualitative Study in Kuala Lumpur
abstract: The aim of this qualitative study is to examine how administrative leaders in public secondary schools in Kuala Lumpur approach strategic planning for artificial intelligence (AI) integration in education. Three consolidated research objectives guided thc inquiry: (1 ) to explore administrators' understanding and strategic planning of AI integration, (2) to identify challenges and barriers in AI integration planning, and (3) to examine stakeholder engagement and leadership support required for successful AI integration. Through semi-structured interviews with ten experienced school administrators, including principals, senior assistants, and heads of departments, and employing reflexive thematic analysis, the study revealed five major themes: infrastructural and resource considerations, pedagogical transformation and teacher preparedness, ethical and equity concerns, stakeholder engagement strategies, and adaptive leadership approaches. Findings indicate that while administrators recognize AI' s transformative potential, strategic planning remains fragrnented, resource-constrained, and lacking systematic frameworks. The study underscores the critical need for multilevel support systems to ensure equitable and effective AI adoption in Malaysian secondary education. title: Energy-Efficient Optimal Control of a Hexarotor UAV Based on High-Order Fully Actuated Gust Disturbance Rejection
abstract: To address the challenge of simultaneously satisfying attitude stability constraints and achieving multi-motor energy efficiency optimization for a hexarotor UAV under complex low-altitude gust disturbances, this paper proposes a coordinated control method that integrates high-order fully actuated disturbance rejection with energy-efficient allocation. First, a low-altitude composite wind field model incorporating random wind, gusts, and improved Dryden turbulence is established. On this basis, a mapping relationship from wind field parameters to attitude disturbance torque and motor load is constructed to characterize the load imbalance among the six motors induced by gust disturbances. Second, an extended state observer (ESO) is designed at the attitude layer to estimate and compensate for the equivalent disturbances in the angular-acceleration channels. At the actuator layer, a bank of six Z-type extended state observers (ZESOs) is constructed to estimate the lumped disturbance acting on each individual motor channel. Based on the compensated motor dynamics, a coordination protocol is further developed to ensure coordinated reference tracking of the six motors under nonuniform gust loads and actuator constraints. title: Rethinking Educational Participatory Action Research with Migrant and Racialized Youth in Border Contexts
abstract: Abstract Youth-led participatory action research (YPAR) has gained increasing relevance as an approach for promoting youth agency and addressing social inequalities in educational contexts. However, when implemented with migrant and racialized youth in border regions, participatory research faces specific ethical, political, and methodological challenges that may limit its transformative potential. This article offers a situated reflection on the possibilities and constraints of educational participatory action research developed with migrant and racialized young people in the Canary Islands, one of the main border territories of southern Europe. Drawing on 15 years of experience in participatory research, education, and community action, as well as practice-based insights from Emancipatory Communicative Action Laboratories involving migrant and racialized youth, the paper reflects on recurring tensions that arise in these processes. Five recurring challenges are discussed: functional interculturalism, academic extractivism, performative decoloniality, ethnocentric and adult-centred practices, and the effects of structural violence associated with border regimes. In response, the article proposes a critical anti-racist and dialogical framework grounded in reflexivity, recognition, shared knowledge production, and the creation of safe participatory spaces. abstract: Digitalization is increasingly recognized as a key driver of energy efficiency, renewable energy development, and the decarbonization of energy systems. Artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, big data analytics, smart grids, and digital twins contribute to more efficient energy generation, transmission, and consumption while enhancing resource management and reducing operational costs. Nevertheless, significant differences remain among the EU Member States regarding their levels of digitalization, energy efficiency, renewable energy deployment, and greenhouse gas emissions. Assessing these differences is essential for designing effective policies that support both the digital and green transitions. abstract: Abstract Background Identifying individuals with undiagnosed HIV remains a global challenge. Mobile health (mHealth) approaches that leverage social networks hold potential to increase HIV testing uptake but also raise ethical considerations. Methods We conducted a qualitative study in Moshi, Tanzania, to examine how a pilot test of an SMS-based confidential referral system for HIV testing (CONSORT) was experienced by individuals sending and receiving testing invitations. Focus group discussions were conducted prior to the pilot, while phone-based interviews were conducted both before and after pilot implementation. Data were analyzed thematically using the four ethical principles of mHealth delivery: transparency, agency, accountability, and equitable access. Results Interpretations of message origin and purpose varied, shaping levels of trust and engagement. While many participants viewed the messages as supportive reminders, a few expressed confusion or concern about why they were selected. Attitudes also varied regarding the sharing of phone numbers without prior consent, with some participants viewing this as acceptable and others raising privacy concerns. Perceptions of confidentiality, message timing, and message content influenced acceptability of the intervention. These perspectives informed modifications to the design of the CONSORT system. title: Computational systems immunology and multi-scale modeling for the design of a Multi-Epitope Vaccine (MEV) against emerging multidrug-resistant Klebsiella michiganensis
abstract: Abstract Klebsiella michiganensis , an emerging multidrug-resistant member of the Klebsiella oxytoca complex, has become an important opportunistic pathogen responsible for nosocomial infections, including bacteremia and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Owing to its rapidly evolving resistance to carbapenems, new preventive strategies are urgently needed. This study presents a computational systems immunology framework integrating subtractive proteomics, reverse vaccinology, and immunoinformatics to design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) against K. michiganensis strain ATCC 8724. From the complete proteome (5,483 proteins), four proteins associated with the bacterial envelope and LPS-related processes were prioritized as computational vaccine targets: the outer-membrane β-barrel proteins BamA and LptD, the periplasmic LPS transport component LptA, and the outer-membrane lipoprotein LolB. These were selected as non-homologous and antigenic candidates. Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes derived from these proteins were evaluated for antigenicity, toxicity, allergenicity, and global HLA population coverage. The selected epitopes were assembled using AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers with the Mycobacterium tuberculosis 50 S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant to construct a 386-amino-acid chimeric MEV. abstract: Abstract Automated harvesting is pivotal to smart agriculture, yet precisely localizing picking points in complex orchard environments remains a key challenge for robotic harvesting systems. To this end, this study proposes a collaborative perception framework integrating a lightweight pose estimation model termed RepViT-DSConv-ARC-PoseHead enhanced YOLO (RDA-YOLO) with Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2). RDA-YOLO is the lightweight component responsible for real-time fruit detection and keypoint localization, while SAM2 is adopted for fruit contour segmentation and occlusion assessment. Based on the YOLOv11n-POSE architecture, we introduce Distribution Shift Convolution (DSConv) to reduce computational overhead and design the C3k2_RepViT module to enhance multi-scale feature fusion. Crucially, a specialized Adaptive Regression Coordination Pose Head (ARC-PoseHead) is developed to replace traditional prediction structures, employing log-scale polar regression and subpixel refinement to significantly improve coordinate perception of jujubes and key points under complex backgrounds. RDA-YOLO performs real-time detection and locates key points such as the pedicel-fruit transition zone to calculate optimal harvesting angles, while SAM2 performs fine-grained contour segmentation based on detection boxes to determine occlusion status and establish harvesting priority. From Participation to Exposure: NFTs and the Socio-Environmental Tensions of Digital Innovation
abstract: Digital innovation is typically discussed in terms of inclusion, efficiency, and value creation. Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) reveal a less visible dimension of digital innovation: their benefits can accrue to a relatively small number of actors, while their environmental and social costs extend beyond those who participate in, or benefit from, the technology. Using NFTs as a revealing case, we examine the tension between digital value creation and socio-environmental cost externalisation. Drawing on the Anthropocene and, in particular, the Capitalocene as a productive interpretive lens, we examine how digital artifacts, often perceived as intangible, are embedded in economic, infrastructural, and institutional arrangements through which benefits, responsibilities, and socio-environmental consequences are unevenly distributed. We argue that this tension adds an important dimension to digital inequality because participation and exposure need not coincide. We therefore call on Information Systems scholars to examine not only who accesses, participates in, and captures value from digital innovation, but also who bears responsibility and who is exposed to its (unintended) consequences. We outline avenues for doing so through multidimensional approaches to digital inequality, climate justice, socio-environmental externalities, and critical futures thinking.

title: Historical roots of commodity markets: from mercantilism to the theory of storage
abstract: Commodity markets today are shaped by financialization, price volatility, and the demands of the energy transition. This paper traces the historical development of commodity market theory from the seventeenth to the mid-twentieth century, identifying two parallel trajectories. The first examines the evolving conception of commodities—from precious metals as instruments of state power, through land as a gift of nature, to standardized outputs of finite natural resources traded as financial assets. The second traces the transformation of income from mere ownership—from classical land rent, through scarcity rent, to convenience yield. By integrating traditions often studied separately—mercantilist bullionism, physiocratic natural philosophy, classical rent theory, neoclassical marginalism, conservation economics, Keynesian forward-market analysis, and the theory of storage—the study reveals both conceptual continuities and methodological shifts. In doing so, it traces the historical roots of contemporary approaches to commodity pricing, risk transfer, and sustainable resource use.

abstract: Retail central bank digital currency (CBDC) is frequently justified as a tool for financial inclusion, yet the three retail CBDCs in live operation have struggled to attract sustained use, and the people they were meant to reach remain largely absent from the adoption literature. Existing studies of CBDC acceptance draw on samples of banked, digitally connected consumers and apply technology acceptance models whose assumptions those samples satisfy. This paper argues that the unbanked violate several of those assumptions and that three constructs at the centre of adoption theory, trust, privacy, and habit, operate differently for them. Drawing on research in information systems, monetary economics, consumer payments, and development finance, the paper develops a conceptual framework in which trust is layered across the state, intermediaries, and the technology, privacy concern is directed primarily at the state rather than at commercial actors, and cash habit acts both as a barrier to first use and as the mechanism through which sustained use must eventually be secured. Ten propositions specify how these constructs and their interactions shape adoption intention, initial use, and habituated use, and how CBDC design choices such as tiered identification, offline capability, agent networks, and government to person payments moderate the relationships. title: Physics-Informed Multimodal Sensing and Machine Learning Framework with Real-Time Digital Twin for Intelligent Structural Health Monitoring of Marine Wharves
abstract: Marine wharves, consisting of concrete or steel decks supported by pile foundations, operate in harsh marine environments involving waves, vessel impacts, and corrosive seawater. Even minor cracks or early-stage corrosion in piles can lead to sudden structural failure. Early detection is therefore essential. Traditional vibration-based structural health monitoring (SHM) methods often struggle to deliver reliable results in real operational settings because environmental and operational variations can mask damage-induced frequency changes. This study presents a multimodal SHM framework that integrates accelerometers, strain gauges, high-resolution cameras, acoustic transducers, and corrosion sensors with edge computing, advanced machine learning, and a real-time physics-informed digital twin. Edge nodes preprocess sensor data to extract modal frequencies, crack indicators, and acoustic features, reducing communication loads by over 90% while preserving diagnostic fidelity. A hybrid pipeline combined attention-based multimodal fusion, XGBoost screening, and a feedforward deep neural network trained using a composite physics-informed objective. title: Implementasi Face Recognition Berbasis Support Vector Machine dan MediaPipe
abstract: Autentikasi berbasis biometrik dengan wajah menawarkan kemudahan dan keamanan, namun akurasinya masih dipengaruhi dengan adanya perubahan pencahayaan, pose, ekspresi, dan occlusion. Penelitian ini mengimplementasikan sistem face recognition yang ringan dan praktis dengan deteksi wajah menggunakan MediaPipe Face Mesh, ekstraksi fitur melalui face encoding (dengan dukungan pola tepi ala HOG), dan klasifikasi identitas memakai Support Vector Machine (SVM) dengan tiga varian kernel yang dibandingkan secara sistematis. Sistem dikembangkan dalam Python (MediaPipe, OpenCV, scikit-learn) dengan antarmuka web untuk pendaftaran dan identifikasi wajah. Data uji berupa citra wajah pengguna yang diubah menjadi vektor embedding, kemudian pelatihan/validasi dilakukan memakai 5-fold cross-validation dan perbandingan beberapa kernel SVM. Hasil menunjukkan sistem mampu mengenali wajah dengan baik pada kondisi pencahayaan normal dan pose frontal. Kernel Linear memberikan akurasi rata-rata tertinggi 99,38% (confusion matrix 100%), disusul RBF 98,72% dan Polynomial 96,11%. Mekanisme stabilisasi confidence antar frame membuat tampilan identifikasi lebih halus dan konsisten. Meski demikian, ukuran data yang terbatas membuat performa belum sepenuhnya merepresentasikan kondisi nyata dan masih rentan terhadap occlusion serta pencahayaan ekstrim (indikasi overfitting). title: INOVAÇÕES PEDAGÓGICAS EM AMBIENTES DE E-LEARNING: O IMPACTO DAS METODOLOGIAS ATIVAS NA EDUCAÇÃO CONTEMPORÂNEA
abstract: Este estudo tem o objetivo de identificar e avaliar as estratégias implementadas por esses gestores para fomentar uma abordagem pedagógica que seja tanto inovadora quanto interativa, buscando resultados que contribuam para uma educação mais engajadora e alinhada com as necessidades educacionais contemporâneas. A pesquisa centra-se no papel dos gestores educacionais na implementação de plataformas de e-learning, destacando como podem tanto reforçar práticas tradicionais quanto facilitar abordagens pedagógicas inovadoras. Este artigo foi desenvolvido com base em uma metodologia bibliográfica, selecionando referências teóricas pertinentes abordadas na disciplina e ajustadas às discussões relativas ao contexto atual relevantes que discutem as interseções entre gestão educacional e TICs, focando em como os gestores podem utilizar essas ferramentas para promover um ensino mais interativo e participativo. A análise revela que uma liderança eficaz e a formação contínua dos docentes são essenciais para aproveitar o potencial das tecnologias de e-learning, necessárias para criar ambientes de aprendizado inclusivos e eficazes. Conclui-se que os diretores são fundamentais na atualização das práticas educacionais, ressaltando a necessidade de uma utilização crítica e inovadora das Tecnologias de Informação e Comunicação para aprimorar a qualidade e a acessibilidade da educação.

Development Of Cyber Office Administrator for Digital Administration Competence Learning
abstract: This study aimed to develop the Cyber Office Administrator Application based on Digital Administration competencies to support learning for Digital Office Administration students. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model, consisting of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. The participants were 35 students enrolled in a Digital Records Management course. Data were collected through needs analysis, expert validation, student responses, and pre-test and post-test assessments. The application obtained an expert feasibility score of 87%, categorized as highly feasible, while student responses reached 86%, indicating high practicality. Students’ mean scores increased from 83.03 in the pre-test to 87.09 in the post-test. Although the paired-test result showed a significant difference, the N-Gain value of 0.24 was categorized as low. The findings indicate that the application is feasible and practical as a competency-based digital learning environment, while further experimental testing is needed to establish its learning effectiveness

title: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning applied to liver MRI for hepatocellular carcinoma detection: a systematic review and HSROC meta-analysis of patient-level evidence
abstract: Abstract Background Liver MRI is central to non-invasive hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) diagnosis. Deep learning (DL) is increasingly studied for detection and interpretation, but the maturity, transportability, and patient-level diagnostic evidence for these systems remain uncertain. Main body We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science from 2010 through July 2025 (the exact original execution day was not retained) and updated the same strategies through 20 July 2026. Eligible studies evaluated stand-alone DL or radiologist-interpreted DL-assist MRI and provided reconstructable patient-level 2 × 2 data. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed QUADAS-2 and AI-reporting items. Four retrospective Chinese tertiary-centre cohorts ( N = 698; three stand-alone systems and one radiologist-interpreted DL-assist system) were included; the update identified no additional eligible study. Model-derived exploratory pooled estimates were sensitivity 0.862 (95% CI 0.819–0.896) and specificity 0.916 (0.881–0.941); MCMC median LR + was 10.19 (95% interval 7.22–14.55), LR- was 0.151 (0.114–0.199), and diagnostic odds ratio was 67.59 (41.10–111.10). Between-study variance estimates lay at the boundary and the confidence and prediction regions were nearly identical; with four studies, this does not establish statistical or clinical homogeneity. Unsupervised machine learning for automated crystal orientation mapping on noisy 4D-STEM data
abstract: Abstract Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is a high-throughput measurement used to comprehensively acquire diffraction patterns across a region of interest in a specimen. While the measurement is useful for identifying crystallographic microstructures, the data analysis requires significant effort owing to the complexity and high dimensionality of the data. Furthermore, the analysis of low signal-to-noise data from beam-sensitive materials such as polymers is particularly challenging. This study proposes an automatic analysis pipeline that leverages denoising and unsupervised crystallographic analysis for 4D-STEM data. The denoising method is based on a self-supervised approach that eliminates the need for clean training images. The developed method is extended to 4D-STEM data by utilizing diffraction patterns observed at neighboring probe positions. The subsequent unsupervised analysis is designed to be invariant to the crystal in-plane rotations, enabling the effective identification of crystal components. The efficacy of the proposed pipeline is evaluated using both synthetic and experimental 4D-STEM data. Quantitative evaluation for synthetic data across various noise levels demonstrates the robustness of our approach. title: Learning curves in robotic and laparoscopic colorectal surgery: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate and compare learning-curve assessment in laparoscopic and robotic colorectal surgery and to develop a standardized framework for future learning-curve reporting. Background Learning curves in minimally invasive colorectal surgery are widely reported, but inconsistent definitions limit interpretability and comparability. This systematic review analyzed learning-curve assessment in laparoscopic and robotic colorectal surgery and proposes a standardized framework. Methods MEDLINE, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were systematically searched according to PRISMA guidelines (registered in PROSPERO, CRD42026128860). Included were randomized, prospective, and retrospective studies on learning curves in colorectal surgery. Primary outcome was the number of procedures required to reach the initial learning phase. Secondary outcomes included definitions of learning curves, analytical methods, and classification of learning phases. Analyses were stratified by procedure type (colon vs. rectal resections), and pooled breakpoint regression was used to identify learning phases. Results A total of 114 studies comprising 167 learning-curve analyses were included. CUSUM or risk-adjusted CUSUM was used in 66.4% of analyses, whereas 33.3% applied arbitrary definitions; operative time was the most frequently used endpoint (79.6%). abstract: Abstract Background Digital tools and simulation-based learning are playing an increasingly important role in medical education. Earlier studies have shown that video and virtual reality can be just as effective for teaching clinical skills as presentation-based teaching methods. This exploratory study compared two standardized self-directed instructional formats, video-based and presentation-based instruction, for teaching basic neuroangiographic skills. In addition to comparing objective and subjective learning outcomes between instructional formats, the study explored whether prior angiography experience influenced performance and moderated the effect of the teaching method. Methods Twenty participants with different levels of prior angiography experience were randomly assigned to either a video-based group (VG; n = 9) or a presentation-based group (PG; n = 11). The VG watched expert-narrated recordings of a physician performing neuroangiography on a silicone flow model. The PG independently worked through static simplified slides derived from the same instructional material, including schematic illustrations and brief written annotations. Afterwards, all participants performed neuroangiography on the silicone flow model using three different catheter types (Vertebralis, Simmons 2, Headhunter). title: Legal Education in Bangladesh: Assessing the Gap Between Pre-Tertiary and Tertiary Learning
abstract: Education is the pillar of individual and social development, as it equips individuals with the knowledge and skills necessary to create a sustainable future. In addition, legal education empowers people with knowledge regarding their rights and duties and how the justice system works. The Latin maxim, ‘Ignorantia juris non excusat’ meaning ignorance of the law is not an excuse, also emphasizes the importance of legal awareness. However, in Bangladesh, legal education is confined only to tertiary levels, with limited opportunities for students to acquire basic legal knowledge during pre-tertiary education. This study examines the gap between pre-tertiary and tertiary legal education in Bangladesh using a mixed-method approach that combines survey data with documentary and comparative analysis. Data were collected from 100 LLB students and 12 law faculty members across four universities in Bangladesh. The survey data were analyzed descriptively to examine respondents’ exposure to pre-tertiary legal education and their perceptions of its relevance to LLB studies, while documentary and comparative analysis was used to examine selected approaches to pre-tertiary legal education in other jurisdictions. Intellectual Intelligence, Empowering School Environment and Economics Learning Outcomes among High School Students
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of intellectual intelligence and an empowering school environment on students’ economics learning outcomes at the senior high school level. This research employed a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. Data were collected using questionnaires and documentation of students’ learning outcomes. The findings revealed that intellectual intelligence significantly influenced students’ economics learning outcomes. In addition, the empowering school environment also had a significant positive effect on learning outcomes. Simultaneously, intellectual intelligence and the empowering school environment contributed significantly to students’ economics learning outcomes. The findings indicate that intellectual intelligence and empowering school environment significantly influence students’ economics learning outcomes. It can be concluded that improving students’ cognitive abilities and creating an empowering school environment are essential for enhancing academic achievement in economics. These findings imply that economics teachers and school administrators should implement student-centered learning strategies and foster supportive learning environments to promote meaningful learning and improve students’ learning outcomes. title: ASDAE-OPF: an adaptive data reduction and optimization model for efficient data handling and routing in wireless sensor networks
abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks face severe energy limitations, with data transmission consuming the majority of a node’s power. To address this, the proposed framework combines three energy aware mechanisms. First, an Adaptive Sparse Denoising Autoencoder compresses and reconstructs sensor data, transmitting clean and essential information rather than raw redundant readings. Second, cluster head selection is handled through Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering integrated with the Firefly Algorithm. It’s enabling energy-balanced and adaptive cluster formation. Third, a Cross-layer Opportunistic Routing Protocol, built on Grey Wolf Optimization and Particle Swarm Optimization, selects efficient forwarding paths that reduce latency while preserving network connectivity. Together, these components reduce transmission overhead, balance energy usage across nodes, and extend overall network lifetime. Simulation results confirm improved energy efficiency and prolonged operational life compared to existing WSN schemes. This hybrid technique combines the three methods, and therefore, it would provide faster convergence, better CH selection and link stability by combining the parameters like distance, residual energy, trust, and link quality. The proposed system shows that the QOS can be improved considerably for different network sizes from 100 nodes to 500 nodes. The nodes framework…

abstract: Abstract Background Robotic-assisted technologies and evolving implant designs have been introduced in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) to improve the accuracy and reproducibility of component positioning. However, the relative contribution of robotic assistance compared with conventional instrumentation to radiographic outcomes in experienced, high-volume centers remains unclear. Methods This retrospective comparative study included 96 consecutive medial UKAs performed at a single high-volume institution. Patients were stratified into three groups: Journey I UKA implanted with NAVIO imageless robotic assistance ( n = 38), Journey II Uni UKA implanted using conventional instrumentation ( n = 27), and Journey II UK UKA implanted with CORI imageless robotic assistance ( n = 31). Standardized standing long-leg weight-bearing radiographs were obtained preoperatively and postoperatively. Radiographic evaluation included hip–knee–ankle (HKA) angle, femoral component coronal angle (FCCA), tibial component coronal angle (TCCA), and sagittal alignment parameters. Tibial coronal alignment was interpreted according to the Cartier metaphyseal alignment philosophy. Intergroup comparisons were performed using appropriate statistical tests. Establishment and multi-resolution transcriptomic landscape profiling of diverse equine intestinal organoid models
abstract: Abstract Background Equine intestinal organoid (EIO) models can recapitulate the in vivo structure and function of the small intestinal epithelium, making them ideal tools for studying the equine intestine. However, the specific marker genes of equine intestinal epithelial cells remain incompletely understood. These issues pose challenges to assessing the differentiation status and functional integrity of the EIO model in practical applications. Results In the present study, four types of equine intestinal in vitro models were successfully constructed, including conventional undifferentiated 3D EIOs, differentiated 3D EIOs, submerged 2D EIO monolayers, and air-liquid interface (ALI) monolayer models. All models were established using jejunal crypts isolated from three healthy 3-year-old male Yili horses. A total of 54,495 high-quality nuclei obtained from conventional and differentiated 3D EIOs were profiled via single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Five major intestinal epithelial cell subtypes were identified, including enterocytes, proliferative crypt cells, SOX9 + crypt cells, goblet cells, and proliferative transit-amplifying (TA)-like cells, with unique equine-specific cell marker expression patterns. title: Innovative approaches to developing talent and organizational culture in the context of digital transformation of russian universities
abstract: This article examines modern approaches to talent development and organizational culture formation in Russian universities against the backdrop of the digital transformation of higher education. It explores mechanisms for integrating digital tools to identify, attract, and retain talented faculty and researchers, as well as methods for fostering an adaptive corporate culture that fosters innovation. A review of theoretical talent management models is provided, along with practical cases of implementing digital platforms, HR analytics tools, and corporate training programs. Based on this analysis, recommendations are proposed for creating integrated systems for personnel development and cultural transformation, necessary to enhance the competitiveness of universities in the digital economy.

Embedded finance, buy now pay later, and consumer financial wellbeing. Toward an integrative conceptual framework
abstract: Buy now pay later has become a mainstream form of consumer credit, but research on it is divided across three communities that seldom meet. Finance and economics scholars measure downstream indicators of household distress. Information systems scholars study embedded finance as a question of platform architecture. Consumer researchers treat it as a payment mechanism that alters how a cost is evaluated. Each explains part of the phenomenon and none connects them. This paper develops an integrative conceptual framework linking the architecture of embedded credit to the decision environment it produces, and that environment to consumer financial wellbeing. Using theory synthesis, we argue that relocating credit into a merchant's checkout determines four properties of the consumer's decision environment, namely deferral, partitioning, frictionlessness and opacity, which would be weaker in a product with identical contractual terms sold separately. We treat these as affordances, which are enabling rather than determining, and specify the conditions under which each is actualised toward liquidity smoothing or toward obligation accumulation. The framework accommodates a counterweight that critical accounts omit, since providers bear credit risk and impose limits that brake accumulation on their own book but not across providers. We derive 12 propositions and a research agenda. We do n…

title: The impact of international economic relations on the global market for resources, goods and services under contemporary conditions
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive study of how international economic relations affect structural, price, spatial, and institutional transformations in global markets for resources, goods, and services. The research is relevant because of the simultaneous strengthening of economic interdependence, geoeconomic fragmentation, tariff and non-tariff restrictions, digitalization, competition for critical resources, and global value chain vulnerability. The article aims to systematize the channels through which international trade, capital movements, transnational corporations, monetary and financial relations, international migration, technology exchange, and global regulation influence markets for resources, merchandise, and services. The study applies systemic, structural-functional, comparative, and dynamic analysis, generalization, grouping, and logical modeling. The empirical base draws on materials from the WTO, UNCTAD, the IMF, the World Bank, the IEA, and the OECD. International economic relations affect global markets through trade-regulatory, investment-production, monetary-financial, logistics, technological-digital, labor, environmental, and geopolitical channels. In 2025, global trade in goods and commercial services reached about USD 34.9 trillion, while services rose to 27.5 percent. title: Entrepreneurship Development Programmes and Market Expansion of Small and Medium Enterprises in Kebbi State: A Cross-sectional Survey
abstract: This study examined the association between entrepreneurship development programmes and the market expansion of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Kebbi State, Nigeria. A quantitative cross-sectional descriptive survey design was adopted. From a population of 1,280 registered SMEs, a target sample size of 305 was determined using the Taro Yamane formula, while the reported analyses were based on 269 observations obtained from SME owners and managers who had participated in entrepreneurship development programmes. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression at the 5% significance level. The regression model explained 75.6% of the variation in market expansion (R² = 0.756) and was statistically significant, F (4, 264) = 204.855, p < 0.001. Technology Adoption (B = 0.331, p < 0.001), Awareness and Motivation (B = 0.311, p < 0.001), and Skills Development (B = 0.231, p < 0.001) showed statistically significant positive associations with market expansion. Access to Finance was not statistically significant in the fitted model (B = 0.040, p = 0.365). The findings indicate that programme-related skills, entrepreneurial awareness and motivation, and technology adoption are positively associated with SME market expansion in the study sample. title: Beyond Market Access: A Stakeholder Perspective on Marketing Challenges and Opportunities for Rural Agropreneurs in Sabah, Malaysia
abstract: Rural agropreneurship plays an important role in promoting food security, rural livelihoods, and sustainable economic development. However, rural agropreneurs in Sabah continue to face various marketing-related challenges that constrain business growth and competitiveness. This study explores these challenges and opportunities from the perspectives of key stakeholders involved in rural agropreneur development. A qualitative approach was employed using Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) involving 16 stakeholders representing government agencies, financial institutions, agricultural associations, business incubators, and private organisations. The data were analysed using thematic analysis. The findings identified four key themes influencing rural agropreneur marketing performance: market access, financial accessibility, institutional support, and policy implementation. Limited market access, dependence on intermediaries, inadequate financial documentation, land tenure issues, and bureaucratic financing procedures were identified as the main barriers to business development. Although institutional support and government policies are available, existing programmes remain largely production-oriented, with less emphasis on marketing capabilities, commercialisation, and digital marketing. Structural changes in the labor market under digital transformation
abstract: The article examines the digital transformation of the Ukrainian labor market. It clarifies the concept by defining it as a systemic process of qualitative changes in the structure, functioning mechanisms, and interactions among labor market actors, driven by the adoption and diffusion of digital technologies. The study analyses how digital changes have been reflected in Ukraine’s strategic and regulatory documents. The study identifies a gradual broadening of the government’s approach to these issues, ranging from considering individual components of digital development to incorporating them comprehensively into national employment policy. This chapter synthesizes contemporary scholarly approaches to transformations in employment, work organization, occupational structure, regulatory mechanisms, and workforce requirements. The paper justifies systematizing digital changes in the labor market into six interrelated dimensions. The paper specifies the content of each dimension and shows that considering them together provides a comprehensive framework for characterizing government priorities for labor market development, regulatory mechanisms, the digital infrastructure that supports them, transformations in employment forms and occupational structure, and changing competency requirements for workers. The proposed systematization complements existing scholarly approaches to study…

title: AI-enabled marketing analytics for SMEs: multimethod evidence on application potential and adoption conditions
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing analytics by enabling advanced data processing, predictions, and decision support. However, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often face substantial barriers to AI adoption due to limited organizational, technological, and human resources. To bridge theoretical and practical perspectives, this study employs a hybrid approach combining a systematic literature review of 49 studies with an empirical survey of more than 100 SMEs. The findings identify organizational, technological, and user-related conditions, as well as AI application potential, that shape AI adoption in SMEs. Based on these insights, a conceptual framework is proposed that differentiates between opportunistic, operational, strategic readiness, and strategic AI use. The framework translates SMEs’ AI application potential and adoption conditions into practice, thus structuring AI-enabled marketing analytics, which provides SMEs with new opportunities for data-driven operations despite resource constraints.

title: DIGITAL SKILLS AND CAREER ADAPTABILITY AMONG YOUTH IN KAZAKHSTAN: THE TRANSITION FROM HIGHER EDUCATION TO A TRANSFORMING LABOUR MARKET
abstract: The transition from higher education to employment is becoming increasingly difficult, as digitalization shifts job requirements and places greater emphasis on people’s ability to adapt, learn, and manage their own careers. This study examines the relationship between digital competence, career adaptability, practical experience and the degree with which young people in Kazakhstan feel ready to enter the labor market. The study was conducted from January to April 2026. The sample used for analysis consisted of 1,015 university and college students, as well as recent graduates at various stages of transition from education to work. Career adaptability was assessed using six indicators related to career planning, job flexibility, adapting to changes in the labor market, confidence in acquiring new skills, developing a career development strategy in the context of digital transformation, and an emphasis on the skills being transmitted; this measure showed a satisfactory internal sequence (α Kronbach = 0.860). Digital competence was found to be significantly related to perceived readiness for work, although this link was weak and non-linear, χ2(12) = 77.69, p <0.001, V Kramer = 0.160. Both internship experience and current employment status were also significantly related to willingness, but the scale of the effect was small. Effect of Cooperative Market Networking Policies on Small-Scale Potato Farmers' Livelihood Outcomes in Selected Counties in Kenya
abstract: This study sought to determine the effect of agricultural cooperatives’ market networking policies on small-scale potato farmers’ livelihood outcomes in selected counties in Kenya. The selected counties included Meru, Uasin Gishu, Elgeyo Markwet, Nandi, Bungoma, and Nyandarua that have well-established potato cooperatives. A cross-sectional survey research design was used. The target population was 3053 small-scale potato farmers. Slovin’s formula was used, and the sample size of the research was 350 small-scale farmers. Stratified sampling was used to take into account the representation of farmers from the different counties identified for the study. The data collection method involved the use of questionnaires administered to the farmers. A pilot study was conducted to determine the validity and reliability of the instrument. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, summarized and presented using percentages, means, and standard deviations. Assessment of the relationship between agricultural cooperative policies and livelihood outcome was undertaken using correlation and regression models. The correlation coefficient (r =0.617) and regression result (R squared=0.380). The findings indicated that market networking policies had a positive effect on the livelihood outcome of the small-scale potato farmers in the selected counties.

title: New insights into the epidemiology of frogeye leaf spot of soybean ( Glycine max L.)
abstract: Frogeye leaf spot (FLS), caused by Cercospora sojina, is an important foliar disease of soybean in the United States, yet quantitative information describing FLS epidemic dynamics during soybean reproductive stages remains limited. This study characterized the temporal FLS progress under natural field conditions and evaluated disease risk using survival analysis. Field observations were conducted in university-managed soybean fields in northwestern Missouri during the 2017, 2019 and 2024 growing seasons, without artificial inoculation or fungicide application. Disease severity was quantified as lesion counts on tagged upper-canopy leaflets repeatedly photographed and analyzed over time. Disease progress was modeled using exponential, monomolecular, logistic, and Gompertz nonlinear growth models. Logistic and Gompertz models consistently provided the best fit. Apparent infection rates estimated from logistic models ranged from 0.10 to 0.19 across epidemics, and lesion accumulation showed evidence of density-dependent dynamics with progressive deceleration. Survival analysis estimated the time required for leaflets to reach a threshold of 40 lesions, corresponding to approximately 4 to 6% leaf area affected. title: SUSTAINING RURAL ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION THROUGH THE MERAH PUTIH VILLAGE/SUBDISTRICT COOPERATIVE: AN ANALYSIS OF COMPETITIVE PRESSURES ON INCLUSIVE BUSINESS MODEL IN A HYBRID MARKET
abstract: This article analyzes the Merah Putih Village/Subdistrict Cooperative (KDKMP) as an instrument for sustaining rural economic transformation in Indonesia. The program is developed through an inclusive business model structured around seven integrated business units to strengthen institutional capacity and expand rural economic activities. The analysis employs Porter’s Five Forces framework to identify the competitive pressures faced by the cooperative within a hybrid market structure-namely, the interaction between market mechanisms and government policy intervention. The findings indicate that although the national target for establishing KDKMP has been surpassed, significant operational gaps remain at the regional level, including in Central Java Province. Variations in business management capacity, limited human resources, and strong dependence on policy support have resulted in uneven operational performance among cooperatives. In addition, KDKMP faces considerable competitive pressure from local retail businesses, microfinance institutions, and consumer goods distribution networks that have already established a strong presence in rural markets. These findings underscore that the sustainability of KDKMP is determined not only by institutional expansion, but also by the cooperatives’ ability to build operational efficiency, managerial adaptability, and business competitivene…

Targeted market survey of undeclared sildenafil in high-risk sexual enhancement supplements marketed in Hungary
abstract: Abstract Undeclared phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitors in dietary supplements marketed as natural sexual enhancers remain a consumer protection and food safety concern. This article investigates the occurrence of undeclared sildenafil in 12 high-risk sexual enhancement supplements marketed in Hungary as part of a targeted market survey. Sildenafil was screened using an in-house HPLC–UV/DAD method. Seven of the 12 products showed signals consistent with sildenafil, with contents ranging from 0.22 to 122 mg per unit. Two products contained amounts exceeding the maximum recommended dose of 100 mg, while 3 additional products contained amounts approximately equivalent to the 50 mg reference dose. These findings demonstrate that undeclared pharmaceutical adulteration remains present in selected high-risk sexual enhancement supplements available on the Hungarian market. Continued risk-based post-market control and regulatory monitoring are warranted to reduce consumer exposure to undeclared pharmacologically active substances.

title: Behaviour of Market Arrivals and Prices of Garlic in Gujarat, India
abstract: Garlic (Allium sativum L.) is an important commercial spice-cum-bulb crop in Gujarat, where price instability can affect farmers and market participants because production and market supply are seasonal. This study examined the seasonal, cyclical, and irregular behaviour of garlic market arrivals and wholesale prices in Rajkot, Jamnagar, and Gondal APMC markets using monthly secondary data for 2011–2025. A multiplicative time-series decomposition model was applied, and seasonal indices were estimated using the ratio-to-moving-average method. Garlic prices were below the annual average from February to April in all three markets, with the lowest seasonal price index in March and the highest in November. Arrival indices were generally elevated during parts of January–April and October–December and were lowest during July–August. Intra-year price variation was greatest in Gondal, where the intra-year price rise reached 99.83%, compared with 62.72% in Rajkot and 54.91% in Jamnagar. Annual price indices showed marked inter-annual variation, with the highest values in 2024: 3.56 in Rajkot, 2.77 in Jamnagar, and 3.53 in Gondal relative to the respective study-period means. Irregular components also varied across years and markets. Overall, the results demonstrate pronounced seasonal and inter-annual variation in garlic marketing conditions and support the importance of storage, market…

abstract: The announcement of the MSCI (Morgan Stanley Capital International) Index Review on May 12, 2026, which temporarily suspended the rebalancing of Indonesian equities, represented a major information event for the Indonesian capital market and raised questions about investor responses. This study examines market reactions by analyzing Abnormal Return (AR) and Trading Volume Activity (TVA) of 30 stocks included in the Jakarta Islamic Index (JII). The market-adjusted model was employed to estimate abnormal returns, while the t-test and paired sample t-test were used for statistical analysis. The results show that Average Abnormal Return (AAR) did not change significantly throughout the event window, including the periods before, on, and after the announcement. In contrast, trading activity was statistically significant on Day −9, Day −8, Day −7, Day −6, and Day −4, although no significant changes were observed on the remaining trading days. The paired sample t-test further confirms that there was no significant difference in abnormal returns before and after the MSCI Index Review announcement, whereas Trading Volume Activity differed significantly. These findings indicate that the MSCI Index Review announcement influenced trading activity rather than stock returns. Therefore, investors should not rely solely on the announcement to obtain abnormal returns, while regulators and liste…

Rooted in a post-positivist paradigm and employing a descriptive cross-sectional survey design, the study collected data from 34 final-year pre-service teachers across universities and the colleges of education in Lagos State using the adapted Pre-Service Teacher Inclusive Readiness Questionnaire (PTIRQ). Data were analyzed using the descriptive statistics (means and standard deviations) and frequency distributions. The outcomes indicate that pre-service teachers hold a moderate-to-strong theoretical knowledge of inclusive principles, a generally optimistic, rights-based orientation toward inclusion, and positive attitudes toward teaching learners with disabilities, while expressing some apprehension about their practical readiness to manage changing classrooms. abstract: This study analyzed the influence of shift work perception and employee motivation on service delivery among employees of 24-hour convenience stores in Tagum City, Philippines. Anchored in the Job Demands–Resources Theory and supported by Self-Determination Theory, Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, and the Service-Profit Chain model, the research employed a quantitative, non-experimental descriptive–correlational design. A stratified random sample of 180 rank-and-file employees from selected convenience stores completed validated survey questionnaires measuring shift work perception using the Perception of Effects of Shiftwork Questionnaire, employee motivation using the Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale, and service delivery using an adapted SERVPERF instrument. Results indicated that shift work perception and employee motivation were at moderate levels, while service delivery was rated high. Correlation analysis revealed significant relationships between shift work perception, employee motivation, and service delivery, although some dimensions exhibited non-significant associations. Regression analysis showed that social relationship, integrated regulation, and external regulation significantly influenced service delivery. The study concludes that employees' perceptions of shift work and their motivational orientation are important predictors of service performance, a…

title: Extending Service Beyond Active Duty: Generalizability of Rheumatoid Arthritis Research Conducted Among US Veterans
abstract: Biomedical research involving US veterans continues to advance health care beyond the Veterans Health Administration. This is particularly true in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), where veteran‐centric research has uncovered novel insights into pathogenesis, risk factors, and disease manifestations, informing clinical care and research across both veteran and nonveteran populations. This includes clinical trials and epidemiologic studies in cardiovascular disease, frailty, glucocorticoid use and complications, malignancy, medication adherence, mental health, metabolic comorbidity, mortality, multimorbidity, osteoporosis, RA‐associated interstitial lung disease, sex differences in treatment response, and smoking or other environmental interactions. Given the unique characteristics of the veteran population, the generalizability of veteran‐centric research findings toward other populations has been questioned. Although there are certain exposures specific to the veteran population (eg, burn pits or toxic exposures), most RA research objectives in veterans, including those listed above, are equally relevant to the nonveteran population, and their generalizability across these groups should be carefully considered. The aim of this review is to compare findings between veteran and nonveteran populations, demonstrating and supporting the generalizability of this research.

title: Development of Fire-Resistant Polymer Composites for Decorative Building Materials and Comprehensive Evaluation of their Fire-Technical and Service Properties
abstract: This study focuses on improving the fire-technical and mechanical performance of decorative polymer composite materials based on unsaturated polyester resin. CaCO₃, SiO₂, marble granules, Ammophos, and, in selected formulations, Al(OH)₃ were used as functional fillers and flame-retardant additives. Four compositions (Polyester-1 to Polyester-4) were evaluated by limiting oxygen index (LOI), UL-94 vertical burning classification, time to ignition (TTI), total heat release (THR), flexural behavior, and tensile properties. All formulations achieved UL-94 V-0. LOI increased from 27.8 to 35.4%, TTI increased from 24 to 41 s, and THR decreased from 76 to 58 MJ/m². Polyester-3 exhibited the highest flexural load capacity together with substantial deformability, whereas Polyester-4 produced the strongest fireperformance indicators. The results show that a combined mineral-phosphorus-aluminum-hydroxide system can be used to balance fire safety and service performance in decorative construction composites. The proposed formulations are promising for artificial marble, decorative slabs, interior wall panels, and related finishing elements.

Factors Shaping Patients Choice of Health Service at the Council-Designated Hospitals in the Lake Zone, Tanzania

abstract: ABSTRACT Peanut ( Arachis hypogaea L.) flavour quality is an important determinant of its market value and consumer acceptance. No‐tillage (NT), a widely adopted conservation agricultural practice, reduces soil disturbance and alters soil microbial communities, potentially influencing the accumulation of flavour‐related compounds in peanut. However, the mechanisms linking NT management to peanut flavour quality, particularly through soil nitrogen dynamics and microbial processes, remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of NT versus conventional tillage (CT) on soil physicochemical properties, microbial community function, and flavour quality of peanut in the red soil region of Southern China. Results showed that, compared to CT, the NT substantially increased the soil pH, total nitrogen, and ammonium (NH 4 + ) nitrogen content, while decreasing nitrate (NO 3 − ) nitrogen. NT also substantially enhanced the abundance of nitrification functional genes that is, AOA ‐amoA and AOB ‐amoA and reduced cumulative CO 2 emissions and global warming potential, but increased CH 4 and N 2 O emissions. Localization and anticipation of seizure onset and propagation using network architecture of pathological high‐frequency oscillations
abstract: Abstract Objective In focal epilepsies, seizures originate from a presumed seizure onset zone (SOZ) and propagate through a network of dynamically interconnected brain regions. Accurate identification of the SOZ and propagation pathways is critical for surgical planning in patients with drug‐resistant epilepsy. We tested the hypothesis that pathological high‐frequency oscillation (pHFO) network properties can characterize seizure propagation at the individual‐patient level. Methods We measured pHFOs (80–500 Hz) in >9000 channel‐hours of intracranial electroencephalographic data recorded during early epilepsy monitoring unit recordings and across 46 seizures in 20 patients implanted with subdural ( n = 11) or depth electrodes ( n = 9). An additional prospective validation patient with two seizures was included for independent testing. We used graph theory‐based features to map pHFO networks, measured propagation latency, and applied machine learning frameworks to determine how network metrics inform seizure propagation. We then evaluated the predictive utility of these network features for identifying both the origin and propagation pathways of pHFOs and examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of the pHFO network prior to seizure onset. title: Beyond the Black Box: Algorithmic Accountability and the Legal Regulation of Predictive Analytics and Machine Learning in India
abstract: The proliferation of predictive analytics and machine-learning systems has transformed decision-making across banking, insurance, healthcare, employment, policing, welfare administration, education and advertising in India. Algorithms no longer merely inform human choices; with increasing frequency they determine outcomes that affect individuals’ rights, livelihoods and opportunities. This transformation has produced what is commonly described as the “black box” problem: decisions are generated through processes that are technically complex, commercially proprietary and cognitively opaque, leaving affected persons unable to understand, contest or seek redress against them. Algorithmic systems trained on historical data further risk reproducing and amplifying existing patterns of discrimination against already disadvantaged groups. India’s existing legal architecture, anchored principally in the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, offers meaningful safeguards for the processing of personal data but does not comprehensively regulate the algorithmic decisions that such data ultimately produces. Constitutional guarantees of equality and non-arbitrariness under Article 14 and of privacy, dignity and personal liberty under Article 21 supply an important normative foundation for extending accountability beyond data governance. This paper undertakes a doctrinal examination of a…

A systematic methodology for strain–temperature decoupling in dual-band flexible frequency-selective surface sensors
abstract: Abstract To address the degradation of measurement accuracy in frequency selective surface (FSS) sensors caused by temperature interference during strain measurements, this work presents a K/Ka dual-band flexible FSS sensor. The sensor exploits the differential sensitivity of the two frequency bands to strain and temperature to obtain resonant frequencies containing coupled strain–temperature information. To resolve the cross-coupling problem in dual-parameter measurements, a systematic decoupling framework is proposed, comprising three decoupling strategies with distinct modeling pathways: physics-based analytical modeling using linear matrix decoupling with nonlinear error compensation; globally data-driven black-box modeling employing two-dimensional spline interpolation combined with numerical optimization; and lightweight modeling for locally sparse data based on nearest-neighbor interpolation. Decoupling performance was evaluated using mutually exclusive calibration, validation, and independent test conditions generated by full-wave simulations, and was quantified in terms of RMSE, MAE, and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Separate strain-only and temperature-only experiments confirmed the differential sensitivities of the two resonant bands. Bilateral Keratouveitis and Secondary Glaucoma in a Young Dog With Immune‐Mediated Polyarthritis and Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome
abstract: ABSTRACT A 7‐month‐old intact female mixed‐breed dog presented emergently for inability to walk, lethargy, and vomiting. The patient was diagnosed with immune‐mediated polyarthritis (IMPA) and secondary systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Bilateral keratouveitis and secondary glaucoma developed within 24 h of presentation. Thorough diagnostic testing failed to identify an underlying etiology. Despite aggressive medical management, the patient developed rapid vision loss. Due to poor visual prognosis and anticipated need for long‐term medical management, both eyes were enucleated. Histopathological evaluation of both globes revealed severe corneal endothelial injury most consistent with endotheliitis with associated uveitis and endophthalmitis. Testing of ocular tissue with PCR and immunohistochemistry for canine adenovirus was negative, and comprehensive infectious disease screening, joint cultures, and ocular histopathology identified no other causative agents. Following enucleation, the dog systemically improved with anti‐inflammatory and antimicrobial medical management. This report highlights a unique and severe case of bilateral keratouveitis with glaucoma following a systemic inflammatory event.

abstract: Abstract To clarify the intrinsic relationship between overburden structural instability and strata behavior during single-pass full-height extraction of a deep extra-thick coal seam, this study investigated Panel 140,504 of the Kouzidong Coal Mine using an integrated approach that combined in situ strata-pressure monitoring, theoretical analysis of overburden fracture, and FLAC3D numerical simulation. Variations in shield working resistance, main-roof fracture characteristics, and the mining-induced stress field were systematically examined as the face advanced. The results showed that shield working resistance remained at 18–20 MPa during the initial mining stage but increased rapidly after immediate-roof caving, reaching a peak of nearly 40 MPa. As the exposed span of the main roof increased, first weighting occurred after the face had advanced approximately 32.5 m. Theoretical calculations based on multi-stratum equivalent-load transfer and an elastic-foundation beam fracture criterion yielded first- and periodic-fracture spans of 32.5 and 13.27 m, respectively. title: Microbiome-related polygenic risk scores and treatment response in depression
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in microbiome research have underscored the intricate connection between the human gut microbiota and mental health disorders, such as depression. This study pioneers a unique investigative approach within the field of the gut-brain axis, focusing on the gut microbiome’s capacity to serve as a biomarker for predicting antidepressant response, a novel concept in neuropsychiatric research. Using the unique Texas Resillience Against Depression (T-RAD) study, we computed polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for 25 heritable gut bacteria from individual-level genotype and microbiome data. PRSs were also computed in 226 participants in the Establishing Moderators and Biosignatures of Antidepressant Response in Clinical Care (EMBARC). This design allowed us to validate microbial PRSs identified in T-RAD. The ability of microbial PRS to predict treatment outcome was tested in the EMBARC cohort using individual-level genotype data and treatment outcome. Logistic regression analysis in EMBARC demonstrated that 3 microbiome PRS showed a significant predictive value for remission after 8 weeks of treatment with sertraline and 1 microbiome PRS that showed a significant predictive value for remission at 16 weeks following augmentation of sertraline treatment with bupropion. title: NexGen Smart Traffic Controller System with Emergency Response
abstract: Urban traffic congestion imposes a severe and measurable cost on emergency response, delaying ambulances, fire trucks, and police vehicles at precisely the moments when minutes determine patient outcomes. Existing traffic-signal infrastructure is predominantly static or locally reactive and provides no mechanism for city-scale, real-time emergency prioritization, hospital pre-arrival awareness, or verifiable, role-based control over who may exercise such priority. This paper presents the design of NexGen, a software-only intelligent transportation system that combines real-time GPS tracking, machine-learning-assisted route optimization, and dynamic, temporary-corridor traffic-signal control across three coordinated interfaces — an emergency-vehicle application, a hospital dashboard, and a traffic-control-center dashboard with a dedicated field-officer mode. The design places particular emphasis on the identity-and-access layer: a shared, accessible, light-themed UI spans login, role-specific registration, verification, and a formal administrator account-approval workflow with step-up re-authentication and multi-factor authentication for high-privilege roles, ensuring that emergency-priority capability is granted only to verified, auditable accounts. abstract: Alternative Learning System (ALS) mobile teachers work across community-based settings that require instructional flexibility, mobility, and sustained engagement with diverse learners. This descriptive phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of ALS mobile teachers in Lower Apayao during School Year 2023-2024 and examined how participants perceived these experiences as shaping their instructional practice and interpersonal relationships. Ten current ALS mobile teachers were purposively selected. Data were generated through semi-structured individual interviews and analysed using Colaizzi's phenomenological procedure, including repeated reading, extraction of significant statements, formulation of meanings, clustering of themes, integration of findings, and participant validation. Four prominent experience domains emerged: commuting and transportation, security, finances, and community mapping. Participants described variable travel distances, difficult road and weather conditions, occasional safety concerns during community-based work, resource limitations and out-of-pocket instructional expenses, and challenges in identifying and enrolling prospective learners. abstract: Pupils with disabilities require well-managed support services to participate effectively in learning and achieve satisfactory academic outcomes in inclusive primary schools. In Serengeti District, limitations in trained personnel, instructional resources, coordination, and monitoring may reduce the effectiveness of these services and adversely affect pupils’ academic performance and retention. This study examined the relationship between the management of support services and the academic performance of pupils with disabilities in primary schools in Serengeti District, Tanzania. The objective was to assess the relationship between the management of support services and the academic performance of pupils with disabilities. A mixed-methods convergent design was employed, involving both questionnaires and interviews. The sample included 126 respondents, comprising head teachers, ward education officers, and district education officers selected from a population of 166 school leaders. Questionnaires provided quantitative data from head teachers, while interviews with ward and district education officers generated qualitative insights. title: Residual‐Risk Concentration and the Reliability of Value‐Weighted Portfolio Returns
abstract: ABSTRACT Value‐weighted factor portfolios can hold more than a thousand stocks yet remain exposed to firm‐specific risk through only a few. I measure this concentration with residual‐risk breadth , the effective number of firms contributing to return variation unexplained by standard equity factors. Across 70 anomaly portfolios from 1980 to 2024, median breadth falls from 12.7 to 4.0 while the stock count remains above 1000. Weight concentration explains about 41% of the decline; much of the remainder reflects erosion of a historical diversification advantage associated with lower residual variance among larger firms. Recent factor returns are consequently more sensitive to a few companies. A 10% constituent cap raises recent breadth by 81%, reduces the upper tail of residual returns by 14%, and lowers the median within‐predictor alpha standard error by 13% without increasing drift‐adjusted rebalancing turnover. The evidence points to declining reliability of realized value‐weighted factor returns.

title: EMPLOYEE REWARD SYSTEM AND PERFORMANCE OF INSURANCE COMPANIES IN NAIROBI CITY, KENYA
abstract: Insurance companies operate in a highly competitive and regulated environment that demands motivated, productive, and retained employees to sustain organizational performance. Despite the strategic importance of employee reward systems in driving performance, many insurance firms in Kenya continue to experience challenges related to employee motivation, inequitable compensation, and weak non-financial recognition structures. title: Lean Construction Practices and Construction Waste Management in Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: Rapid urbanization in megacities such as Lagos, Nigeria, has intensified construction waste generation, creating environmental and municipal waste management challenges. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. title: Between Treaty Text and Arbitral Reasoning: Overlap and Divergence in the Core Investor-Protection Standards
abstract: This paper examines the core standards of investor protection in international investment law, namely fair and equitable treatment, full protection and security, most-favoured-nation and national treatment, expropriation, and umbrella clauses. Adopting a doctrinal approach, it argues that the content of these standards cannot be derived from treaty drafting alone. Open-textured clauses acquire practical shape through tribunal reasoning, which has prompted states to recalibrate treaty language. Proceeding standard by standard, the paper maps dominant treaty drafting approaches and traces how tribunals have interpreted them across a representative sample of awards selected for doctrinal salience, forum diversity, and the availability of reasoned decisions. It shows that fair and equitable treatment is the principal site of interpretive divergence, that full protection and security has expanded from physical protection towards legal security, and that the procedural reach of most-favoured-nation clauses remains contested, while expropriation and umbrella-clause doctrine test the boundaries between regulation and takings, and between treaty and contract. title: Adaptive multi-scale dual-attention network with hyperparameter learning for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Abstract Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for reliable operation and efficient dispatch of modern power systems. However, PV generation is strongly affected by meteorological variability and exhibits pronounced intermittency, fluctuations, and heterogeneous temporal characteristics. To address the strong intermittency and complex temporal dynamics of PV generation, this study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework, SSA-DABNet. First, a multi-scale dilated convolutional neural network (MCNN) with parallel branches and different dilation rates is developed to capture short-term fluctuations and long-term trends while enlarging the effective receptive field. Then, a dual-stage attention mechanism is introduced by integrating the squeeze-and-excitation (SE) block with temporal attention, enabling adaptive feature weighting in both channel and temporal dimensions to enhance critical information representation while suppressing redundant features. Finally, the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is employed to optimize key hyperparameters, including the sliding-window size, SE reduction ratio, and initial learning rate, reducing dependence on manual tuning and improving model adaptability. Experiments conducted on real-world data from a PV power station in Gansu demonstrate that the proposed model achieves stable and accurate forecasting performance, wit…

title: PENGARUH EARNINGS PER SHARE (EPS) DAN PRICE TO BOOK VALUE (PBV) TERHADAP HARGA SAHAM PADA PERUSAHAAN INFRASTRUKTUR DI BURSA EFEK INDONESIA (BEI) PERIODE 2022-2024
abstract: ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Earnings Per Share (EPS) dan Price to Book Value (PBV) terhadap harga saham perusahaan sektor infrastruktur yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) periode 2022–2024. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh pentingnya indikator kinerja keuangan dalam memengaruhi keputusan investor dan pergerakan harga saham. Kajian pustaka berfokus pada teori sinyal dan teori nilai perusahaan yang menjelaskan bahwa EPS dan PBV mencerminkan kinerja serta prospek perusahaan di masa depan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain ex post facto. Populasi penelitian terdiri atas 70 perusahaan sektor infrastruktur yang terdaftar di BEI, sedangkan teknik purposive sampling menghasilkan 46 perusahaan dengan 138 observasi. Data diperoleh dari laporan keuangan tahunan yang dipublikasikan pada situs resmi BEI dan dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda data panel melalui aplikasi E-Views 12. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa EPS dan PBV secara parsial maupun simultan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap harga saham. EPS yang tinggi menunjukkan kemampuan perusahaan menghasilkan laba per saham, sedangkan PBV yang tinggi mencerminkan nilai perusahaan dan kepercayaan investor yang baik. Nilai koefisien determinasi sebesar 99,88% menunjukkan bahwa variasi harga saham sebagian besar dapat dijelaskan oleh EPS dan…

title: From Pest Surveillance to Precision Management: Emerging Technologies for Monitoring, Forecasting and Sustainable Management of Rice Stem Borers
abstract: Rice stem borers continue to be major pests in rice cultivation because their larval forms exhibit cryptic behaviour, asynchronous development and dependence on crop phenology, which undermine conventional scouting approaches. The yellow stem borer, Scirpophaga incertulas (Walker), and the striped stem borer, Chilo suppressalis (Walker), are among the major rice pests that have been widely studied. Studies have demonstrated that a combination of pheromone and light traps, weather, phenology, remote sensing, geographic information systems, computer vision and machine learning can contribute to improved integrated pest management. Weather-based, spatio-temporal and phenology-driven models can be used to predict the temporal abundance of crop pests at specific developmental stages, while satellite and unmanned aerial system (UAS), remote sensing allows pest infestation to be assessed at large scales. Automated trapping systems, hyperspectral imaging and convolutional neural networks can improve detection speed and accuracy. Nevertheless, adoption of these technologies is limited by data shifts, difficulties in species- and life-stage-specific identification limited field validation of modern technologies”high sensor costs, and the absence of links between predicted risks and management actions. Biological control agents, mating disruption, host plant resistance, RNA interference t…

Every Locale Has Its Rhythm: Endow Time-Series Transformers with Spatial Insights for Long-term Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
abstract: Transformers have demonstrated promise in time-series forecasting, attributed to their superior capability of capturing temporal dependencies. Nevertheless, prevailing transformer models predominantly concentrate on the temporal dependencies within single-/multi-variate time series. This focus results in insufficient characterization of spatial correlations among time series. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces G raph T i me-Ser i es T ransformer (GïT), a novel approach aimed at enhancing long-term spatio-temporal forecasting. GïT judiciously integrates the principles of Transformer and Graph Neural Network (GNN). It designs a novel Vertex-wise Decoupled Patching scheme, where each univariate time series in the temporal graphs is segmented into subseries-level patches, which serve as input tokens to the Transformer. These patches are subsequently input into a Transformer encoder to generate representations of patches that capture temporal correlations. The Transformer representations of univariate time series are subsequently processed by Cross-vertex Multivariate Representation , where representations of univariate time series are re-associated to vertices in the temporal graphs and enhanced with Laplacian position encoding. The enhanced representations are further processed by a graph convolutional network to capture the spatial correlation between time series. GïT is e…
