title: Patient-environment transmission dynamics of multidrug resistant Enterobacteriaceae in a Dutch intensive care unit: a longitudinal retrospective and prospective analysis in a non-outbreak setting
abstract: Abstract Background In the intensive care unit (ICU), nosocomial acquisition of multidrug resistant Enterobacteriaceae (MDRE) may lead to adverse patient outcomes; however, investigating the link between patient MDRE colonization and environmental reservoirs is often not straightforward in a non-outbreak setting. This study aimed to characterize the patient-environment transmission dynamics of MDRE strains with a common resistance phenotype and genotype at the ICU wards of two hospitals. Methods The sink drains, faucet aerators, high-touch sites of medical devices and beds of (non-)patient rooms of two ICU were repetitively sampled (up to ten times) over the course of 18 months (2022 to 2023). Patient isolates and epidemiological data were collected retrospectively (2017 to 2022) and prospectively (during the environmental sampling). Inclusion criteria for MDRE isolates were: resistance to 3 rd -generation cephalosporins, gentamicin, ciprofloxacin and cotrimoxazole; and PCR positive for the antimicrobial resistance genes bla CTX-M-15 , qnrB1 and bla OXA-1 — aac(6’)-Ib-cr . Patient and subsetted environmental MDRE isolates were whole genome sequenced using Illumina technology. Clonal clusters were identified with SNP-analysis (≤25 SNPs), and further assessed through spatial and temporal epidemiological links. title: From Creative Content to Commercial Value: Determinants of Financial Viability in Student-Led Publishing Startups
abstract: This study examines the determinants of financial viability in student-led publishing startups in Vietnam by investigating how creative and market-oriented attributes contribute to perceived commercialization capability and, subsequently, financial viability. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities View, the study develops a model incorporating content quality, visual design, community engagement, brand authenticity, and digital accessibility as antecedents of perceived commercialization capability. Data were collected from 217 respondents involved in student-led publishing ventures and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that all five antecedents positively influence perceived commercialization capability, while perceived commercialization capability is strongly associated with financial viability. The results also demonstrate significant indirect relationships between all five antecedents and financial viability through perceived commercialization capability. The findings highlight the importance of developing commercialization capabilities alongside creative resources and suggest that student publishing ventures should integrate content development, brand building, community engagement, and digital distribution with systematic market-oriented activities. Defect-Controlled p-Type Conductivity in an Ultrawide-Bandgap ZnGa2O4 Film
abstract: Abstract Ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors are central to next-generation power electronics and deep-UV optoelectronics, yet the absence of reliable p-type materials remains a critical bottleneck. Here, we demonstrate stable intrinsic p-type conductivity in the spinel UWBG oxide ZnGa2O4, epitaxially grown on c-plane sapphire via mist chemical vapor deposition. The films exhibit high crystalline quality, evidenced by relatively narrow rocking curves and atomically smooth surfaces. Hall measurements confirm stable p-type conduction with a hole mobility of 4.43 cm2 V−1 s−1 and a carrier concentration on the order of 1015 cm−3 in the optimized film at room temperature. By off-stoichiometrically tuning the Zn/Ga precursor ratio, we reveal that intrinsic p-type behavior originates from the antisite defect, establishing cation disorder as an important mechanism governing carrier polarity. Comprehensive structural, optical, electrical, and first-principles analyses indicate the interplay between defect chemistry and charge transport in spinel oxides. These results position ZnGa2O4 as a viable p-type UWBG semiconductor and introduce defect-controlled spinel oxides as promising materials for future high-power and extreme-environment electronics.

title: We're Mutually Helping Each Other Out: Intergenerational Learning Between Adult Artists and Teen Participants Through a BIPOC , Community‐Centred Arts Programme
abstract: Abstract This study examines intergenerational learning within a community‐based art education (CBAE) summer programme serving multilingual BIPOC youth in Oakland, California. Using embedded ethnography, semi‐structured interviews and surveys, we investigated how high school youth and adult teaching artists co‐created public art installations for community spaces. Grounded in communities of practice, culturally sustaining pedagogy and constructionism, findings reveal three interconnected outcomes: first, youth developed technical artistic and professional workforce competencies through hands‐on mentorship; second, newcomer youth practised English organically through low‐stakes collaborative art‐making; and third, participants deepened civic engagement and cultural identity by connecting personal immigrant experiences to local place‐based histories. This learning flowed in both directions, disrupting traditional power dynamics as adult artists also deepened their facilitation, leadership and community‐engaged practices through working alongside youth. This study contributes to CBAE by demonstrating how reciprocal intergenerational public art‐making creates unique conditions that bring together skill development, language practice, civic engagement and workforce readiness within BIPOC communities.

title: From State Financial Loss to Investment Risk: Reconstructing State Financial Accountability in SOEs Management Based on Fairness and Sustainable Governance
abstract: State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) play a strategic role in national economic development. Yet, their investment management is constrained by the coexistence of the result-based liability paradigm under Law No. 17 of 2003 and the risk-based governance paradigm introduced by Article 3H of Law No. 16 of 2025. This regulatory disharmony creates legal uncertainty that discourages directors from making strategic investment decisions because commercially reasonable investments may be criminalized when they fail. This study examines the paradigm shift in state financial accountability and reconstructs an accountability model grounded in fairness and sustainable governance. Employing normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and philosophical approaches, the study analyzes legislation, Constitutional Court decisions, legal doctrines, and relevant literature. The findings demonstrate that investment losses should not automatically be classified as state financial losses. Instead, they should be recognized as ordinary business risks, provided investment decisions are made in good faith, with due care, free from conflicts of interest, and in accordance with the principles of Good Corporate Governance and the Business Judgment Rule. Accordingly, legal accountability should focus on the integrity of the decision-making process rather than solely on financial outcomes. The proposed re…

title: Characterization of Formation Deformation during Production Test from Gas Hydrate in Alaska: A Distributed Fiber Optic Sensing Approach
abstract: Abstract Reliable monitoring of geomechanical responses is essential for the safe and sustainable production of gas hydrate reservoirs. This study reports the first field-scale application of distributed strain sensing (DSS) during a 10 month extended gas production test on Alaska’s North Slope. DSS cables installed in production and monitoring wells continuously captured axial and bending strain at high spatial resolution, directly linking depressurization to formation deformation. The observations revealed compressive strain within the hydrate-bearing interval and tensile strain in the surrounding layers, consistent with stress redistribution previously predicted by geomechanical simulations. After the transition from electric submersible pump (ESP) to jet-pump operation, localized bending strain became evident, suggesting possible casing–cement deformation. Interwell measurements further demonstrated strain propagation and physically consistent attenuation away from the production well. Integrated analysis indicated that inward casing–cement deflection during depressurization could have a greater contribution to the measured strain than reservoir compaction and that plastic strain may have developed in the cement where the DSS cable was embedded. This finding emphasizes the need for integrated validation with numerical simulations and additional testing to improve the curren…

title: Grating-lens metafiber with enhanced angular acceptance for broadband light coupling
abstract: Efficient coupling of light into optical fibers is essential for a wide range of applications in telecommunications, sensing, imaging, and quantum photonics. Conventional fiber interfaces typically exhibit a limited angular acceptance interval, restricting their ability to efficiently collect and route light from off-axis sources. Here, we present a 3D-nanoprinted Metafiber that enables angle-selective coupling into a single-mode optical fiber while providing a broadband angular acceptance interval through a multiphase on-fiber grating lens. The device combines directional light coupling with suppression of undesired diffraction orders and is fabricated directly on spacer-enhanced fibers using high-resolution 3D nanoprinting. Optical characterization demonstrates efficient coupling over a substantially extended angular range while maintaining selective excitation of the fiber mode and strong zeroth-order suppression. These results establish a versatile Metafiber platform for directional light collection and spatial demultiplexing, offering new opportunities for fiber-based imaging, sensing, and integrated photonic systems.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance dan Investment Opportunity Set terhadap Kebijakan Dividen
abstract: The increasing demand for transparent corporate governance and effective dividend policies has become a critical issue for companies operating in the mineral and coal sector, particularly due to the industry's capital-intensive nature and investment uncertainty. Understanding the factors that influence dividend policy is essential for balancing shareholders' expectations with corporate growth opportunities. This study aims to examine the effect of good corporate governance, proxied by managerial ownership and institutional ownership, and the investment opportunity set on dividend policy. This research employs an associative quantitative approach. The population consists of 23 mineral and coal sector companies listed during the observation period. The sample was selected using purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria, resulting in eight companies observed over five years, yielding a total of 40 panel data observations. Panel data regression analysis was applied to test the proposed hypotheses. The partial test results indicate that managerial ownership, as a proxy for good corporate governance, has no significant effect on dividend policy. In contrast, institutional ownership has a significant effect on dividend policy. The investment opportunity set also has a significant effect on dividend policy. Furthermore, the simultaneous test demonstrates that good corporate go…

title: Investigation on Thermally-Induced Dynamic Response of an On-Orbit Orthotropic Laminated Panel Based on Carrera Unified Formulation
Decentralized Solar-Driven Plant Factories Secure an Adequate Global Vegetable Supply beyond the Electricity Grid and Water Limitations
abstract: Abstract Conventional open-field vegetable production is increasingly constrained by climate volatility and natural resource endowments, creating supply instabilities and shortages that threaten global food resilience and human health. Here, we integrate solar photovoltaics and atmospheric water harvesting with plant factories, creating a technically mature off-grid agricultural system using plant factories (OASIS). By decoupling production from local water and grid infrastructure, OASIS significantly expands the area suitable for cultivation. Globally, OASIS can meet the recommended upper vegetable intake (600 g capita–1 day–1) for at least 98.3% of the population, leveraging mostly non-arable land. Cropland substitution could spare approximately 578,000 km2 for staple food production and, under the idealized zero-operational-loss case, reduce agricultural nitrogen and phosphorus losses by up to 9.90 and 0.95 Tg yr–1, respectively. Estimated global, production-weighted levelized costs were 3.8–4.0 USD kg–1 across six scenarios. Under the 600 g capita–1 day–1 scenario with cropland substitution, OASIS offered cost advantages over existing production benchmarks in 115 of 166 comparable countries, including all 26 low-income countries, which could meet modeled supply targets with a 32.2% average cost advantage. These results highlight OASIS’s potential to advance resilient, clean…

title: The Black Market for Human Organs in India: A Criminological Analysis of Exploitation, Organised Crime, and Regulatory Failure under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994
abstract: The illegal trade in human organs in India represents a serious intersection of organised crime, poverty, medical demand, exploitation, and regulatory failure. This paper examines the black market for human organs through a doctrinal, criminological, and interdisciplinary analysis of the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 (“THOTA”), related rules, academic literature, and judicial decisions. It argues that organ trafficking should not be understood merely as an isolated violation of medical regulation. It is a networked form of exploitation involving brokers, vulnerable donors, recipients, medical professionals, hospitals, document facilitators, and administrative authorities. The paper analyses the economic and health consequences experienced by organ sellers, the role of poverty and debt in recruitment, the use of forged relationships and documents, and the involvement of legitimate medical infrastructure in concealing illegal transactions. It further examines six important judicial decisions concerning authorization, altruistic donation, administrative delay, and uniform implementation of transplantation law. The analysis demonstrates that THOTA provides an important statutory foundation but remains weakened by fragmented enforcement, inadequate hospital audits, insufficient victim protection, weak financial investigation, and inconsistent implementation. …

title: When transparency fails: Performative governance in emerging-market oil and gas supply chains
abstract: Purpose: This study examines how sustainability disclosure relates to supplier trust and collaborative willingness in Nigeria’s oil and gas supply chain, drawing on performative governance theory. Design/methodology/approach: A survey of 148 procurement, sustainability and regulatory managers tested a moderated sequential mediation model using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), with 5000 bootstrap resamples, measurement invariance testing and multigroup comparisons. Covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) provided a sensitivity assessment. Findings/results: Sustainability signalling quality was positively associated with perceived authenticity, which predicted supplier trust and collaborative willingness through the hypothesised sequence. Policy alignment perception positively moderated the signalling quality-authenticity relationship, with the largest estimated moderation coefficient among regulators. Practical implications: Managers should prioritise specific, decision-useful and internally consistent disclosure aligned with salient policy expectations. Policymakers should improve policy interpretability and verification cues. Originality/value: The study identifies authenticity as an evaluative mechanism linking sustainability communication to relational governance and policy alignment as a contextual condition shaping this relatio…

title: Mediating effects of total quality management between entrepreneurial and market orientations, and international performance: from the developing-country context
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the direct effect of entrepreneurial orientation (EO) and market orientation (MO) on the international performance of apparel small and medium enterprises (SMEs). It also examines the mediating impact of total quality management (TQM) on the relationship between EO, MO and SMEs’ international performance. Design/methodology/approach The research has used a cross-sectional survey method to collect data from apparel SME owners and senior-level managers in Bangladesh. Data have been collected from 360 exporting firms, and the partial least squares structural equation modeling method has been applied for the final analysis. Findings This research has revealed a positive association among EO, MO and SMEs’ international performance. It has also found a positive mediating effect of TQM on the relationships between EO, MO and SMEs’ performance. Practical implications The results of this study will provide guidelines for the apparel industry executives to apply strategic orientations and TQM to enhance their firms’ performance. Social implications TQM fosters a culture of accountability and collaboration, enhancing employee morale and stakeholder trust across diverse regions. It enables SMEs to meet global quality standards, improving customer satisfaction and competitiveness. Originality/value This pioneering study examines the impact of EO, MO and TQ…

title: Geographical indications, consumer segmentation and market performance: an assessment of extra-virgin olive oil in an emerging market
abstract: Purpose Geographical indications (GIs) and Denominations of Origin (DO) have been introduced worldwide under intellectual property rights agreements. In Chile, extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO) produced in Valle del Huasco holds this type of origin protection. This study analyzes the factors influencing EVOO consumption and the market performance of EVOO brands with and without DO labels. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through a survey questionnaire and analyzed using cluster analysis to segment the market, and multidimensional scaling and logistic regression to assess brand performance. Findings Three consumer clusters were identified: value-seeking mainstream buyers, quality-oriented consumers and origin-proximate direct consumers. Consumers residing near producing regions value product origin, though only a small proportion appreciate DO labels specifically. DO brands outperform most non-DO brands but underperform the two market leaders. The most influential predictors of recommendation and purchase frequency vary by brand. However, DO status, contest prizes and consumer proximity to producing regions consistently emerge as relevant to consumers’ decision-making. Originality/value These findings provide a foundation for marketing strategies that promote EVOO, enhance sustainability, diversify product offerings and preserve regional cultural identity.

title: The moderating role of competitive intelligence in the international market selection and export performance relationship
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether competitive intelligence (CI) strengthens the relationship between international market selection (IMS) and export performance (EP). It argues that CI functions not only as an input to market selection but also as a post-entry execution capability. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was used. First, 12 interviews with export professionals clarified the mechanisms linking CI, IMS, and EP. Second, survey data from 113 Turkish exporters were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Findings IMS and CI both have positive direct effects on EP. More importantly, CI positively moderates the IMS–EP relationship, indicating that systematic IMS produces stronger performance returns when CI capability is higher. Originality/value The study advances a decision–execution explanation of EP by showing that the value of systematic market selection depends partly on firms' ability to sense, interpret, and adapt after entry. It clarifies CI's role as both a direct capability and a moderator of the IMS–EP relationship.

title: Digital leadership and digital capability development for organizational innovation in emerging market SMEs
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how digital leadership (DL) is associated with organizational innovation in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through digital capability (DC) development. It further investigates whether digital culture (DIC) strengthens the relationship between DL and DC, and whether environmental dynamism (ED) conditions the relationships between DC and two forms of organizational innovation: incremental innovation (II) and radical innovation (RI). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 298 Vietnamese SMEs and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The study examines the direct relationships among DL, DC, II and RI, the mediating role of DC, and the moderating roles of DIC and ED. Findings The results show that DL is positively associated with DC and II, whereas its direct relationship with RI is not significant. DC is positively associated with II, but its direct relationship with RI is not supported. DC mediates the relationship between DL and II, but not between DL and RI. DIC strengthens the positive relationship between DL and DC. ED strengthens the relationships between DC and both II and RI, with a substantially stronger moderating effect on RI. These findings suggest that II is more directly associated with leadership orientation and digital capability development, whereas RI depends more he…

title: Mentoring Program for Teachers at Kao Yip Middle School on Creating Interactive, Exploratory, and Inclusive Reviews
abstract: Tinjauan pembelajaran merupakan unsur penting dalam menjamin kualitas pengajaran di sekolah-sekolah yang mengadopsi kurikulum International Baccalaureate (IB), namun program pendampingan internasional yang berfokus pada aspek ini masih terbatas. Kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk mendampingi para guru di Sekolah Menengah Kao Yip di Makau dalam mengevaluasi pembelajaran yang interaktif, eksploratif, dan inklusif. Kegiatan ini dilaksanakan pada 4 Juni 2025 melalui tiga sesi aktivias di kelas 11 bagian internasional yang membahas topik optimasi (Matematika Analisis dan Pendekatan Tingkat Lanjutan), dengan melibatkan anggota ahli lintas negara (dari Afrika Selatan, Italia, dan Belanda) untuk memberikan perspektif kolaboratif. Pengamatan tersebut mengungkap tiga masalah utama: tindak lanjut yang kurang optimal terhadap tugas siswa di Padlet, kurangnya pemanfaatan alat bantu pengajaran kertas HVS, serta ketimpangan partisipasi verbal antara siswa laki-laki dan perempuan. Berdasarkan temuan ini, tim pengabdian mengusulkan tiga solusi: panduan untuk mengoptimalkan tindak lanjut di Padlet, pelatihan dalam perancangan pembelajaran menggunakan alat bantu pengajaran, serta strategi untuk memastikan partisipasi siswa yang setara di dalam kelas. Program pendampingan ini diharapkan dapat memperkuat kapasitas guru dalam menciptakan ekosistem pembelajaran yang dinamis dan inklus…

title: Kepuasan Coste Coffee: Dominasi Layanan dan Peran Terbatas Atmosfer (Coste Coffee Satisfaction: Service Dominance and Atmosphere's Limited Role)
abstract: Penelitian ini menguji hubungan harga, store atmosphere, kualitas produk, dan kualitas pelayanan dengan kepuasan konsumen Coste Coffee di Surabaya. Survei kuantitatif eksplanatori melibatkan 100 konsumen yang memenuhi kriteria dan dipilih melalui accidental sampling dengan kriteria kelayakan purposif. Data dianalisis menggunakan partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan WarpPLS 8.0. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan harga, kualitas produk, dan kualitas pelayanan berhubungan positif dan signifikan dengan kepuasan konsumen, sedangkan store atmosphere tidak menunjukkan hubungan langsung yang signifikan. Kualitas pelayanan menunjukkan hubungan paling kuat di antara prediktor yang diuji , sehingga atribut inti layanan dan produk lebih konsisten dalam menjelaskan kepuasan dibandingkan isyarat lingkungan fisik. Hasil penelitian menegaskan pentingnya standardisasi layanan, konsistensi produk, kejelasan nilai, dan perbaikan atmosfer yang berorientasi fungsi.

title: The role of fintech and digital transformation in enhancing customer satisfaction: Mediating evidence from service quality in online transportation
abstract: This study examines the influence of digital transformation and financial technology (fintech) on customer satisfaction in online transportation services in Indonesia, with service quality as a mediating variable. The study focuses on explaining how technological capabilities are translated into customer satisfaction through perceived service quality. The findings indicate that both digital transformation and fintech have positive and significant effects on customer satisfaction and service quality. Service quality also has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction and mediates the relationships between digital transformation, fintech, and customer satisfaction. These findings suggest that technological innovation creates greater customer value when it is translated into reliable, responsive, and customer-oriented service experiences. The novelty of this study lies in integrating digital transformation and fintech within a single mediation framework, positioning service quality as the mechanism linking technological capabilities to customer satisfaction. The study highlights the importance of complementing technological investment with improvements in service reliability, system responsiveness, transaction security, and overall customer experience to support sustainable customer satisfaction in online transportation services.

Enterprise Architecture for the Research and Community Service Department of Politeknik Internasional Bali Using the TOGAF ADM
abstract: The Research and Community Service Department (LPPM) of PoliteknikInternasional Bali requires an integrated information system to support the management of research activities, community service programs, monitoring and evaluation processes, publication outputs, grant administration, as well as institutional performance and accreditation data. At present, these activities are managed through separate and largely manual procedures, resulting in challenges such as data duplication, delays in information dissemination, difficulties in document retrieval, reduced operational efficiency, and limited integration across business processes.This study aims to develop an Enterprise Architecture blueprint using the TOGAF Architecture Development Method (ADM) framework to support the design of an integrated information system aligned with organizational requirements. A qualitative research approach was adopted through observations, interviews, and document analysis. The TOGAF ADM phases applied in this study include the Preliminary Phase, Architecture Vision, Business Architecture, Information Systems Architecture, Technology Architecture, and Opportunities and Solutions.The proposed architecture consists of several architectural artifacts, including use case diagrams, an Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), network topology design, gap analysis, an implementation roadmap, and information te…

title: Dietary inclusivity as a vulnerability-reducing service condition in hotel food services: evidence from online reviews in Central Europe
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how dietary inclusivity may function as a vulnerability-reducing condition in hotel food services. Drawing on consumer vulnerability theory, it considers dietary restrictions as food-related conditions that may become vulnerability-inducing when service arrangements constrain guests’ control, information, trust or access to suitable food. Design/methodology/approach A quantitatively led sequential mixed-methods design was applied to 88,986 non-empty textual comment fields extracted from Booking.com reviews of 20 four-star hotels in Bratislava and Prague. Computational text analysis identified food-related comment fields, and manual validation retained 439 fields referring to dietary restrictions. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests and qualitative content analysis examined their visibility, valence and associated service conditions. Findings Within the analysed, self-selected corpus, dietary restriction-related content was rare but proportionally more visible in negative than in positive food-related narratives. Evaluations varied across medically grounded, lifestyle-based and religious motives. Five recurring service conditions were associated with dietary accommodation: availability, variety, staff responsiveness, labelling clarity and perceived adequacy. The findings suggest that dietary inclusivity in hotel food services is shaped by …

title: The mediating role of organizational justice in the relationship between cost consciousness and resource efficiency among human service professionals
abstract: Background Organizational psychology research suggests that employees’ perceptions of workplace practices play an important role in shaping organizational outcomes. In resource-constrained Human Service Organizations (HSOs), organizational justice may represent a key psychological mechanism linking cost-conscious practices to resource-efficient behaviors. Objective This study examined whether organizational justice explains the association between cost consciousness and resource efficiency among professionals working in Human Service Organizations (HSOs). Methods A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 246 professionals working in public and municipal human service institutions in Türkiye, including social workers, nurses, and administrative personnel. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and regression-based mediation analysis with Hayes’ PROCESS Macro (Model 4) and 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results Cost consciousness was positively associated with both organizational justice perception ( β = 0.500, p < 0.001) and resource efficiency ( β = 0.466, p < 0.001). Organizational justice was also positively associated with resource efficiency ( β = 0.207, p = 0.001). Mediation analysis indicated that organizational justice partially explained the association between cost consciousness and resource efficiency (indirect effect = 0.104, 95% CI [0.047–0.…

title: Long-Term Service, Fleet, and Robustness Planning for Bali LRT Phase 1A Airport Access
abstract: Bali LRT Phase 1A is a planned 6.04-km airport rail connection from I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport to the Sunset Road area. Its Final Feasibility Study (FS) presents operating quantities at seven forecast horizons. This paper asks what sequence of operating decisions is implied when those quantities are read together. Using the FS as the only numerical source, demand-based service is reconstructed, applied headway is compared with that minimum, fleet needs are checked from the 29-min round-trip time, and transition timing is stressed at ±10% and ±20% demand. The seven horizons collapse into four service states: 10, 8, 7, and 6 min. Passenger fleet requirement follows 4, 5, 6, and 6 trainsets. The last step is therefore not another fleet-purchase point; service becomes denser with the same six passenger trainsets while the passenger-baggage route-conflict indicator reaches 31.51%. Demand deviation mainly changes the calendar. In the +20% case, thresholds associated with the baseline years 2039, 2049, and 2059 are crossed at about 2033, 2041, and 2044. For long-term planning, these results support treating the FS years as review points tied to observed demand rather than as fixed activation dates.

title: Land-use dynamics and multi-scenario projections in a mountainous ecological barrier: ecosystem service value responses and spatial sensitivity
abstract: Introduction Regional changes in ecosystem service value (ESV) may remain limited even when land-use conversion produces pronounced ecological gains or losses at specific locations, making aggregate scenario comparisons insufficient for identifying spatially concentrated responses. Methods Taking the Shaanxi section of the Qinling Mountains as a representative mountainous ecological barrier region, this study examined land-use dynamics from 2000 to 2020 and projected land-use patterns to 2040 under natural development, urban development, cropland protection, and ecological protection scenarios. We coupled Markov–PLUS scenario projections with an equivalent-factor ESV assessment and developed a 240-m grid-based sensitivity index (SI) to relate local relative ESV change to the intensity of land-use conversion. Results Historical hindcasting achieved an overall accuracy of 92.03% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.780. Across the four scenarios, total ESV changed only modestly, ranging from a 0.84% decline under urban development to a 0.42% increase under ecological protection. However, the SI revealed strong and spatially concentrated responses that were not apparent from regional totals. Negative responses were concentrated mainly in river valleys, piedmont zones, peri-urban areas, and forest margins under urban development, whereas positive responses were most extensive under ecologi…

Probiotic modulation of the neonatal gut–lung axis in the regulation of early respiratory function
abstract: Introduction The gut -lung axis represents bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal and respiratory systems that contributes to immune regulation and inflammatory homeostasis. This study evaluated the effects of probiotic-conditioned media (PCM) and live probiotics on epithelial barrier function, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function using Caco-2 intestinal epithelial and A549 pulmonary epithelial cell models under inflammatory conditions. Methods Cells were treated with 20% PCM or live probiotics at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 50:1 and exposed to LPS (1 μg/mL) or TNF-α (10 ng/mL). Barrier integrity was evaluated using transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) and FITC-dextran permeability assays. Reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), inflammatory and tight junction gene expression, and SCFA concentrations were assessed using DCFH-DA staining, JC-1 staining, qPCR, and GC-MS, respectively. All experiments comprised three independent biological replicates (n=3), with data presented as mean ± SD and analyzed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc multiple-comparison test. Results Probiotic treatment increased TEER from 318 ± 21 Ω·cm 2 with LPS to 468 ± 23 Ω·cm 2 with 20% PCM and reduced ROS from 198 ± 12% to 118 ± 8%. Live probiotics produced comparable responses, restoring TEER t…

title: The Clinician’s Scaffold: Manualised Protocols as Regulatory Tools for Therapist Presence and Co-Regulation
abstract: Manualised therapies are typically justified as vehicles for treatment fidelity and evidence translation. However, clinicians often experience manuals as stabilising structures that reduce uncertainty and performance pressure and alleviate the cognitive load of the question “What do I do next?”, especially under high-arousal or high-uncertainty conditions. This article develops the concept of the clinician’s scaffold: manuals, session structures, and decision aids that function as external regulatory supports for therapist presence and relational availability. The central proposal is that some of the apparent value of structured therapies may be mediated not only through direct client-facing mechanisms but also through their effects on the therapist. By narrowing the decision space, scaffolds may reduce stress-driven attentional narrowing, support therapist regulation, and preserve the relational micro-behaviours required for attuned therapeutic work. The article defines key constructs, outlines a parallel process model, considers digital and alternative explanations, and proposes falsifiable predictions. It offers therapist self-regulation under load as a clinical competency deserving further empirical and conceptual development.

Metacognitive thinking and academic self-regulation as predictors of academic burnout among university students in Jordan
abstract: Background This study examined the predictive relationship between metacognitive thinking, academic self-regulation sub-dimensions, and academic burnout among undergraduate students in Jordan. Methods Using a convenience sample of 631 students, three validated scales were administered: the Metacognitive Awareness Inventory, the Academic Self-Regulation Inventory, and the Academic Burnout Inventory. Two-way ANOVA, correlation analyses, and multiple stepwise linear regression were employed to analyze the data. Results Two-way ANOVA revealed no statistically significant differences in metacognitive thinking, self-regulation, or academic burnout based on gender. However, significant differences were identified based on the year of study; upperclassmen (third- and fourth-year students) demonstrated significantly higher levels of metacognitive thinking and self-regulation, whereas first-year students reported the highest levels of academic burnout. Correlation analyses revealed significant inverse relationships between metacognitive thinking, self-regulation, and academic burnout. Multiple stepwise linear regression indicated that self-regulation dimensions—specifically decision-making, goal setting, and learning from mistakes—along with metacognitive thinking, significantly predicted academic burnout, with decision-making emerging as the strongest individual predictor. Conclusion In…

Molecular mechanism of dynamic regulation of the proNGF/NGF ratio in controlling hair follicle cycle transition in liaoning cashmere goats
abstract: Background Nerve growth factor (NGF) and its precursor proNGF exert opposing biological functions in cell proliferation and apoptosis through distinct receptor systems—TrkA versus p75NTR/Sortilin. This study aimed to investigate whether dynamic changes in the relative ratio of proNGF to NGF regulate hair follicle cycle transition in Liaoning cashmere goats (Capra hircus) via the dynamic balance of the TrkA/p75NTR signaling axis, and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms Methods Skin samples from Liaoning cashmere goats were collected during the telogen (March), anagen (September), and catagen (January) phases. Histological structures of hair follicles were examined via hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. The mRNA and protein expression levels of NGF, proNGF, TrkA, p75NTR, and Sortilin across distinct hair follicle cycle stages were assessed using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blotting. In vitro , rat hair follicle stem cells (rHFSCs) and human dermal papilla cells (hDPCs) were employed as cellular models and subjected to 11 different treatment conditions, including NGF alone, proNGF alone, combined treatments with varying proNGF/NGF ratios, and intervention with the TrkA inhibitor K252a. Cell proliferation and apoptosis were evaluated via CCK-8 assay and flow cytometry. Differential ratio groups (control, high-ratio, and low-ratio groups) wer…

title: A method for characterising fire events in high fire frequency landscapes: case study application to North Kimberley fire regimes, Western Australia
abstract: Background Identifying fire events provides insights into fire size distribution, the timing of significant fire events, their behaviour and ignition causes. However, this can be challenging when using temporally coarse datasets across high-fire-frequency savanna landscapes. Aims Develop and validate a fire event delineation (FED) methodology. Methods We introduce a fire size distribution (FSD) method combining high-resolution burnt area mapping with high temporal resolution hotspot data to produce detailed day-of-burn attributed mapping. This approach is applied to 2014–2023 fire mapping of North Kimberley savannas, northern Australia. Key results Analysis of the ten largest fires per year (n = 100) indicated their responsibility for 33.3% of total area burnt annually, with 69% occurring during the late dry season. Additionally, only 35% of these fires started in locations with on-ground access. Remote ignition fires burnt 51 and 64% of total area with all land burnt late in the year, respectively. A ~50% decrease in large fire sizes was observed, due to improved intensive fuel management. Conclusions The FED method provided an easily implementable and useful new approach for understanding fire regimes in high fire frequency landscapes. Implications Previous FSD methods underestimated total fire size for fires burning over multiple months. The method presented here improves on…

Optimization of variable geometry regulation law for a Turboshaft turbofan conversion engine during mode transition using an LPV model
abstract: Abstract To satisfy the requirements of high-speed vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) vehicles for multi-mode propulsion, a Turboshaft turbofan conversion engine is required to achieve smooth and efficient transition between turboshaft and turbofan operating modes. However, during the mode transition process, the coordinated regulation of variable geometry mechanisms induces significant variations in aerodynamic and thermodynamic parameters, resulting in strong nonlinearities, multi-variable coupling, and time-varying characteristics. These complex behaviors may lead to thrust fluctuations and degraded dynamic performance. To address these issues, an optimization method for variable geometry regulation of a Turboshaft turbofan conversion engine based on a linear parameter-varying (LPV) model is proposed.First, the importance of variable geometry control variables during the mode transition process is evaluated using a random forest algorithm, and the scheduling parameters of the LPV model are reduced accordingly. Subsequently, local linear state-space models are established within the selected scheduling parameter space, and an LPV model covering the entire mode transition process is constructed through interpolation. Based on the developed LPV model, a dynamic optimization problem considering actuator constraints and trajectory smoothness is formulated, where the minimum tot…

title: Supporting managers’ emotion regulation in virtual leadership: a qualitative study of HRD and workplace learning conditions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how workplace learning and human resource development (HRD) conditions shape managers’ emotion regulation (ER) capacity in virtual leadership. Rather than treating ER as a stable individual competence, it focuses on workplace learning processes and organizational support through which managers develop and sustain ER capacity. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on 45 semistructured interviews conducted in Germany in 2022 with managers who had led employees virtually or in hybrid settings during the pandemic period. It uses abductive qualitative content analysis, with job demands-resources theory as the primary organizing framework, workplace learning/HRD as the developmental perspective and affordance theory as a supporting lens. Findings The findings show that virtual leadership creates reduced emotional observability, making it harder for managers to perceive mood, strain and relational tension. Managers’ ER capacity was shaped by organizational resources such as trust, autonomy and cultural permission, while HRD support varied considerably. Reflective and social learning spaces emerged as a developmental condition. The study also identifies ambivalent emotional affordances: virtual work can reduce cues and create distance but can also enable safety, disclosure and new forms of closeness. Practical implications The findings suggest …

Adsorption-dominated interfacial regulation by sarcosine via hydrogen-bond water modulation for stable Zn metal anodes
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) hold great promise for safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet their practical application is seriously hindered by the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), uncontrolled dendrite growth, and inert byproduct (Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O) deposition on the Zn anode. In this work, sarcosine (Sar) was adopted as a multifunctional bipolar electrolyte additive, and first‐principles calculations combined with electrochemical tests and interfacial characterizations were performed to reveal its adsorption‐dominated interfacial stabilization mechanism. Sar strongly adsorbs on the Zn surface to homogenize Zn2+ flux, regulate the electric field distribution, and reconfigure the interfacial environment. Meanwhile, Sar forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water molecules via its amino and carboxyl groups, reducing free water activity and suppressing HER. First‐principles calculations verify the favorable adsorption configuration and high adsorption energy of Sar on the Zn surface. As a result, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers ultra‐long cycling stability over 2100 h at 1 mA cm‐2, and the Zn||Cu half‐cell exhibits a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.7%. The full cell with ZnI@CNT‐AC cathode maintains excellent capacity retention after 3000 cycles. This work provides a simple, green, and low‐cost strategy for stabilizing Zn anodes toward practical aqueous…

title: A multimodal deep learning radiomics nomogram integrating clinicopathological features for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in triple-negative breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective study
abstract: Background Accurate noninvasive estimation of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may support multidisciplinary discussions, but multimodal MRI-ultrasound evidence remains limited. We developed and externally validated a clinicopathological deep learning radiomics nomogram and explored its potential auxiliary value in a strictly hypothetical post-hoc surgical-planning scenario. Methods With institutional review-board approval and waived consent, this retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study included 436 biopsy-proven TNBC patients who underwent NAT and surgery: Center 1 training cohort (n = 268) and internal validation cohort (n = 86), plus historical cases from cooperating Centers 2–3 for external validation (n = 82). pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Pretreatment dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and B-mode ultrasound were analyzed. Intratumoral and 5-mm peritumoral ring radiomics features were extracted and selected by LASSO. DenseNet-121 extracted modality-specific deep features, fused using multi-head self-attention. Age, tumor size, Ki-67, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), cT/N stage, and histological grade were integrated with imaging scores in a logistic-regression nomogram.…

title: Human macrophages activate a coordinated program linking inflammation and cell death in response to intracellular Poly(I:C)
abstract: Background Macrophages sense viral double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) via the innate immune receptors TLR3 and MDA5 whose activation drives a robust inflammatory program, often coupled to cell death. TLR3/TRIF-dependent apoptosis has been described in response to dsRNA. Growing evidence suggests that dsRNA may trigger multiple forms of cell death with mechanisms yet to be elucidated. In addition to TLR/TRIF axis, the necroptosis regulator RIPK3 has been implicated in both inflammatory response and cell death during viral infections in several cell types. However, its role in regulating these two events in human macrophages remains unclear. Methods Here, we investigated in human monocyte-derived macrophages (hMDMs) the mechanisms of dsRNA induced cell death and its temporal and molecular linkage to inflammatory signaling, with a focus on the interplay between RIPK3 and the TLR3/TRIF pathways. Results We found that intracellular Poly(I:C), a synthetic analogue of dsRNA, induced cell death with apoptotic and necroptotic features. TRIF-mediated signaling cascade and RIPK3 jointly contributed to caspase-8 activation leading to apoptosis. RIPK3 also promoted necroptosis by inducing MLKL phosphorylation. Downstream of caspases, Poly(I:C) induced cleavage of Gasdermin E (GSDME), which remained intracellular and localized in mitochondria contributing to the amplification of caspase-3 activatio…

title: Interpreting a Multimodal Late-Fusion Model for Municipality-Level Community Bus and Demand-Responsive Bus Classification in Kyushu Area Using SHAP and Grad CAM
abstract: Limited public transport accessibility remains a serious issue in aging and low-density areas such as Japan. Local governments have introduced Community Bus (CB) and Demand-Responsive Bus (DRB) services, but methods for explaining the regional patterns associated with these two service types remain limited. This paper examines the interpretability of a multimodal late-fusion model that integrates tabular regional indicators and Geographic Information System (GIS)-based spatial images for municipality-level CB and DRB classification. The research used municipalities in Kyushu, Japan. A multimodal late-fusion architecture was adopted as a commonly used integration strategy for image and tabular data. Model interpretation was conducted using SHAP for the tabular branch and Grad-CAM for the image branch. Performance was summarized using Macro F1-score as the main metric. The late-fusion model achieved a mean Macro F1-score of 0.5978 and a mean accuracy of 0.6797 under the non-TTA setting. TTA was evaluated as an inference-time robustness strategy and showed slightly smaller fold-wise variability, although the non-TTA setting produced higher mean predictive scores. Therefore, the subsequent interpretation analysis was based on the non-TTA results. SHAP showed that single elder household density, lowest elevation, elder rate, highest elevation, and total population were among the mos…

title: Pediatric Institutions' Instagram Response to the 2025 Acetaminophen-Autism Controversy
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: To describe the timing, frequency, and accessibility of Instagram posts from pediatric health institutions during the 2025 acetaminophen-autism controversy. Methods: Cross-sectional audit of public Instagram accounts of 62 pediatric health institutions from September 22 to November 15, 2025. The a priori sampling frame comprised the top 50 US children's hospitals for pediatric behavioral health, the top 10 Honor Roll children's hospitals (US News and World Report), 5 national medical societies, and health departments of the 10 states with the largest pediatric populations. Posts were extracted with a web-scraping tool and manually verified. Two reviewers independently coded relevant posts for prespecified content and accessibility features. Readability was assessed with two validated measures. Results: Twelve of 62 institutions (19%) posted relevant content. The American Academy of Pediatrics and the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists posted on day 0, while hospital time to first post ranged from 3 to 51 days. No state health department posted. Nonresponding institutions remained active: 1 hospital published 108 unrelated posts. The 26 relevant posts had a mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.4 and SMOG Index of 10.2. Among coded features, 88% included resource links, 73% directed audiences to a health care provider, 46% featured a named cl…

title: Optimizing Buck Converter Transient Response: ESR Considerations and Loop Design
abstract: As the magnitude and slew rate of digital-load current continue to increase, peak output-voltage deviation, recovery time, and stability with low-equivalent-series-resistance (ESR) ceramic capacitors have become central concerns in the design of DC-DC buck converters. This review adopts transientdetection delay, power-stage current-slew capability, and feedback-signal quality as a unified analytical framework to compare hysteretic control, constant-on-time (COT) control, V 2 control, and their voltage-, inductor-current-, and capacitor-current-feedback variants. In addition to examining insufficient ripple, phase lag, and subharmonic-oscillation mechanisms under low-ESR conditions, the review evaluates the benefits of virtual-ripple injection, adaptive boundaries, frequency locking, DCoffset cancellation, and auxiliary-current injection in terms of peak voltage deviation, recovery time, switching-frequency stability, and DC regulation accuracy. Engineering factors that have received comparatively limited attention in earlier reviews are also considered, including the die-area, quiescent-power, calibration-complexity, and light-load-efficiency penalties associated with sensors, error amplifiers, phase-locked loops (PLLs), digital logic, and auxiliary power stages. Multiphase and digital/hybrid ripple-control techniques are further discussed. Finally, architecture-level compariso…

title: Predictive Modelling of Laser Hardening in EN25 Steel using Analytical Heat Source Theory, Response Surface Methodology, and Comparative Gaussian Process–Support Vector Regression
abstract: The present work investigates laser transformation hardening (LTH) of EN25 low-alloy steel (0.3 wt.% C) through an integrated analytical–statistical–predictive modelling framework combining analytical heat source theory, Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR). A moving flat-top rectangular laser beam (10 × 30 mm) was employed to analytically estimate the case depth (CD), case hardness (HD), and residual stress (RS) developed within the hardened zone (HZ). Experiments were conducted according to a Box–Behnken design by varying laser power (1000–1500 W), scan speed (4–6 mm/s), and laser head stand-off distance (300–340 mm). The analytical model, incorporating austenitization-limited heat transfer, predicted case depths in the range of approximately 1.5–2.45 mm and reasonably captured the experimentally observed parametric trends. Experimental case depths ranged from ~0.68 to 2.52 mm, depending on the selected processing conditions. Experimental results showed case hardness values between ~500 and ~747 HV and compressive-type residual stresses ranging from ~-177 to ~-221 MPa. Quadratic RSM models were developed and validated using analysis of variance (ANOVA) to establish quantitative relationships between process parameters and responses; a composite desirability of 0.9623 identified an optimum process condition …

title: Sensitizing tumor response to topoisomerase I antibody-drug conjugate by selective CDK7 inhibition
abstract: This study investigates the transcriptional impact of Q901, a highly selective cyclin-dependent kinase 7 (CDK7) inhibitor in clinical development. Q901 primarily disrupted MYC and E2F-dependent transcription programs, down-regulating cell cycle control and DNA damage repair pathways. CDK7 binding at the promoter-proximal regions was markedly stabilized by Q901, leading to reduced occupancy of MYC, E2F, and RNA polymerase II (RNAPII). These findings offered a novel therapeutic strategy to enhance cancer susceptibility to topoisomerase I (TOP1) DNA-protein cross-links (TOP1-DPCs) induced by TOP1 inhibitors. Resistance to TOP1 inhibitors arises through activation of DNA repair pathways when elongating RNAPII encounters TOP1-DPCs. By suppressing RNAPII transition from initiation to elongation and DNA repair pathways, Q901 stabilizes TOP1-DPCs and sensitizes tumors to TOP1 inhibitors. Preclinical studies demonstrated enhanced tumor suppression when combining Q901 with TOP1 inhibitor–based antibody-drug conjugates (TOP1i-ADCs), highlighting its potential as a therapeutic option for cancers resistant to TOP1i-ADC therapy.

title: Assessing early therapeutic response in extrapulmonary tuberculosis using [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging
abstract: Introduction Monitoring treatment response in extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) remains challenging due to limited microbiological accessibility and the lack of validated biomarkers. [18F]FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography [(18F)FDG-PET/CT] enables assessment of metabolic disease activity and has been explored in infectious diseases, but evidence supporting its use in EPTB is limited. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study including adults diagnosed with EPTB at a tertiary referral center in Denmark between 2016 and 2018. Participants underwent baseline and follow-up [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging after completion of the intensive treatment phase. Clinical data and laboratory parameters, including C-reactive protein (CRP), hemoglobin, leukocytes, albumin, and alanine aminotransferase were collected at baseline and during follow-up. Changes in standardized uptake values (SUVmax) and laboratory markers were analyzed descriptively. Results Seventeen patients were included. Metabolically active disease was detected in all participants at baseline. Most patients (11 out of 14) demonstrated a reduction in lesion number and SUVmax at follow-up, indicating a metabolic response to therapy. However, persistent [18F]FDG uptake was observed in a subset of patients (3 out of 14). Median CRP levels declined from 12 mg/L (range: 0.3–190) at baseline to 3.6 mg/L (ra…

title: Chronic XBP1s-mediated activation of the unfolded protein response impairs CD8+ T cell anti-tumor immunity
abstract: CD8 + T cells play a crucial role in anti-tumor immunity; however, their functionality is compromised by exhaustion driven by chronic antigen exposure, poor tumor microenvironment, and metabolic dysfunction. Activated CD8 + T cells undergo extensive proteomic remodeling, which includes the induction of the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis of the unfolded protein response. However, the functional consequences of sustained IRE1-XBP1 activation in exhausted CD8 + T cells remain elusive. Using a model of constitutive XBP1 activation in CD8 + T cells, we demonstrate that sustained XBP1s signaling leads to reduced homeostatic CD8 + T cell populations, impaired migratory capacity, and dampened anti-tumor immunity. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of the IRE1-XBP1 axis significantly reduces tumor burden through a dual mechanism that targets both tumor cells and the immune compartment. Our findings reveal a previously unappreciated role for XBP1s in regulating CD8 + T cell biology and highlight the IRE1-XBP1 axis as a therapeutic target in solid tumors.

title: Interdisciplinary human-centric architectural framework for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response: leveraging AI modelling and IoT environmental monitoring
abstract: Successful pandemic preparedness and sustainable healthcare security increasingly rely on One Health—linking humans, animals, and the environment. Novel real-time geolocated data sources from social media, the web, digital traces, and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, combined with traditional surveillance data, are increasingly used to power AI models and enhance environmental sensing that is essential for preparedness and response in the One Health context. Despite the abundance of data streams and sensing data, the potential of AI and IoT environmental monitoring for One Health remains unfulfilled. The OHSEW (One Health Surveillance and Early Warning) framework architecture fills this gap by defining a human-centric architecture for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response, leveraging AI modelling and IoT environmental sensing, designed in particular for monitoring vector-borne diseases, zoonoses, and other environmental reservoirs of infectious diseases where the risk of spillover to human populations is high. In the OHSEW framework, we identify a rich spectrum of multiple heterogeneous data sources and a pipeline for improved surveillance, data visualisation, and training predictive AI models. These include open-source population and socioeconomic data, land use, satellite sensing, and weather forecasts, enriched by IoT environmental sensing (providing microcli…

title: NAT10 governs development through the Xrp1-mediated stress response rather than its RNA acetylation activity
abstract: N 4 -acetylcytidine (ac 4 C) is installed by N -acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) and represents the only known acetylation mark on messenger RNA. Since NAT10 also acetylates transfer RNA, ribosomal RNA (rRNA), and proteins, its in vivo molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that knockdown of Drosophila NAT10 induces an eye-to-antenna transformation, c-Jun amino-terminal kinase activation, and cell apoptosis. NAT10 facilitates ac 4 C modification in rRNA, and its loss impairs rRNA processing and ribosomal assembly. Depletion of NAT10 activates the integrated stress response, ultimately leading to reduced global protein synthesis. Crucially, Xrp1 plays a key role in the stress response and its ablation rescues most NAT10 loss-of-function defects and transcriptomic alterations. We also performed acetylated RNA immunoprecipitation and sequencing (acRIP-seq) on control and NAT10 knockdown flies. Furthermore, a catalytically deficient form of NAT10, which is unable to mediate ac 4 C acetylation, completely rescues the lethality of NAT10 mutants. Collectively, these findings establish that NAT10’s primary developmental function stems from its roles in ribosome biogenesis and Xrp1 activation, which are independent of its RNA acetylation activity.

title: Comparative analysis of treatment response to PSMA radioligand therapy using Ga-68 PSMA-11 and F-18 DCFPyL PET imaging
abstract: Purpose Multiple prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET tracers are used for patient selection in radioligand therapy (RLT). This study compared treatment response to RLT across different PSMA tracers. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent Lu-177 PSMA-617 RLT with baseline imaging using either Ga-68 PSMA-11 or F-18 DCFPyL PET. PET parameters were measured, including SUV mean , SUV max , and total tumor volume (TTV). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with PSA50 response, and Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with overall survival. Results Of 140 patients analyzed (Ga-68 PSMA-11: n=51; F-18 DCFPyL: n=89), SUV max and SUV mean did not differ significantly between groups; however, TTV was significantly higher in the Ga-68 PSMA-11 group (p=0.038). In multivariable analysis adjusted for age, baseline PSA, PET tracer type, SUVmean, and log-transformed TTV, PET tracer type was not significantly associated with PSA50 response (OR, 1.318; 95% CI, 0.585–2.970; p=0.505), whereas higher SUVmean was associated with greater odds of PSA50 response (OR, 1.285; 95% CI, 1.126–1.466; p<0.001). Overall survival did not differ significantly between tracer groups (HR, 0.760; 95% CI, 0.507–1.138; p=0.183), with median overall survival of 8.4 and…

title: Determinants of trade in the palm oil industry between exporting and importing countries: A gravity model analysis in Asia, Oceania and Africa
abstract: Background: The global palm oil industry plays a strategic role in international agricultural trade, particularly for developing economies that depend heavily on crude palm oil (CPO) exports as a major source of foreign exchange. Aim: This study aims to analyse the determinants of bilateral CPO exports from major producing countries to importing countries in Asia, Oceania and Africa. Setting: The study is conducted at the bilateral country level, covering 10 leading palm oil exporting countries and a wide range of importing countries across Asia, Oceania and Africa over the period 1995–2023. Method: This study employs a structural gravity model using panel data with a Poisson Pseudo Maximum Likelihood (PPML) estimator to control for multilateral resistance and unobserved heterogeneity. Results: The findings show that conventional gravity variables remain important determinants of bilateral CPO exports; however, their effects differ substantially across regions and income groups. Beyond traditional economic factors, carbon emissions and land-use change emerge as significant environmental determinants, highlighting the heterogeneous role of environmental conditions in shaping international palm oil trade. Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that, beyond traditional economic drivers, environmental conditions play an increasingly important role in shaping global palm oil trade pat…

title: Pengaruh Gaya Kepemimpinan Egosentris, Penerapan Kebijakan Berlebihan dan Lingkungan Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan di Cafe Fork Solo
abstract: This study examines the effect of egocentric leadership style, excessive policy implementation, and work environment on employee performance at Café Fork Solo. In the service industry, particularly the café sector, employee performance plays a crucial role in maintaining service quality and customer satisfaction. However, leadership approaches and internal policies often create challenges that may influence employee productivity. The objective of this research is to analyze both partial and simultaneous effects of egocentric leadership style, excessive policies, and work environment on employee performance. This study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method. Data were collected through online questionnaires distributed to 40 employees using a Likert scale. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS 26, supported by validity, reliability, and classical assumption tests. The results show that egocentric leadership style has a positive and significant effect on employee performance, indicating that firm and centralized leadership can improve work effectiveness. Excessive policies do not have a significant effect, suggesting that employees tend to adapt to strict regulations. Meanwhile, the work environment has a positive and significant influence, confirming that a conducive environment enhances productivity. Simultaneously, all independent variabl…

title: Pengakuan Kerja dan Pengembangan Bakat sebagai Determinan Kepuasan Kerja Barista: Studi Empiris pada Coffee Shop di Kawasan Medan Pancing
abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in Indonesia has created significant challenges in human resource management, particularly regarding the high turnover rate among baristas, which reflects low levels of job satisfaction. This study aims to analyze the effects of work recognition and talent development on the job satisfaction of baristas working in coffee shops located in the Medan Pancing area, both partially and simultaneously. The study employed a quantitative approach using an explanatory research design. The sample consisted of 70 baristas who had been employed for at least three months in coffee shops within the Medan Pancing area, selected through a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale, supported by interviews and documentation. The data analysis techniques included validity testing, reliability testing, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results indicate that work recognition has a positive and significant partial effect on baristas' job satisfaction (t = 3.721; p = 0.000). Likewise, talent development has a positive and significant partial effect on job satisfaction (t = 2.775; p = 0.007). Simultaneously, both independent variables have a significant effect on job satisfaction (F = 10.5…

title: Analisis Persepsi Mahasiswa Akuntansi terhadap Peran Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dalam Pencegahan Fraud di Era Digital
abstract: Digital transformation has strengthened the role of Accounting Information Systems (AIS) as a means of processing financial data that is fast, integrated, and technology-based. On the other hand, technological developments have also increased the complexity of fraud risks, necessitating more effective control systems. This study aims to explore accounting students’ perceptions of the role of AIS in fraud prevention in the digital age. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collected through in-depth interviews with students who have taken courses in Accounting Information Systems, Auditing, and Internal Control. The data were analyzed through the stages of reduction, presentation, and drawing conclusions. The results indicate that students view AIS as a crucial tool in fraud prevention by enhancing transparency, recording accuracy, data security, and providing audit trails that facilitate transaction tracing. The use of technologies such as automation, big data, and artificial intelligence is also considered capable of supporting the early detection of fraud. However, the effectiveness of AIS remains dependent on the competence of human resources, individual integrity, and the quality of an organization’s internal controls. This study is expected to provide input for the development of accounting education and to enhance the readiness of prospective acc…

title: Environmental Jurisprudence in Anthropocene: Evaluation of Law in Addressing Impact of Environment Degradation on Economically Disadvantaged Communities
abstract: The Anthropocene represents a period in which human activities have become a major force influencing the Earth’s ecological systems. Environmental degradation arising from climate change, pollution, deforestation, biodiversity loss and resource depletion does not affect all sections of society equally. Economically disadvantaged communities, including rural, tribal, forest-dependent, agricultural and fishing communities, often experience greater environmental burdens because of their dependence on natural resources and their limited capacity to adapt or to obtain effective remedies. This study examines the relationship between environmental degradation and environmental justice in the Indian context. It analyses the constitutional, statutory and judicial framework governing environmental protection, with particular emphasis on Articles 14, 21, 38, 39(b), 48A and 51A(g), on the major environmental legislation, and on principles such as sustainable development, the precautionary principle, polluter pays, public trust and intergenerational equity. The study further evaluates environmental justice through its distributive, procedural and recognition dimensions. Using a doctrinal and analytical methodology, it examines primary and secondary legal sources in order to assess whether existing Indian environmental law adequately protects economically disadvantaged communities. The study…

title: Analisis Perhitungan Harga Pokok Produksi sebagai Dasar Penetapan Harga Jual pada UMKM Ayam Geprek Nirmala (Studi Kasus)
abstract: This research investigates how the Cost of Goods Manufactured (COGM) determines the retail selling price at Ayam Geprek Nirmala MSME. Utilizing a descriptive quantitative approach within a case study framework, primary data were gathered through direct observations, owner interviews, and financial documentation. The findings reveal daily production costs comprising IDR 330,000 for raw materials, IDR 125,000 for direct labor, and IDR 35,000 for factory overhead. By implementing the Full Costing method, the overall daily production expense reaches IDR 490,000 for 100 servings, resulting in a unit COGM of IDR 4,900. Comparing this calculation to the established retail price of IDR 10,000 per portion yields a profit margin of IDR 5,100 per unit. This positive margin proves that the current pricing strategy effectively covers all manufacturing outlays while ensuring financial gain. In conclusion, accurate COGM calculation is vital for formulating competitive prices, maximizing profit, and maintaining MSME sustainability in a competitive market.

title: Intelligenter Umgang mit dem Waschbär
abstract: Der Waschbär (Procyon lotor) polarisiert. Als invasive Art steht er in Deutschland unter besonderer Beobachtung. Seit der Aufnahme in die EU-Liste invasiver Arten von unionsweiter Bedeutung ist klar: Es muss gehandelt werden. Doch wie? Flächendeckende Bejagung ist aufwendig, teuer und oft wenig effektiv. Neue Ansätze sind gefragt, die ökologisch und praktisch umsetzbar sind. Eine aktuelle Studie in der Uckermark zeigt einen vielversprechenden Weg: das individuenbasierte Management.

title: Prenatal Identification, Transitional Hemodynamic Remodeling, and Multidisciplinary Management of Ebstein's Anomaly with Coexistent Urogenital Malformations: An Observational Analytic Case Study
abstract: Background: Ebstein’s anomaly is an uncommon congenital heart defect with failed tricuspid delamination, right-ventricular atrialization, and severe regurgitation. Prenatal detection is difficult on routine obstetric ultrasonography, and perinatal hemodynamic transition carries substantial mortality. Objective: To document the prenatal identification, transitional neonatal hemodynamic remodeling, and multidisciplinary management of Ebstein’s anomaly with coexistent urogenital malformation. Methods: A 28-year-old multigravida referred at 34–36 weeks with a suspected cardiac anomaly was followed through multidisciplinary re-evaluation, term cesarean delivery, neonatal intensive care, and 3-month follow-up, with serial hemodynamic profiling and risk stratification. Results: Initial referral ultrasound suspected double outlet right ventricle, which was revised to Ebstein’s anomaly (Carpentier Type B) with dilated pulmonary trunk and coexistent bilateral testicular hydrocele and hypospadias upon joint fetomaternal-pediatric cardiology assessment. Delivery at 38–39 weeks yielded a male neonate (3,050 g, Apgar 5/7, SpO2 85%). Postnatal echocardiography confirmed Ebstein’s anomaly with moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (peak pressure gradient 78 mmHg), a 3–4 mm atrial septal defect with right-to-left shunting, and a 3 mm patent ductus arteriosus with left-to-right shunting. title: Faktor-Faktor Penggerak Tax Avoidance : Financial Distress, Firm Size, dan Inventory Intensity
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of financial distress, firm size, and inventory intensity on tax avoidance in Food & Beverage subsector companies in the Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The method used in this study is quantitative. The type of data used is standard data in the form of published financial reports of Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2020–2024 period. Samples were collected using a purposive sampling method. The number of companies used as research samples was 18 companies, with observations for 5 years from 2020–2024, resulting in a sample of 90 samples. The analysis technique in this study used panel data analysis, coefficient of determination, f-test, t-test with the help of Eviews-12 software. The results of this study indicate that financial distress, firm size, and inventory intensity have a simultaneous effect on tax avoidance. Partially, financial distress has no effect on tax avoidance. Firm size has an effect on tax avoidance and inventory intensity has no effect on tax avoidance.

title: Development of an Iot-Based Automated Plant Monitoring and Watering System Using Two-Input Sugeno Fuzzy Logic
abstract: Manual plant irrigation often leads to inefficient water usage and delayed responses to changing environmental conditions. This study aims to develop and implement an Internet of Things (IoT)-based monitoring and automatic irrigation system using ESP32 and ESP32-CAM. The proposed system continuously monitors air temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and light intensity while simultaneously capturing plant images for remote observation through a web-based interface. A zero-order Sugeno Fuzzy Logic algorithm is employed to determine irrigation duration based on soil moisture and light intensity inputs, enabling adaptive watering decisions according to environmental conditions. Sensor data and captured images are transmitted to a remote server and displayed through a monitoring website for real-time access. Outdoor testing demonstrated that the system was able to continuously monitor environmental parameters, perform adaptive irrigation based on fuzzy inference results, successfully transmit sensor data to the database, and synchronize captured images with the web platform. The experimental results indicate that the proposed system can provide reliable monitoring and automated irrigation functions, supporting the implementation of IoT-based smart agriculture applications.
