title: Mechanical Response and Stability Assessment of Deteriorated Tunnel Linings Under Prescribed Cyclic Stress Changes
abstract: This study investigates how initial material deterioration and repeated stress changes affect the response of lining–rock systems during tunnel reconstruction and expansion. Monotonic uniaxial compression tests on limestone specimens with gypsum linings were monitored using digital image correlation. A corresponding numerical model was compared with the monotonic test response and used for incremental–static cyclic loading simulations. The numerical series examined cyclic stress amplitude, initial lining deterioration and initial surrounding-rock deterioration separately. Higher cyclic stress amplitudes produced greater convergence and more extensive plastic-zone development. The lining plastic-zone fraction increased more markedly between surrounding-rock deterioration levels of 20% and 30% than across the lower sampled levels, indicating a possible transition within the investigated range. Axial work-density changes depended on the parameter series and were not uniformly monotonic. A weighted five-indicator framework with prescribed engineering weights combines convergence, plastic-zone fractions and lining cohesion loss for relative comparison of the simulated cases. The findings identify regions and material conditions that warrant attention when assessing deteriorated linings and planning tunnel reconstruction and expansion.

title: Unified Pressure and Field Response Across Distinct Charge‐Order Regimes in Ti‐Doped CsV 3 Sb 5
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the phase diagram of kagome superconductors from a microscopic perspective is crucial for clarifying the interplay between charge order and superconductivity. Here, we report muon spin rotation () study of Ti‐doped at two representative compositions: underdoped (–CVS) and optimally doped (–CVS), exhibiting long‐range and short‐range charge order, respectively. Using zero‐field and high‐field , we find the presence of spontaneous weak internal magnetic fields in the normal state of both compositions, suggestive of time‐reversal‐symmetry (TRS) breaking. The TRS breaking response is strongly enhanced by an applied magnetic field and associated with long‐range and short‐range charge‐order, respectively. In the superconducting state, both samples exhibit anisotropic nodeless pairing with low superfluid density. Hydrostatic pressure substantially enhances both the superconducting transition temperature and the superfluid density (by 2.5), revealing a linear correlation between them and pointing to unconventional pairing. Above 1 GPa, a crossover from anisotropic to isotropic nodeless pairing is observed. Despite the different nature of charge order in the two doping regimes, the superconducting responses are remarkably similar, suggesting that the competition between superconductivity and charge order occurs on a local scale, largely independent of the long‐ran…

title: How Tumor Immune Neighborhoods May Help Predict Lung Cancer Treatment Response
EZH2 Inhibition Induces a Metabolic Stress Response Sensitizing Triple-Negative Breast Cancer to Glutaminase Targeting
abstract: Abstract EZH2, the catalytic subunit of the histone methyltransferase complex PRC2, is overexpressed and associated with poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Although EZH2 inhibition significantly alters chromatin landscapes and gene expression, it has limited impact on the growth of TNBC models, suggesting adaptive compensatory mechanisms. Here, we demonstrated that EZH2 inhibition causes the accumulation of misfolded proteins and double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), triggering an essential integrated stress response (ISR) through PKR and PERK activation. By inducing ISR-mediated ATF4, EZH2 inhibition enhanced amino acid flux and promoted glutaminolysis to support TNBC cell survival. Pharmacological targeting of this metabolic axis with a glutaminase inhibitor in combination with EZH2 inhibition significantly impaired TNBC cell proliferation and tumor growth. These findings reveal a stress-driven metabolic adaptation that sustains TNBC survival upon EZH2 blockade and highlight inhibition of this pathway as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of EZH2 inhibitors in TNBC.

title: Response of Vestibular Schwannomas in NF2-Related Schwannomatosis (NF2-SWN) to Losartan: A Case Series
abstract: Objective: Identify response rates of vestibular schwannomas in NF2-related Schwanomatosis to treatment with losartan alone or combined with other treatments. Study design: Single-institution retrospective case series. Setting: Tertiary referral center. Patients: Twenty patients with NF2-related Schwannomatosis. Intervention(s): Losartan alone, Losartan plus other therapy (bevacizumab, brigatinib, axitinib). Main outcome measure(s): Volumetric progression, defined as a change in VS size >20%, in accordance with the Response Evaluation in Neurofibromatosis and Schwannomatosis (REiNS) criteria. Audiometric progression is defined as a change in hearing measures, either a 10 dB or greater increase in PTA or a 10% or greater decrease in WRS. Results: This study included 20 patients, with 33 VSs, treated at our institution from 2014 to 2023. Losartan treatment duration ranged from 8.09 to 153.04 months (mean: 53.8, SD: 37.32). Twelve VSs were concurrently managed with antineoplastic therapy. Among 21 VSs treated with losartan alone, volumetric regression, progression, and stability were seen in 23.8%, 47.6%, and 28.6% of tumors, respectively. Among 5 VSs treated with combination losartan and bevacizumab, 40% of tumors regressed, 20% progressed, and 40% remained stable during the combination period. One tumor that progressed during bevacizumab monotherapy treatment achieved volumetric…

title: Monitoring the Response to JAK Inhibitor Treatment in Alopecia Areata Using Reflectance Confocal Microscopy and Videotrichoscopy: A 60-Week Observational Study
Semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models for Separate Forecasting of GDP Growth and Inflation in African Economies
abstract: Reliable forecasts of GDP growth and price dynamics support macroeconomic monitoring and economic planning, particularly in heterogeneous African economies where macroeconomic relationships may vary across economic conditions. This study develops and evaluates separate semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models (Panel GAMs) to examine nonlinear conditional associations and forecast GDP growth and the inverse hyperbolic sine-transformed Consumer Price Index (IHS-CPI). We analyse quarterly panel data for 53 African economies covering 2005Q1–2025Q4. The models represent the effects of exchange rate, money supply, interest rate, and time using smooth functions while accounting for country-specific heterogeneity through country-level random effects. We evaluate out-of-sample forecasting performance against a Linear Mixed Model. The estimated smooth terms provide evidence of statistically significant nonlinear conditional associations for both GDP growth and IHS-CPI. The Panel GAM achieves adjusted R2 values of 0.230 for GDP growth and 0.709 for IHS-CPI, indicating stronger in-sample fit for IHS-CPI. For out-of-sample forecasting, the Panel GAM produces RMSE and MAE values of 3.465 and 2.027 for GDP growth and 1.669 and 1.211 for IHS-CPI, respectively, compared with 3.368 and 1.931 for GDP growth and 1.632 and 1.192 for IHS-CPI from the Linear Mixed Model. Thus, the Panel GAM d…

title: Decoding Gen Z’s Second-hand iPhone Purchases: The Interplay of Price, Brand Image, Quality, and Psychological Factors
abstract: This study aims to analyze the factors influencing Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers’ decisions to purchase second-hand iPhones in Indonesia. Four main variables were examined: price perception, product quality, brand image, and psychological factors, including trust and risk perception. Data were collected from Gen Z respondents who had experience with or were interested in purchasing second-hand iPhones, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The results show that all variables have a positive and significant influence on purchasing decisions, with price perception being the most dominant factor. These findings indicate that Gen Z prioritizes economic value and affordability while still considering device quality and trust in the seller. In addition, Apple’s brand image contributes to purchasing decisions through the symbolic value attached to young consumers’ digital identities. This study confirms that the decision to purchase a second-hand iPhone is influenced not only by rational factors such as price and quality but also by psychological and symbolic factors. These findings have important implications for refurbished-industry players to develop competitive pricing strategies, improve transparency in product quality, and build consumer trust through clear guarantees and information.

title: Pooled Information and Model Flexibility: Decomposing Machine-Learning Gains in Corporate Budgeting and Forecasting
abstract: Corporate financial planning and analysis (FP&A) is being reorganised around machine learning, yet the supporting evidence consists largely of vendor case reports using undefined accuracy measures. This study decomposes the machine-learning advantage into components that prior work bundles together—information recency versus model re-estimation, and pooled estimation versus learner flexibility—measured on corporate income-statement data rather than retail or equity series. An open benchmark from SEC XBRL data covering 2599 non-financial US filers and 118,406 firm-quarters, from 2011 to 2025, evaluates five pre-registered hypotheses under rolling-origin validation with clustered inference. First, the advantage of continuous re-forecasting over annual budgeting derives from information recency rather than parameter updating: supplying current quarterly actuals to a model estimated once at fiscal year start recovers 27 to 58 percent of forecast error, whereas quarterly re-estimation produces no detectable improvement (p = 0.82), a result that holds across the COVID-19 and 2022 inflation regimes. Second, the advantage is an interaction rather than a main effect: a pooled linear model modestly outperforms a Theta benchmark, a flexible learner fitted per firm underperforms it, and a foundation model pooled across unrelated domains underperforms further; only pooling across comparable…
venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: A Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture for Noisy Panel Environments
abstract: Machine learning forecasting systems in noisy, non-stationary, multi-entity environments are commonly optimized for pointwise predictive accuracy, although many downstream decisions depend on the relative ordering of entities rather than exact numerical forecasts. This creates a potential prediction–ranking–decision misalignment, where the model with the lowest forecast error may not generate the most useful ranking or decision outcome. This paper proposes a Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture (LDFA) that separates predictive calibration from decision-oriented transformation. Layers 1 and 2 generate heterogeneous forecasts through base learners, stacking, and adaptive weighting, while the main methodological contribution is Layer 3: a selective post-prediction controller based on source selection, activation gating, veto logic, and regime-aware scaling. LDFA is evaluated using daily data for 30 EGX firms from 2020 to 2025 under a leakage-controlled expanding-window walk-forward protocol. The results show that prediction, ranking, and decision metrics favor different models: the Ridge meta-model provides the strongest target-scale accuracy, the XGBRankerLTR learning-to-rank baseline achieves the strongest ranking information coefficient (IC), and the SoftmaxHybridGate achieves the highest Sharpe ratio. The Layer 3 controller slightly improves over the Ridge backbone …

Determinants of Purchase Intention for Natural Organic Cosmetics: Price, E-Service Quality, Product Quality, and Social Media Marketing
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of selling price, electronic service quality, and producte quality on customer satisfication. It also examines the effects of the product itself and social media marketing on consumers’ purchasing intent for natural based cosmetics products, spesifically Deepmire Skin brand. This study employs a quantitative approach, collecting data through a questionnaire administrated to 171 respondents. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method with the assitance of SmartPLS software. The resulth of this study indicate that selling price has a significant effect on consumers’ purchasing intent toward Deepmire Skin products, with coefficient value of 0,4333 an a p-value of 0,000. In addition, the quality of electronic service also has a positive effect on consumer purchasing intent with a coefficient of 0,283 and a p-value 0,001. Meanwhile, product quality also influences consumer purchasing intent but in a negative direction, with a coefficient of -0,384 and p-value od 0,001. Meanwhile, social media marketing has positive effect on consumer purchasing interest, with a coefficient 0,701 and p-value of 0,000, making it the variable with the greatest influence. These findings indicate that consumer purchasing interest is influenced by price, digital services, product quality, and social media marketing…

title: Biases in near-surface meteorological conditions over Alaska within the HRRR model revealed using observations from the U.S. Climate Reference Network
abstract: Abstract The Arctic atmosphere intricately impacts midlatitude weather and climate across diverse timescales. Thus, an accurate representation of the Arctic and its surrounding regions in numerical weather prediction models is critical across many applications, including fire weather, aviation forecasts, marine forecasts, etc. Doing so requires that models properly simulate near-surface radiation, temperature, and moisture fields. However, knowledge of model performance over the Artic is limited largely due to the paucity of observations. To help close this gap, we used five years of observations obtained from 1 Jan 2021 through 31 Dec 2025 from 22 stations comprising the U.S. Climate Reference Network in Alaska to evaluate how well the 1-h through 48-h forecasts from version 4 of the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) model represent incoming shortwave radiation ( SW d ), surface (i.e., skin) temperature ( T s ), near-surface air temperature ( T a ), and humidity (RH) on interannual, seasonal, and diurnal timescales. We found that the HRRR had a net positive SW d bias but, counterintuitively, had negative T s and T a biases during the summer. In the winter, the T s and T a biases were positive. Overall, the T s and T a biases were smallest from 06 – 15 UTC and largest from 18 – 00 UTC. They were also largest on the subset of days with the largest T a changes and SW d . In cl…

title: PENGARUH PERCEIVED RISK, TRUST, EFFICIENCY, DAN FUNCTIONAL BENEFIT TERHADAP CONTINUANCE INTENTION DAN PRICE SENSITIVITY PADA PENGGUNA M-COMMERCE GENERASI Z DI KOTA BATAM

title: Decadal Wildfire Risk Projection in Guangxi, China, Using a Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework with Recursive Environmental Factor Forecasting
abstract: Multi-year wildfire risk projection requires environmental drivers to be estimated beyond the observational period. This study develops a two-stage framework for Guangxi, China. FactorLSTM recursively estimates nine time-varying environmental factors, and an LSTM–Transformer combines these estimates with four projection-static factors to generate monthly wildfire probability estimates on a 1 km grid for 2019–2028. Observed-driver classification and recursive, predicted-driver evaluation are distinguished. An additional retrospective experiment using a separately trained classifier with a positive-class weight of 10 and Platt calibration yielded a pooled ROC-AUC of 0.7835 and average precision of 0.001475 for available valid observations in 2019–2025. However, its mean predicted probability was approximately 4.50 times the observed positive fraction, indicating residual overestimation. Seasonal maps summarise monthly outputs for January–April, May–September, and October–December. The ten-year outputs are conditional projections under extrapolated environmental drivers and fixed projection-stage land cover. The results identify limitations in probability calibration, rare-event detection, and observation coverage; they do not establish reliable monthly forecasting across the complete ten-year horizon.

title: Differentiated Responses of Major Korean Ports to Macroeconomic Conditions: Container Throughput Forecasting and Management Strategies
abstract: Maritime transport carried 99.7% of Korea's international cargo in 2023, and container throughput at Korean ports moves with economic conditions abroad. This study identifies the macroeconomic indicators that move throughput at Busan Port, Incheon Port, and Gwangyang Port, and carries those indicators into forecasting models built for each port. A common candidate set and selection procedure were applied to the three ports and to their combined total over 120 monthly observations from January 2013 to December 2022, so that differences in the estimates follow from the ports rather than from model specification. Significant variables entered ARIMAX, SARIMAX, LSTM, and Bi-LSTM models as exogenous regressors, trained on 84 months and tested on the 36 months from January 2020. Interaction and squared terms were estimated for the combined total. The base interest rate, the economic growth rate of China, and the SCFI carried negative coefficients for the combined total, Busan Port, and Incheon Port. At Gwangyang Port both Chinese growth and the SCFI carried positive coefficients, and the interest rate did not enter the final model. LSTM produced the lowest RMSE and MAPE at every port, with MAPE between 4.67% and 7.91%. The interaction between the interest rate and Chinese growth was negative, so throughput falls furthest when both run high. Because response directions differ across po…
venue: Journal of Maritime Innovation and Sustainability

title: Spatially-Aware Temperature Forecasting using Graph Attention and Temporal Convolution Networks
abstract: Accurate local temperature forecasting is difficultin topographically complex regions such as Nepal, where atmosphericbehavior is governed by strong spatiotemporal dependenciesthat conventional statistical and deep learning models fail tofully capture. In this study, a new Graph Attention Network-Temporal Convolutional Network (GAT-TCN) model is proposedfor multi-step temperature forecasting over Bagmati Province,Nepal. A 3×3 grid of ERA5 reanalysis data is encoded as aspatial graph, where a GAT learns heterogeneous dependenciesamong neighboring grid points while a TCN captures temporaldynamics from a 24-hour historical window using causal, dilatedconvolutions. Spatial and temporal representations are combinedthrough a late-fusion strategy, and 14-day forecasts are generatedautoregressively. Experimental results show that the proposedlate-fusion GAT-TCN model outperforms GAT, TCN, GCNLSTM,GAT-LSTM, and an early-fusion GAT-TCN variant,achieving an R2 of 0.944 and MAE of 0.149°C on Day 1,degrading gracefully to R2 of 0.768 at Day 14. Transfer learningexperiments using a progressive layer-unfreezing strategy furthershow that the pretrained model adapts effectively to mountainand Terai regions, confirming the generalizability of the proposedspatiotemporal framework.
venue: Proceedings of International Conference on Innovation in Computing, Science, Engineering and Technology

title: Adaptive Modality Routing for Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting with Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: Temporal knowledge graph forecasting aims to predict future missing facts from continuously evolving relational data in dynamic information systems. Such forecasting tasks are increasingly important for intelligent applications involving complex interactions among entities, events, and evolving environments. Existing approaches typically employ unified architectures that process all queries through the same representation pipeline, despite substantial variations in structural connectivity, historical availability, and semantic information among different queries. Such a homogeneous modeling strategy may limit the ability to effectively handle diverse forecasting scenarios, including highly connected entities, recurrent temporal patterns, and cold-start cases with insufficient historical evidence. To address this challenge, we propose a Heterogeneous Modality Mixture-of-Experts (H-MoE) framework that adaptively selects specialized reasoning pathways according to query characteristics. Unlike conventional mixture-of-experts architectures with homogeneous subnetworks, our framework incorporates three complementary experts with distinct inductive biases: a time-aware graph neural network for structural relational reasoning, a temporal transformer for historical sequence modeling, and a semantic representation adapter based on pretrained language models for knowledge transfer in spa…

title: Development of an integrated heat strain index for personalized assessment and forecasting
Forecasting Fluctuations in Bioclimatic Humidification Zones Under Climate Change Conditions
abstract: Understanding potential bioclimate changes is key to developing effective adaptation measures. Using integrated GIS, Selyaninov’s hydrothermal coefficient (HTC), and model data from the CORDEX project, the study examined fluctuations in various humidification biozones in southern Russia under representative RCP 2.6 and RCP 8.5 scenarios for the period 2021–2100. Scenario analysis based on the MOHC-HadGEM2-ES (GERICS-REMO2015) combination revealed heterogeneous responses of bioclimatic conditions. At RCP 2.6, the total humidification level will increase and reach a maximum in the period 2071–2080, when the semi-desert and desert biozone will not appear, and the zone of deciduous forests will expand to the north–west of the region and cover an area of 150.715 thousand km2. At RCP 8.5, the humidification level will decrease, which will lead to the dominance of the biozones of the dry steppe, semi-desert and desert. As a result, by 2100, the arid biozones will cover approximately 546.739 thousand km2 or 92.5% of the region’s territory. According to the resulting models, the areas of biozones are significantly dependent on fluctuations in temperature and precipitation, and these factors explain up to 82.7% of their variability. The methodological approach presented can be applied to assess the dynamics of bioclimatic humidification zones in other regions of the world.

title: Aerial Phenotyping of Coffee Flowering Using Deep Learning for Early Yield Prediction
abstract: Early yield estimation is important for improving decision-making and management practices in coffee production systems. However, approaches that use aerial imagery to characterize flowering and relate it to subsequent yield remain limited. This study evaluated the potential of RGB imagery acquired by remotely piloted aircraft (RPA) combined with Deep Learning techniques to classify coffee plants according to three levels of a flowering proxy and to investigate its relationship with yield. A dataset comprising 1593 segmented RGB images was classified into Low, Medium, and High flowering levels using a custom convolutional neural network and three transfer learning architectures: VGG16, ResNet50V2, and MobileNetV2. ResNet50V2 was selected for final evaluation based on its validation performance and achieved 92.12% accuracy, 92.40% macro-precision, 91.81% macro-recall, and 92.06% macro-F1 on the test dataset. The flowering proxy showed a positive association with field-observed yield, with Spearman’s ρ = 0.701 (p < 0.001) and R2 = 0.528 for the combined dataset of Arara and Mundo Novo. In consolidated out-of-sample predictions, the model achieved R2 = 0.489, MAE = 1.03 kg plant−1, and RMSE = 1.18 kg plant−1. Performance differed between cultivars, with consolidated R2 values of 0.567 for Arara and 0.329 for Mundo Novo. Spatial analysis also showed correspondence between the distr…

title: A Generalized Analytical Framework for Prediction of Self-Excited Backward Whirl in Geometrically Nonlinear Rotor/Stator Rubbing Systems
abstract: Traditional analytical models for dry friction backward whirl predominantly rely on linear shaft assumptions, failing to capture amplitude-dependent frequency shifts and nonlinear response dynamics. For the geometrically nonlinear rotor/stator rubbing systems characterized by isotropic, smooth odd-polynomial restoring forces with arbitrary truncation orders, a generalized analytical framework for prediction of self-excited backward whirl is presented in this paper. By expanding the restoring force via a Taylor series with an arbitrary truncation order, a response decomposition strategy is established to treat the steady-state response as a superposition of a synchronous forced forward response and a self-excited backward whirl. A harmonic balance procedure is subsequently employed to decouple these components, yielding closed-form analytical solutions for both stability thresholds and orbital topologies. With the aid of numerical simulations, the proposed framework is validated across multiple degrees of nonlinearity, demonstrating excellent agreement with low root-mean-square errors when the relative sliding duration ratio exceeds 0.7. Crucially, compared with traditional linear rotors, geometric nonlinearity introduces a strong stiffness-hardening effect, resulting in reduced, self-limiting whirl amplitudes and pronounced upward frequency shifts. Furthermore, the instability …

title: Engineering Data Analysis Beyond Statistics vs. Machine Learning: A Review of Explanation, Prediction, Hybrid Modeling, and Responsible Decision Support
abstract: This structured narrative review explores how engineers select and evaluate traditional statistical, machine learning, mechanistic, and hybrid methods for explanation, prediction, and responsible decision support. We identified representative literature available through 2025 via iterative searches of Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, and conducted a thematic synthesis. We qualitatively assessed the credibility and relevance of the literature sources. Application areas covered include manufacturing, semiconductor processing, mechanical and materials systems, civil infrastructure, chemical processes, energy and construction, robotics, and greenhouse engineering (excluding healthcare). Comparisons included analytical objectives, data characteristics, hypotheses, interpretability, uncertainty, causality, physical consistency, validation, and deployment. The synthesis yielded three recurring conclusions. First, a method’s applicability depends on information content, dependency structure, operating conditions, and decision consequences, not dataset size or method labels. Second, statistical significance and predictive accuracy do not independently demonstrate causal validity, physical plausibility, or operational effectiveness. Reliable evaluation combines internal validation, feasible external testing, repeatable benchmarking against meaningful benchmarks,…

title: Exploring SPI-Based Machine Learning and Statistical Models for Drought Prediction in Southeastern Romania
abstract: This study analyzes the performance of several forecasting models applied to Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) time series for the 1967–2021 period, using data from six weather stations in southeastern Romania. Four temporal aggregation scales (SPI3, SPI6, SPI12, and SPI24) were considered for one-step-ahead (one-month) forecasting. The evaluated models included Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Regression (SVR), N-BEATS (generic variant), and SARIMA (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average), covering machine learning, deep learning, and statistical approaches. To ensure a rigorous out-of-sample evaluation, SPI distribution parameters were estimated solely based on the pre-test calibration period and held constant when calculating SPI values for the independent test period, thereby preventing information leakage from the preprocessing stage. Forecast performance was assessed using RMSE, MAE, NSE, and a skill score relative to a persistence benchmark, while differences in forecast accuracy were statistically evaluated using the Diebold–Mariano test. The results revealed a clear scale-dependent pattern: absolute forecast accuracy increased with the SPI aggregation scale—alongside more pronounced temporal persistence—though this did not necessarily translate into superior skill compared to the persistence model. Among the data-driven models, SVR demonstrated th…

title: Machine Learning for Screening Bioactive Compounds in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Computational Prediction, Multi-Omics Integration, and Clinical Translation Potential
abstract: Identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) requires computational prioritization to be connected with chemical and pharmacological evidence. This structured narrative and critical review examines machine learning applications in compound prediction, formula-compatibility analysis, multi-omics integration, and drug development and repurposing. Molecular fingerprints, graph and sequence representations, knowledge graphs, and generative models are discussed in relation to their intended endpoints and validation conditions. Studies are classified along two independent dimensions: application scope, distinguishing direct TCM applications from natural-product studies and general drug-discovery methods, and validation level, ranging from computational prediction to chemical, experimental, and clinical evidence. Three case analyses illustrate a TCM-specific graph-learning platform with chemical confirmation, a downstream animal and metabolomics study without machine learning screening, and a proposed causal framework assembled from separate studies. Across these applications, machine learning supports candidate ranking and hypothesis generation, but predicted targets, attention weights, and multi-omics associations do not independently establish target engagement, formula synergy, or therapeutic efficacy. Major limitations include chemical-domain shift, incon…

title: Development of a high-temperature asphalt pavement temperature prediction model for performance grade zoning in Thailand
A Two-Stage Prediction Strategy for Primary Hyperparathyroidism
abstract: Background: Primary hyperparathyroidism parathyroid hormone (PTH) hypersecretion is difficult to recognise when calcium is normal and difficult to distinguish from secondary hyperparathyroidism once PTH is found to be elevated. These are separate problems arising at separate points in care. We developed and evaluated two interpretable models corresponding to these decision points using an internal–external validation design. Methods: We analysed 2788 adults undergoing PTH testing across three campuses of one hospital (development n = 1843; internal–external validation n = 445 and n = 500); those with an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded. PHPT was adjudicated in 504 (18.1%) by two endocrinologists using biochemistry, imaging and histopathology. Model 1, for use before PTH is measured, comprised total calcium, ln(alkaline phosphatase) and age. Model 2, developed in the Main campus subgroup with PTH above the reference limit (>65 pg/mL, n = 429 of 623), comprised ln(PTH), total calcium and phosphate. Results: Model 1 achieved AUCs of 0.920 in the development cohort and 0.882–0.908 in the validation cohorts; because serum calcium contributed to the outcome definition, these estimates reflect agreement with the reference standard rather than independent diagnostic accuracy. Among participants with elevated PTH, Model 2 achieved an AUC of 0.90…

title: Data-Driven State-Space Identification with Correlated Fuzzy Parametric Uncertainty for Prediction and Integral Control
abstract: Data-driven models for embedded control must account for acquisition filtering and experimental uncertainty while retaining dependence among identified parameters. This work develops a framework connecting identification in filtered-state coordinates, joint fuzzy uncertainty propagation, and fixed-gain stability assessment. A structured affine discrete-time model is refined through finite-horizon prediction error, and complete bootstrap deviations define a joint radial parameter family. Set inclusion ensures nested prediction envelopes, while endpoint quadratic inequalities certify stability over continuous parameter segments. Evaluation uses 30 identification runs and a main campaign of 60 physical closed-loop trials on a DC motor (30 per controller), complemented by two further campaigns of ten trials per controller: one with an inserted series resistor and one with a sinusoidal reference. Separate calibration and testing quantify predictive coverage and interval width, while marginal-preserving permutation demonstrates the influence of parameter pairing on prediction bands and sampled stability. All 435 retained training families receive continuous stability certificates. Quantitative comparisons with N4SID, SUBNET, and a TSK fuzzy predictor identify complementary predictive strengths, and nominal versus guaranteed-cost control evaluations characterize the trade-off between …

title: Mapping of Land Cover and Prediction and Simulation on the Evolution of the Density of Afzelia Africana (Fabaceae) According to Anthropogenic Activities in the Bénoué National Park (North-Cameroon)
abstract: Afzelia africana (Fabaceae) is an endangered ligneous species which is becoming rare in northern Cameroon due to overexploitation in unprotected natural environments. This leads to its overexploitation in the Benoue National Park by various types of actors. This work aims at predicting the evolution of its densities according to anthropic activities and simulating the evolution of its densities in the Benoue National Park (North-Cameroon). The modeling of the evolution of the densities according to the anthropogenic activities showed that pruning and late fires would been at the origin of the extinction of this species while the calculated annual regression rate was 2.33%, showing that it may disappear in the 2040s. This stresses the necessity to raise awareness on the protection and restoration of this important plant species.
venue: Global Research in Environment and Sustainability

title: Stochastic Mirror-Prox Optimisation of Group Distributionally Robust Multimodal Logistic Regression for Multilingual Fact-Checking Verdict Prediction
abstract: This paper asks whether group distributionally robust optimisation raises the worst-group macro-F1 of a block-masked multimodal logistic regression with availability indicators for multilingual fact-checking. Stochastic Mirror-Prox solves the resulting convex–concave saddle-point problem. The corpus pools 49,584 X-Fact and MediaEval records with 90 language labels. On the in-domain split, the robust solution lifts worst-group macro-F1 from 0.313 under pooled empirical risk minimisation to 0.401 (95% interval of the gain [0.025,0.134]). Overall macro-F1 drops by 0.040, and dispersion of balanced accuracy across languages falls from 0.166 to 0.131. The gain lies in X-Fact claim groups and the cost in MediaEval posts (macro-F1 0.887 to 0.809). Removing the availability indicators moves no worst-group or overall macro-F1 by more than 0.007. The worst-group difference is negative on unseen languages and not resolved on unseen sites or events. A Friedman test detects no difference between solvers in typical group performance. At equal numbers of sampled records, stochastic mirror descent reaches a smaller mean duality gap than Mirror-Prox at each measured mini-batch size from 2 to 128. On this instance, extrapolation does not repay its second call.

title: Conocimiento sobre modelización matemática manifestado por maestros de primaria en ejercicio
abstract: We describe the professional knowledge of mathematical modelling stated by eleven in-service primary school teachers. Particularly, the study focuses on the knowledge of the notion of a modelling problem, its resolution, and the disposition. Based on interviews, the results show that teachers recognize some elements of mathematical modelling but display a limited understanding of the process as a dynamic cycle and of the strategic decisions involved. This knowledge is grounded in prior knowledge but is shaped by general pedagogical training, which limits the integration of mathematical modelling in classroom practice and highlights the need for professional development initiatives centered on exploration and reflective teaching.

Mobility and Logistics as a Service for Healthcare (MLaaS4H): Transport Planning Processes for Enhancing Sustainable People Mobility to Healthcare Facilities
abstract: Rapid urbanisation poses increasingly complex sustainability challenges, while transport systems remain essential for enabling people and businesses to conduct daily activities and access critical services. This study investigates the interactions between passenger and freight mobility and the healthcare sector and proposes Mobility and Logistics as a Service for Healthcare (MLaaS4H), an integrated framework for the sustainable planning of healthcare-related mobility and logistics. The framework aims to support decision-making and service design by combining advanced transport system models (TSMs) with emerging information and communication technologies (e-ICTs), thereby improving accessibility to healthcare facilities and the efficiency of service provision. The proposed planning process comprises two complementary paths. The external path connects the spatial, temporal, and deepening dimensions of transport and healthcare planning, whereas the internal path adopts the Logical Framework Approach (LFA) to establish a transparent causal chain linking invested resources, implemented activities, outputs, outcomes, and long-term goals. Indicators associated with each component are connected through exogenous and endogenous functions, enabling quantitative assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of MLaaS4H solutions. An illustrative case study demonstrates how coordinated hea…

title: Assessing Automotive Graduates’ Readiness and Skills Gaps for Electric Vehicle Repair and Maintenance: Evidence from Automotive Service Garages in Kumasi, Ghana
abstract: Ghana’s automotive sector has significant opportunities for the transition from Internal Combustion (IC) to electric vehicles. Current training remains largely IC-engine focused. TVET programmes, apprenticeship training, and automotive education curricula must align with emerging EV technologies and evolving workforce needs. This study aimed to assess automotive graduates’ preparedness for electric vehicle (EV) repair and maintenance in Kumasi, Ghana, identify critical competency gaps, and determine priorities for strengthening workforce readiness. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among automotive engineering graduates, technicians, industry professionals, and academic staff in Kumasi, Ghana, using a multi-stage stratified sampling approach. A total of 753 eligible respondents provided usable responses to the structured online questionnaire. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistical techniques, and all statistical analyses were performed in R version 4.3.2 and IBM SPSS Statistics version 20. The study revealed a substantial competency gap in EV knowledge, technical skills, and practical competencies, with 51.1% of respondents lacking knowledge in EV fault diagnosis. The findings underscore the need to prioritize periodic practical EV repair and maintenance training, industry internships and apprenticeships, and stronger collaboration between industr…

title: Antibiorésistance des Enterobacteriaceae Isolées dans l’Environnement du Service d’Endocrinologie-Diabétologie et Centre National de l’Obésité de l’Hôpital Central de Yaoundé
abstract: Introduction : Les surfaces et les eaux usées hospitalières sont colonisées par les Entérobactéries potentiellement pathogènes. L’objectif cette étude était de déterminer le profil de résistance aux antibiotiques des Enterobactériaceae isolées dans l’environnement du Service d’Endocrinologie-Diabétologie et Centre National de l’obésité de l’Hôpital Central de Yaoundé. Matériel et Méthode : Il s’agissait d’une étude transversale, réalisée d’avril à juin 2025 au Service d’Endocrinologie-Diabétologie et Centre National de l’Obésité de l’Hôpital Central de Yaoundé. Les prélèvements de surfaces ont été effectués à l’aide d’écouvillons stériles humidifiés avec de l’eau stérile et les eaux usées dans les flacons en verre stérile de 300 ml. Les bactéries isolées ont été identifiées selon les méthodes de bactériologie, la sensibilité aux antibiotiques a été étudiée selon la méthode de Kirby-Bauer. Résultats : Sur 61 prélèvements effectués, 22 (36,1%) étaient positifs et 38 Entérobactéries ont été isolées. Les échantillons les plus souillés provenaient : du lavabo 7/7 (100%), du plateau de soin 1/4(25,0%), et des armoires 2/9 (22,20%). L’étude du profil de résistance a permis d’observer un taux élevé de résistance des entérobactéries vis-à-vis de certaines bêta-lactamines : amoxicilline acide-clavulanique 68,4%, ampicilline 67,9% et sulfamide (triméthoprime-sulfaméthoxazole 66,7%). Par c…

title: Emotional Experiences in Public Service: a Study of Emotions on Informal Learning in the Workplace
abstract: This interpretative qualitative study analyzes how Informal Learning in the workplace can be shaped by the emotions of technical-administrative staff at a public state university faculty in São Paulo. The study draws on a socioconstructionist approach to emotions and Bente Elkjaer’s Pragmatic Theory of Learning, which conceptualizes the organization as an emotional arena in which tensions and conflicts may either facilitate or hinder learning. In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 staff members. The findings indicate that, although emotions arise from social practices, they are still perceived as undesirable interference in learning and work. The study contributes to highlighting the centrality of emotional experiences for understanding organizations, work relationships, learning, and the construction of organizational identity.
venue_publisher: Sindicato das Secretárias do Estado de São Paulo

title: Ubiquitination-Dependent Cyclin Regulation in Gastric Cancer and Emerging Targeted Therapies with Chinese Herbal Bioactive Compounds
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, with a high mortality rate primarily attributable to late-stage diagnosis and limited therapeutic options. Aberrant cell proliferation arising from cell cycle dysregulation is a hallmark of GC pathogenesis. Cyclins, as core regulators of cell cycle progression, exhibit dynamic protein expression patterns that are tightly controlled by the ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS). In GC, cyclins are frequently overexpressed due to impaired ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation. This review systematically elucidates the ubiquitination-mediated regulation of distinct cyclins (Cyclins D, E, A, and B) at specific cell cycle phases—G1, S, G2, and M—and highlights the critical roles of E3 ubiquitin ligases, including SCF complexes and APC/C, in GC progression. We further discuss how dysregulated non-coding RNAs and altered E3 ligase expression contribute to aberrant cyclin ubiquitination, thereby promoting GC cell proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. Importantly, emerging evidence demonstrates that bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can counteract these abnormalities by directly downregulating cyclin expression, modulating E3 ligase activity, or inhibiting 26S/20S proteasome function, thus restoring cell cycle homeostasis and suppressing GC growth. This rev…

title: Positive reappraisal and refocus on planning as cognitive emotion-regulation correlates of psychological resilience: a cross-sectional observational study
Cross-regulation of iron and phosphate homeostasis by Fep1 and Pho7 in fission yeast
abstract: ABSTRACT Iron and phosphate are essential micronutrients with partially interconnected homeostatic control; however, the underlying transcriptional mechanisms that integrate these signals in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe remain unclear. Fep1 (GATA-type repressor) is a key regulator of iron-uptake genes, whereas Pho7 (Zn 2 Cys 6 -family transcription factor) drives phosphate starvation response. However, whether each of the two factors influences the target regulon controlled by the other remains unclear. We combined genome-wide chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, RNA sequencing, and auxin-inducible degron-mediated acute depletion to define the joint Fep1–Pho7 transcriptional control and regulatory landscapes under defined iron and phosphate conditions. Unexpectedly, these analyses showed extensive overlap in chromatin occupancy between Fep1 and Pho7 at a subset of target promoters. Fep1 bound not only to canonical iron-uptake genes but also to the pho7+ locus and multiple phosphate-responsive promoters, whereas Pho7 showed association with a defined subset of Fep1 targets. Acute depletion experiments showed that Fep1 loss substantially increased Pho7 chromatin occupancy at iron-responsive promoters. Under iron-depleted conditions, Pho7 contributed to the transcriptional activation of specific Fep1 target genes ( fio1+/fip1 + and str3+ ), which indicated that…

title: Emotion Regulation and Brain Mechanisms: A Transdiagnostic Perspective on Neural Circuits, Individual Differences, and Clinical Translation
abstract: Emotion regulation (ER) difficulties are now firmly established as a transdiagnostic feature of psychiatric and stress-related disorders. Large-scale meta-analyses published in 2026 confirmed ER impairments across fifteen diagnostic categories, shifting the key question from whether ER is transdiagnostic to how this knowledge can inform diagnosis and treatment. This Perspective argues that ER should be conceptualized as a transdiagnostic neurocognitive dimension rather than a disorder-specific deficit. To support this view, three complementary studies are integrated: neuroimaging studies of prefrontal-limbic and large-scale brain networks involved in cognitive reappraisal; evidence of ER-related neural alterations across mood, anxiety, trauma-related, personality, and addictive disorders; and research on individual differences and neuromodulation that explain variability in regulatory capacity and treatment response. ER is framed within a broader executive-function model, operating as a “hot” executive process alongside “cool” cognitive-control functions. Building on this evidence, a Layered Transdiagnostic Model of Emotion Regulation (LTM-ER) is proposed. The model includes a shared transdiagnostic core circuit (Layer 1), disorder-specific neural signatures (Layer 2), and individual moderators such as developmental history, dispositional traits, regulatory strategies, and stim…

title: Reticulocalbin-2 (RCN2) as a Context-Dependent CREC-Family Modulator: Gene Expression and Regulation, Molecular Biology, Disease Relevance, and Translational Challenges
abstract: Reticulocalbin-2 (RCN2), encoded by the human RCN2 gene (HGNC:9935) and historically identified as E6-binding protein, is a CREC-family EF-hand Ca2+-binding protein. Although first characterized as an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated protein, current evidence extends RCN2 biology to splice-variant and localization complexity, protein interactions, regulatory and signaling networks, extracellular activity, cancer, non-malignant disease, and the RCN2-derived hormone Raptin. This review synthesizes the fragmented and methodologically uneven RCN2 literature within an evidence-stratified framework. Mechanistic evidence, including direct biochemical assays and RCN2-directed functional studies, supports selected interaction and signaling relationships, whereas omics, database-derived and single-context observations remain hypothesis-generating. Across disease settings, RCN2 is best interpreted as a context-dependent modulator rather than a uniform oncogenic driver, validated biomarker or established therapeutic target. Translational progress will require molecular-form-specific assays, disease-specific validation and clinically grounded models.

title: Frequency of reasons of plate removal following maxillofacial trauma in patients presenting to Ayub Teaching Hospital Abbotabad.
abstract: Objective: To find out the incidence and causes of plate removal in cases of maxillofacial trauma at a tertiary healthcare facility. Study Design: Cross-sectional study. Setting: Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Ayub Teaching Hospital, Abbottabad. Period: October 2025-March 2026. Methods: A total of 133 patients having undergone ORIF surgery for maxillofacial fractures and who later needed plates to be removed were selected by non-probability consecutive sampling. Information related to demographic characteristics, location of fractures, and causes of plate removal was collected on a predesigned questionnaire. SPSS version 26 was used for data analysis. Results: A total of 133 subjects were contained in the study; of these subjects, 97 (i.e., 72.9%) were males and 36 (i.e., 27.1%) were females. The maxilla was the most common fracture location (53.4%). 46 (i.e., 34.6%) patients had surgical site infections as the rationale for removing the plate implant. Plate exposure (27 patients; 20.3%), pain or discomfort due to the implant (19; 14.3%), mechanical failure of the implant (15; 11.3%), and the desire for reconstructive surgery (7; 5.3%) were additional reasons for removal of the implants. No statistical association was found between the indication for plate removal and the patient's gender (p=0.110), age category (p=0.505), or the fracture's location (p=0.523). Co…

title: Cross-frequency stochastic gravitational-wave background anisotropy from compact topology: CMB B -mode covariance as a transfer probe
Dual-frequency profiler study of hydrometeor fall speeds in tropical deep convection
abstract: This study investigates hydrometeor fall speeds using a dual-frequency profiling radar operating during the 2005–2006 monsoon season near Darwin, Australia. Our focus is on tropical deep convection where the observations provide a new perspective on hydrometeor fall speeds within and near intense drafts having mixed-phase media. The techniques we employ avoid undue assumptions on the air motion or media distributions, offering a convenient path to estimate bulk radar reflectivity( Z )-weighted hydrometeor fall speed ( V t ). While these mixed-phase media estimates are not specific to size or density, they may be replicated by models and are practical for radar-based retrievals that necessitate V t assumptions. Tests performed under rain and snow conditions show comparable performance to disdrometer and other references. The standard deviation of residuals for rain and snow relationships are ≅1 and ≅0.4 m s −1 , respectively. In convective core regions aloft, Darwin observations align with existing graupel V t - Z treatments, however mixed-phase media typically falls faster (>1–2 m s −1 ) for Z <35 dBZ than prior relationships. Breakdowns suggest that Active and Break monsoon conditions favor a similar V t - Z behavior in strong cores. However, Break conditions – those more favorable to intense daytime tropical convection – potentially indicate the presence of additional lofted …

title: Effects of velocity-based and traditional resistance training on physical performance, anaerobic capacity, and perceptual responses in trained male football players
abstract: Abstract Background Velocity-based resistance training (VBRT) has emerged as a prominent method for optimizing neuromuscular adaptations by accommodating daily fluctuations in athlete performance. Despite its growing popularity, comparative evidence on VBRT versus traditional resistance training (TRT) across multiple performance and perceptual outcomes in trained football players remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the effects of two 8-week, strength-focused resistance-training programs, VBRT and TRT, on explosive performance, anaerobic capacity, balance, football-specific performance, and perceptual responses in trained male football players. Methods Sixteen trained male football players (age: 19.60 ± 1.26 years; height: 174.75 ± 5.49 cm; weight: 73.49 ± 5.24 kg; body mass index (BMI): 24.09 ± 2.35 kg/m²; training age: 10.10 ± 1.37 years) were randomly assigned to a VBRT group ( n = 8) or a TRT group ( n = 8). Both groups completed two resistance training sessions per week for 8 weeks. Performance assessments, including vertical jump (VJ), running anaerobic sprint test (RAST), 30-m sprint, T-change of direction (T-CoD), balance, ball speed, and perceptual measures (rating of perceived exertion (RPE), visual analogue scale (VAS)), were conducted before and after the intervention under standardized conditions. Beyond Perceived Barriers: Human Capacity and Technological Readiness in Sustainable Construction Adoption in Jordan
abstract: Sustainable construction adoption in developing economies is often discussed in terms of financial, regulatory, and institutional barriers, while the organizational capabilities required for implementation have received less attention. This study examines the associations between key organizational and external factors and the adoption of sustainable construction practices in Jordan using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework. Data were collected through a cross-sectional questionnaire completed by 192 contractors, consultants, developers, and other construction professionals. Financial Barriers, Economic Support, Regulatory Support, Human Capacity, and Technological Readiness were modeled as antecedents of adoption, while Perceived Sustainability Value (PSV) was modeled as the outcome. Human Capacity (β = 0.273, p = 0.001) and Technological Readiness (β = 0.300, p = 0.002) were positively associated with adoption, whereas Financial Barriers, Economic Support, and Regulatory Support were not statistically significant in the full model. Adoption was positively associated with PSV (β = 0.563, p < 0.001). The model accounted for 44.5% and 31.7% of the variance in adoption and PSV, respectively. The findings distinguish between barriers identified by practitioners as important and organizational capa…

title: Effects of Protein Levels of Diets and Yeast Culture Supplementation on Performance, Antioxidant Capacity, and Intestinal Health in Laying Hens
abstract: Yeast culture (YC) can improve laying hen performance, but whether this effect depends on dietary protein level remains unclear. This experiment investigated the effects of adding YC to diets with different protein levels on the performance and intestinal health of laying hens. A total of 504 Lohmann pink laying hens aged 55 weeks were selected and randomly assigned to 4 treatments, with 7 replicates per treatment and 18 hens per replicate. A 2 × 2 factorial design was used, with two CP levels of 15.5% (NP) and 14.5% (LCP), and two YC supplementation levels of 0% and 1%. The feeding trial lasted 12 weeks. YC significantly increased the laying rate (p < 0.05). CP and YC interacted to affect the laying rate (p < 0.05). YC significantly increased serum CAT and GSH-Px activities, reduced PCO, and increased trypsin activity (p < 0.05). CP and YC interacted to affect GSH-Px and trypsin activities (p < 0.05). GSH-Px and trypsin activities were significantly higher in the LCP-YC group than in the LCP-0 group (p < 0.05). YC significantly increased jejunal villus height (VH) (p < 0.05). A significant CP × YC interaction was observed for jejunal VH; supplementing the LCP diet with YC significantly increased VH (p < 0.05). YC significantly increased the percentage of goblet cells in the jejunum, the contents of IgG and IgM in the jejunal mucosa, and decreased TNF-α content (p < 0.05). IFN-…

title: Mechanism study of STOML2 regulating hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation, invasion, and migration by activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate the expression characteristics of STOML2 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) at mRNA, protein and subcellular localization levels, clarify its correlation with immune microenvironment, single-cell expression profile, drug resistance and prognosis, and verify its biological functions and mechanism in regulating HCC cell proliferation, invasion, migration and apoptosis via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Method Bioinformatic analyses were performed using TCGA, CPTAC, HPA, TIMER2.0, TISCH and GEPIA2 databases to explore STOML2 expression, prognosis, immune infiltration, single-cell distribution and related signaling pathways. HCCLM3 cells with high STOML2 expression were selected to construct the siRNA-mediated knockdown model. CCK-8, Transwell, scratch assay, flow cytometry and Western blot were used to detect cell phenotypes and pathway protein changes. Result STOML2 was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues at mRNA and protein levels, with strong positive staining in HCC and moderate expression in normal liver tissues by HPA analysis. Paired sample analysis confirmed significantly higher STOML2 expression in HCC than in adjacent non-cancerous tissues (P < 0.001). High STOML2 expression predicted shorter overall survival (HR = 1.67, P < 0.05) and showed moderate prognostic value for 1‑year survival (AUC = 0.690). STOML2 was mainly enriched in mal…

Post-Operative Rehabilitation after Extensor Mechanism Tendon Repair in Cameroon: A Case of Three Reference Hospitals
abstract: Introduction: Postoperative management following knee tendon repair is a delicate undertaking, precisely because it typically involves patients who, until shortly before surgery, enjoyed satisfactory or even perfect function. This analysis focuses on a study conducted across three major hospitals in Douala and Yaoundé, examining the sociodemographic aspects of care provided by surgeons and physiotherapists, as well as patient self-management. Materials and methods: We conducted a multicenter cohort study spanning 10 years of retrospective data, completed with prospective information gathered via live telephone interviews, in three reference hospitals across Yaoundé and Douala. Results: The findings reveal a significant fragmentation in care delivery, with surgeons providing primary oversight of physiotherapy in 56.25% of cases, while dedicated physiotherapists were involved in only 34.38% of cases. This "surgeon-led" model suggests a systemic gap in specialized rehabilitation infrastructure or workforce distribution in Douala and Yaoundé. There is a clear pattern: patients who received physiotherapy from a surgeon or a professional physiotherapist had substantially better outcomes than those who engaged in self-conducted rehabilitation. Surgeon-led physiotherapy: 13 out of 18 (72%) achieved exceptional recovery. Professional physiotherapist: 8 out of 11 (73%) achieved exception…

title: Spatial Metabolomics-Based Integrated Analysis Provides Evidence for the Mechanism of Salvianolic Acid A-Induced Mitochondrial Apoptosis in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer via the ROS-Dependent Caspase Pathway
abstract: Salvianolic acid A (SAA) exhibits antitumor activity against non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the metabolic regulatory mechanisms underlying its effects remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI), network pharmacology, molecular docking, and functional validation to investigate the effects of SAA on NSCLC. SAA inhibited H1299 cell viability, migration, and invasion and induced apoptosis. DESI-MSI analysis of xenograft tumor tissues revealed marked metabolic alterations after SAA treatment, including changes in ceramides, glycerophospholipids, and arachidonic acid candidates. Network pharmacology and molecular docking further suggested the involvement of oxidative stress- and apoptosis-related pathways. Functionally, SAA increased intracellular ROS levels, impaired mitochondrial function, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. Treatment with the ROS scavenger NAC partially reversed SAA-induced ROS accumulation, loss of cell viability, and increased levels of cleaved Caspase-9 and Caspase-3. Consistently, Western blotting and immunofluorescence analyses showed concentration-dependent activation of Caspase-9 and Caspase-3, whereas the pan-caspase inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK significantly attenuated SAA-induced cell death and apoptosis. Collectively, these findings provide evidence that …

abstract: Abstract Repeated sliding disturbs the slope structure and degrades soil mechanical properties, promoting the progressive development of retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Plateau, China. These landslides progressively encroach upon the plateau surface and have caused substantial casualties and property losses. Field investigations revealed that two subsequent retrogressive failures caused the landslide crown to retreat by approximately 8 and 7 m, respectively, suggesting that the near-crown zone formed after the initial failure underwent sustained disturbance and structural readjustment. Accordingly, undisturbed loess samples were collected from a sliding-disturbed zone approximately 5 m from the current crown (No.1) and a relatively undisturbed zone approximately 50 m from the crown (No.2). Consolidated undrained triaxial tests, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) infiltration tests, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses were conducted to systematically compare the strength, water-migration characteristics, and microstructural damage of the soils from the two zones, thereby elucidating the triggering mechanism of retrogressive landslides. The results indicate that: (1) The soil in the sliding-disturbed zone exhibited pronounced mechanical weakening. Under natural conditions, the average shear strength of No. 1 was approximately 20% lower than that of …

title: Environmental Regulation, Green Total Factor Productivity and Sustainable Development in China’s Border Areas: Heterogeneous Effects and Mechanism Analysis
abstract: Border regions are China’s key ecological security barriers, yet their green transition remains poorly understood because existing studies focus mainly on developed coastal and inland areas. Whether uniform national environmental regulation can achieve effects in border regions comparable to those observed in coastal and inland regions, where resource-dependent industries and structural constraints prevail, has not been systematically examined. Using provincial panel data of 30 Chinese provinces from 2006 to 2022, this study constructs an improved two-stage dynamic SBM-DDF model with differentiated pollutant damage weights to measure green total factor productivity (GTFP), and combines panel Tobit regression, structural moderating effect analysis, and subsystem mechanism decomposition to examine the heterogeneous effects of environmental regulation on green development across coastal, inland, and border regions, as well as the underlying mechanisms. The results indicate that the associations between environmental regulation and green development differ substantially across regions. Command-and-control regulation is positively associated with GTFP in coastal regions but negatively associated with GTFP in inland regions, and the border–coastal difference in this coefficient is statistically significant. Market-based regulation is significantly and negatively associated with GTFP …

Multiple chronic conditions and intrinsic capacity among middle-aged and older adults
abstract: With the accelerating global aging process, maintaining intrinsic capacity (IC) among middle-aged and older adults has become a major public health priority. Multiple chronic conditions (MCC) are highly prevalent in later life and may contribute to declines in physical and mental functioning. However, evidence regarding the association between MCC and IC, as well as variations across disease types and socioeconomic contexts, remains limited. This study aimed to examine the association between MCC and IC among middle-aged and older adults and to explore heterogeneity across chronic disease categories, regional contexts, and individual characteristics. Data were obtained from the 2011, 2015, and 2018 waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Using 28,613 pooled repeated cross-sectional person-wave observations, regression models incorporating survey-year and regional fixed effects were applied to examine the association between MCC and IC. Respondent-level cluster-robust standard errors were used to account for the nonindependence of repeated observations. Robustness analyses, instrumental variable estimation, and propensity score matching were conducted to assess the stability of the findings. Subgroup analyses were performed across macro-level (urban/rural residence and regional economic zones) and micro-level (sex, education, and household income) characteri…

title: Dehydrogenation of Biomass‐Derived Aromatic Diol to Value‐Added Acyloin and Hydrogen Production Over Zn 0.3 Cd 0.7 S Solid Solution With Defect Clusters and Its Photocatalytic Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven acceptorless dehydrogenation over semiconductor photocatalysts offers an integrated strategy for selective valorization of biomass and hydrogen evolution. However, the spatial confinement of the dehydrogenation and proton reduction processes generally induces strong Coulombic coupling of photoinduced charges, resulting in frustrated reaction kinetics. In this study, we develop a defect‐cluster synergistic strategy to overcome the above challenges. We construct Mo δ + substitution‐Zn vacancy (Mo Zn V Zn ) defect clusters in Zn 0.3 Cd 0.7 S via in situ charge compensation. The quasi‐continuous defect states arising from these associated point defects enable the persistent decoupling of 56.3% of the photoinduced charges with a lifetime of 2542.9 ps. The Mo Zn V Zn defect clusters also serve as synergistic active sites, simultaneously facilitating hole‐mediated dehydrogenation and the entire electron‐mediated sequence from proton‐coupled electron transfer to surface‐adsorbed hydrogen transfer. Consequently, a lignin‐derived aromatic diol achieves 90.4% conversion in 1 h, yielding hydrogen and value‐added aromatic acyloin at rates of 7.4 and 7.3 mmol·g −1 ·h −1 , respectively. This study offers an integrated strategy that simultaneously decouples photoinduced charges and engineers catalytic sites in spatially confined photoredox reactions, opening up an alterna…

title: Biochar–Straw Interaction Drives Soil Carbon Accrual by Modulating Microbial Metabolic Pathways
abstract: Abstract Straw and biochar additions can enhance long-term carbon storage, yet how their interactions regulate carbon mineralization and allocation remains unclear. We conducted a 360-day microcosm incubation employing a reciprocal 13C-labeling design that paired 13C-labeled straw with unlabeled biochar and unlabeled straw with 13C-labeled biochar and used single-cell Raman spectroscopy and 13C-labeled cell metagenomics. At day 360, biochar reduced cumulative straw-derived 13CO2 from 1391 to 1199 mg C kg–1 soil, while increasing straw-C allocation to fulvic acid (FA) and humic acid (HA) fractions. This shift was associated with enrichment of bacterial taxa such as Chitinophagales and increased abundance of genes involved in phospholipid metabolism, the phenylacetyl-CoA pathway, and potential polyphenol-related processing. Conversely, straw increased biochar-derived dissolved organic carbon from 1.5 to 5.5 mg C kg–1 soil and cumulative 13CO2 release from 17 to 23 mg C kg–1 soil, increasing FA and HA allocation. This shift was associated with the enrichment of genes involved in oxidative degradation, membrane transport (for substrate uptake), exopolysaccharide (EPS) formation, and quinone biosynthesis. Overall, the biochar–straw interaction redirected exogenous carbon from rapid mineralization toward humic substance associated soil organic matter fractions, thereby enhancing soil…

title: Strongly Polarized Emission and Sub-Band-Gap Excitation of Ultrasharp Defect Emitters in MAPbI3 Single Crystals
abstract: Abstract Photoluminescence excitation (PLE) and polarization spectroscopy are used to investigate the origin of the ultrasharp defect-center luminescence of MAPbI3 (MA = CH3NH3) single crystals at low temperature. We find that the excitation of the defect states through the free-exciton (FE) resonance is inefficient. Instead, the defect luminescence is strongly enhanced under sub-band-gap excitation, approximately 20 meV below the band gap. This channel enhances the sharp lines and the broad photoluminescence background nonselectively and is attributed to a bound-to-free (BF) transition. Polarization spectroscopy across multiple crystals reveals a degree of linear polarization as high as 40% for the ultrasharp defect lines, while a maximum of 16% is reached for the near-band-edge (NBE) emission. Distinct polarization axes are observed for the two emissions. This anisotropy suggests a preferential orientation of the defect dipoles, governed by the local symmetry of the emitting centers rather than by the crystal symmetry. The excitation and polarization results are consistent with a donor–acceptor pair (DAP) origin of the ultrasharp emission and open the way to a deeper understanding of the electronic properties of defects in halide perovskites (HPs).

title: Usefulness of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography for T1 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: The utility of 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) for T1 esophageal cancer is unclear. This study analyzed the usefulness of FDG-PET for T1 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Medical records of patients with T1 ESCC between December 2008 and July 2024 at Pusan National University Yangsan Hospital were retrospectively reviewed. The preoperative FDG-PET/CT findings and final pathological results of patients with T1 ESCC confirmed by surgery or endoscopic resection were compared. Among the 133 patients with T1 ESCC, 84 (63.2%) had mucosal cancer, 49 (36.8%) had submucosal cancer, and 9 (6.8%) had lymph node metastasis. The maximal standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of the PET/CT images was positively correlated with the invasion depth ( r = 0.670; P < .001) and tumor length ( r = 0.518; P < .001). PET confirmed FDG uptake in 8 cases of mucosal cancer and 35 cases of submucosal cancer (9.5% vs 71.4%; P < .001). The negative predictive value and positive predictive value of FDG-PET/CT for identifying mucosal cancer were 84% and 81%, respectively. Of the 8 mucosal cancers in which FDG uptake was observed during PET, 5 (62.5%) were whole or near-circumferential lesions. FDG uptake observed using PET/CT was positively correlated with the invasion depth and tumor length of T1 ESCC. FDG-PET/CT may provide complementary informat…

title: Is Carbon Monoxide Poisoning a Potential Trigger for Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection? A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a rare but potentially fatal cause of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), often associated with younger individuals and women without traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning, a known cause of systemic hypoxia, has been implicated in various cardiovascular complications; however, its role in triggering SCAD remains scarcely reported. We present the case of a 55-year-old woman who developed SCAD following acute CO poisoning caused by a domestic gas leak. The patient presented with altered mental status and respiratory failure, requiring hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Following stabilization, typical anginal symptoms emerged, accompanied by rising cardiac biomarkers suggestive of myocardial injury. Coronary angiography revealed spontaneous dissections in both the distal left anterior descending artery and the distal right coronary artery without critical flow limitation. The patient was managed conservatively with medical therapy and remained asymptomatic at six-month follow-up. This case highlights the importance of considering SCAD in patients presenting with cardiac symptoms following CO poisoning and underscores the need for vigilance in atypical presentations of myocardial injury.

title: The Stability and Response Boundaries of AVOC-BVOC Dominance Under Extreme Anthropogenic Emission Reductions: A Natural Experiment in Sichuan, China
abstract: Regional volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions arise from both anthropogenic volatile organic compounds (AVOCs) and biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs), yet the stability of their relative dominance under extreme anthropogenic emission reductions and the spatial extent of potential shifts remain unclear. Using the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown as a natural experiment, we developed a unified 3 km monthly AVOC-BVOC emission inventory for Sichuan Province. The lockdown substantially reduced AVOC emissions but did not eliminate a persistent AVOC emission baseline. Industrial sources consistently contributed approximately 73% of AVOCs, even during the strict lockdown. Continuous production industries accounted for 62.4% of industrial process emissions. Meanwhile, regional VOC emissions remained strongly dominated by BVOCs, which accounted for 92.43% of annual emissions. Despite this strong anthropogenic perturbation, 82.99% of grid cells retained their original dominant source type. Source shifts occurred in only 17.01% of grid cells. These shifts were concentrated in basin margin transition zones, where AVOC and BVOC contributions were comparable. This spatial pattern indicates that extreme anthropogenic emission reductions primarily altered AVOC emission intensity rather than regional source dominance. Persistent industrial emissions maintained a stable anthropogenic emission…

title: Synergistic Enhancement of Mechanical and Thermal Properties in Polydopamine‐Modified Carbon Fiber/Graphene Oxide‐Epoxy Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites, which exhibit excellent mechanical performance and low density, suffer from low surface activity across various applications. Dopamine self‐polymerized on the carbon fiber surface via π‐π interaction to form a nano‐thin surface‐adherent polydopamine (PDA) layer to improve the bonding between the fiber and the epoxy resin. Graphene oxide (GO) was also added to the epoxy matrix to increase the mechanical strength of the composites. The objective of this study is to investigate the thermal and mechanical properties of PDA modified CFRP with embedded various GO loadings (0.25–0.75 wt.%). The composite laminates were fabricated through the vacuum‐assisted resin transfer molding (VARTM) process. The PDA modified carbon fiber was characterized using FT‐IR, XRD, and Raman Spectroscopy. As a result, both the tensile and flexural properties were effectively improved in the PDA‐modified carbon fiber reinforced epoxy (DCFRP) composite and the GO‐embedded DCFRP/GO/epoxy composites. The tensile strength, flexural strength, and glass transition temperature ( T g ) increased by 42.77%, 135%, and 11.6% at a GO loading of 0.50 wt.% compared to the bare CFRP composite. Overall, PDA modification of carbon fibers significantly enhanced both the thermal stability and mechanical performance of the composites, establishing this approach as a …

title: Acid Leaching for Carbon Sequestration with Prospects for Critical Metal Recovery
abstract: Abstract Reducing carbon emissions and supplying critical metals for the green energy transition are essential to limiting global warming to below 1.5 °C. Here, we propose heap leaching ultramafic material with sulfuric acid followed by sequential precipitation for nickel recovery and carbon sequestration. Ultramafic materials were subjected to benchtop-scale acid leaches using 0.08–0.8 M H2SO4. The leachates were combined with NaOH to precipitate Ni (oxy)hydroxide minerals and then with NaOH + Na2CO3 to precipitate Mg carbonate minerals. The carbon sequestration potential of each sample and the efficiency of each experimental stage were calculated to estimate carbon sequestration using these techniques. The acid leaching released 2–57% of the Mg2+ along with 6–64% of the Ni2+ into the leachate, depending on acid strength and tailings mineralogy, while carbonation precipitated up to 95% of the dissolved Mg2+ and 90% of the CO32– + HCO3– in solution, depending on initial Mg2+ concentrations. Techno-economic analysis demonstrates that treatment cost and Ni production are the most important factors determining the profitability of the process, with CO2 removal being less important due to the relatively low value of carbon credits compared to Ni, but still contributing to the sustainability of this process.
