Biomarker Integration in the Perioperative Management of Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: The concept of personalized medicine has tremendous appeal—tailoring diagnosis and treatment to an individual, rather than a “one-size-fits-all” approach. The management of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has rapidly evolved toward strategies increasingly guided by tumor biology and precision oncology. The safety and significant efficacy of biomarker-directed therapies in metastatic disease have fueled interest in applying precision oncology to early-stage, operable NSCLC. Advances in molecular profiling have revealed that a substantial proportion of resected NSCLC harbor actionable driver mutations, enabling the integration of targeted therapies into the perioperative setting. The success of adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor and anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibition established a framework for biomarker-driven therapy and highlights the importance of comprehensive molecular testing at diagnosis. In parallel, perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-based strategies have expanded treatment options for appropriately selected patients, further emphasizing the importance of molecular profiling. Significant implementation gaps remain, including incomplete molecular testing, delayed results, inadequate tissue sampling, fragmented workflows, and disparities in access. Beyond clinically actionable driver mutations, emerging research highlights radiogenomics and advances in…

title: Financial Development and Environmental Sustainability: The Role of Renewable Energy in Non-Oil Exporting Emerging Economies
abstract: Financial development is frequently viewed as a means of inspiring investment, technological innovation and infrastructure development, which in turn can drive sustainable economic transition. However, the impacts on the environment of the growth of financial systems are not clear, especially in emerging economies where increased economic activity is still reliant upon fossil fuels. The study analyzes the direct relationship between financial development and environmental sustainability as well as the indirect route via the adoption of renewable energies, based on the theoretical concepts of sustainable finance, energy transition and the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC), which are also discussed using panel data from emerging countries over the period of 1995-2022. The study employs the Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS) method, and concludes that financial development has a positive impact on CO₂ emissions, thus confirming that financial expansion remains to a large extent focused on traditional, carbon-intensive economic activities. The control variables also suggest that economic and structural factors are also significant in explaining environmental outcomes in emerging economies. Contrary to the view that renewable energy acts as a linker between financial development and environmental sustainability, renewable energy significantly lowers CO₂ emissions, however, it…
venue: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries: Social Science

title: Size and Shape Dependent Band Gap Engineering in III–V Nanosemiconductors Using Qi, Bond Energy and Guisbiers Models
abstract: In this study, the size- and shape-dependent variation of the energy band gap in III–V nanosemiconductors has been systematically investigated using three widely accepted phenomenological approaches, namely the Qi model, Bond Energy model, and Guisbiers model. The theoretical analysis has been performed for important III–V semiconductor compounds such as AlN, GaN, InN, GaAs, and InAs, considering different nanostructured geometries including spherical nanoparticles, cylindrical nanowires, and nanofilms. The band gap expansion (ΔEg) has been evaluated as a function of particle size (diameter or width) as well as structural geometry. The obtained results clearly indicate that the energy band gap increases significantly with decreasing size of the nanostructures, which is mainly attributed to the quantum confinement effect arising from the spatial restriction of charge carriers at the nanoscale. It has also been observed that the geometry of the nanostructure plays an important role in determining the magnitude of band gap enhancement due to differences in surface-to-volume ratio. Among the models considered, the Guisbiers model provides the closest agreement with the available simulated and experimental data, demonstrating its superior predictive capability. Furthermore, the study examines the shifts in valence band and conduction band edges, revealing that the conduction band ex…
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

title: Moisture-Dependent Compressive Behavior of Wheat Kernels: Implications for Energy-Efficient and Resource-Conscious Grain Processing
abstract: Improving grain size-reduction efficiency requires settings adapted to raw-material properties. This study examined how moisture, crosshead speed, imposed displacement, cultivar, and wheat quality group affect individual-kernel compression. Four cultivars representing bread and ‘other’ quality groups were tested at nominal moisture contents of 14–20% (wet basis), crosshead speeds of 5–30 mm min−1, and displacements of 1.8–2.2 mm. Maximum force, crushing energy, and apparent cracking were determined. Crosshead speed did not significantly affect maximum force and had a marginal effect on crushing energy. Displacement and cultivar explained the largest variability shares, while both responses reached their highest means at 18% nominal moisture. Lawina and Sikorka, both in the ‘other’ group, differed by approximately 36% in maximum force and 25% in crushing energy. The share without apparent cracking rose from approximately 5% at 14% to 96% at 20%. Unlike our earlier study of six quality wheat cultivars, this study compares bread and ‘other’ groups and examines differences between cultivars assigned to the same group. The findings inform product-specific screening; industrial energy and material savings remain to be verified.

title: Phenyllactic Acid Suppresses Growth and Induces Coordinated Changes in PSII Photochemistry and Energy Dissipation in the Filamentous Cyanobacterium Dolichospermum sp. FACHB-82
abstract: Dolichospermum sp. FACHB-82, a representative harmful bloom-forming cyanobacterium, has garnered widespread attention in freshwater ecosystems due to its high environmental adaptability and potential for rapid proliferation. Phenyllactic acid (PLA) is a structurally defined aromatic organic acid with known antimicrobial activity, but its inhibitory effects on FACHB-82 and their photosynthetic apparatus remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the concentration-dependent effects of PLA on biomass accumulation, photosynthetic pigment production and photosynthetic activity in FACHB-82. The findings revealed that PLA induced a concentration-dependent biphasic response on biomass accumulation and photosynthetic pigment synthesis of FACHB-82. Chlorophyll a fluorescence analyses revealed that high-concentration PLA exposure disrupted functions of PSII at multiple levels, including reduced PSII performance, enhanced QA− accumulation, accelerated reaction center closure, decreased energetic connectivity, impaired donor side function, and restricted downstream electron transport. Although NPQ was significantly upregulated under high PLA stress, dark-recovery analysis demonstrated that the increased non-photochemical energy dissipation was accompanied by incomplete recovery of PSII photochemical efficiency. Our finding, for the first time, provides physiological insight in…

title: A Formative Evaluation of a Design Guide for Blended Learning Environments
abstract: Abstract A blended learning environment combines offline and online delivery methods. Although such environments can motivate students to learn, designing them is a key challenge. According to self-determination theory, students are motivated to learn when their basic psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness are satisfied. Although self-determination theory is well established, it remains unclear how to design combinations of offline and online delivery methods that support students’ psychological needs. We developed a design guide intended to help teachers design such environments. This study reports on an early-stage formative evaluation conducted to collect feedback on the guide’s applicability. We invited eight teachers to use the guide to design a combination of offline and online delivery methods for their educational programs. We collected qualitative feedback on how the teachers understood the guide through audio recordings of conversations; how their design decisions deviated from what the guide prescribed through design templates; and what aspects of the guide could be improved through reflective questions and focus groups. The main findings highlighted ways to improve how delivery methods are defined and classified. Drawing on these findings, we propose both refinements to the conceptualization of delivery methods and design ideas. This study may…
venue: Journal of Formative Design in Learning

title: Students’ Generative AI Use in Studio-Based Design Education: Selective Use, Design Judgment, and Studio Context
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping studio-based design education, yet relatively little is known about how students decide when and how AI should support their design process. This study examined students’ use, adaptation, and perceptions of generative AI, with particular attention to task-specific use, contextual adaptation, and factors associated with AI-related decision-making. An online survey of 112 undergraduate and graduate design students combined structured questionnaire items with optional open-ended responses to examine AI use across studio tasks, project stages, and learning contexts. Students reported higher AI use for concept development, research, and written articulation than for visual refinement, technical documentation, and later stages of design development. Students also reported becoming more selective in their AI use as projects progressed, while instructor expectations, peer influence, and concern about negative judgment were associated with students’ AI-related decisions. Qualitative responses further highlighted authorship, learning, and professional responsibility as important considerations. Together, these findings suggest that students’ selective and context-dependent AI use can be interpreted as boundary-setting around when and how AI participates in the design process. Rather than viewing AI use simply as technology adop…

title: Inteligência Artificial Generativa no Design de Jogos Digitais
abstract: This article examines the impacts of generative artificial intelligence on digital game design creation, investigating how this technology transforms creative processes in the industry. The research, using a qualitative approach, employed bibliographic review, comparative case study between Palworld and Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, and semi-structured interviews with three professionals in the field. The analysis identified five thematic categories: technological democratization, transformation of creative processes, preservation of human authenticity, ethical issues, and professional adaptation. The results show that generative AI democratizes game development, allowing independent studios to achieve quality comparable to major producers, but raises questions about authenticity and ethical sustainability. As a practical contribution, the study proposes seven guidelines for maintaining human-centered design, balancing technological innovation with ethical values and human creativity.
authors: Cássia Regina D'Antonio Rocha da Silva

title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. The present study proposes an integrated spatial suitability framework employing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) coupled with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to delineate optimal sites for geothermal power plant development within the study area. In the context of escalating global energy demands, geothermal energy, defined as terrestrial heat extracted from the Earth’s crust through deep drilling and surface fluid transport, represents a viable pathway toward energy transition. The analytical framework was constructed from subsurface thermal data derived from 52 hydrocarbon wells, enabling the computation of geothermal gradients at varying depths and heat flow assessments. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to nine (geothermal gradient, heat flow, fault density, geology, seismic activity, proximity to the electricity grid, proximity to roads, land use, and slope) spatially explicit criteria encompassing thermal, geological, topographic, en…

title: Population structure, avirulence profiles and race diversity of Leptosphaeria maculans in western Canada, 2015–2017: implications for R-gene deployment
Next-Generation Modulation and Control of Power Electronic Systems: AI-Enabled Control, Digital Twins, Fault-Tolerant Operation, and Cyber-Physical Security
abstract: Power electronic systems are evolving from conventional fixed-function converters toward intelligent, adaptive, and cyber-physical energy-conversion platforms in which modulation, predictive control, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DTs), fault diagnosis, and cybersecurity increasingly interact within a unified closed-loop architecture. This paper presents an integrated review and mathematical framework for next-generation modulation and control of power electronic systems, with an emphasis on advanced modulation, predictive control, AI-assisted adaptation, converter-oriented digital state estimation, fault-tolerant operation, and cyber-resilient control. The proposed framework links converter dynamics, state and parameter estimation, physical faults, cyber disturbances, supervisory anomaly assessment, and mode-dependent control reconfiguration. Two clearly separated validation levels complement the literature synthesis: experimentally measured operating data are used to establish physically representative operating conditions, whereas a dedicated converter-control model is used to evaluate closed-loop dynamic resilience. Under a combined physical/cyber disturbance, resilient reconfiguration reduced the post-event speed RMSE from 9.203 to 0.425 rad/s, the peak speed error from 29.999 to 1.724 rad/s, and the maximum current from 69.112 to 10.662 A, while eliminating …

title: Self-phase modulation in high-resolution DAS: impact of high-peak-power Gaussian pulses
abstract: Modulation instability (MI) is a well-known limit for distributed fiber sensors. However, self-phase modulation (SPM) is rarely addressed as a standalone constraint in distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). This study demonstrates, through modeling and experiments, that SPM-induced spectral broadening causes significant backscattered signal losses and increased phase noise. These effects are particularly critical when using high-power, short Gaussian pulses commonly used to extend the sensing range. We highlight the predominant role of the detection bandwidth in these excess losses, proving that SPM is a limiting factor independent of MI for high-resolution nonlinear ϕ -OTDR measurements.

title: A Finite-State and Boolean Control Framework for Resilient Power and Thermal Management in Telecommunication Base Stations
abstract: Telecommunication base transceiver stations (BTS) require power-source switching and thermal-management logic that remains predictable and checkable under grid disturbances, generator operation and thermal excursions. Existing microcontroller-based BTS site-management implementations, including the ATmega32-based MBSMECS architecture that motivates this study, provide the basis for the present formal analysis, describe this logic operationally as narrative relay behaviour rather than as an explicit verifiable control model. This paper reformulates the switching and thermal-control logic of that implemented system as a two-layer formal control framework: a finite-state model that represents grid-supply, generator-start-permissive, generator-supply, restoration, transfer and shutdown conditions as explicit states and transition conditions and a Boolean interlock layer that expresses three-phase grid availability, the generator-start permissive and source exclusivity as logical expressions. A symbolic lumped-parameter thermal model with hysteresis switching is developed to represent the thermostat-driven air-conditioner allocation logic and is treated as a discrete-event process coupled to, rather than separate from, the power-switching automaton. Component-level sizing calculations from the original design are retained as supporting engineering-consistency checks rather than as t…

title: Unsettling AI literacies: ethics, power and the pedagogies of critical research
abstract: As GenAI systems have moved from novelty to everyday use in research and learningpractices, higher education institutions are increasingly adopting them in the realms of“literacy”, “responsible use”, and “ethical awareness”. Such framings often assume strategicsimplifications: imagining ethics as a checklist of principles and downplaying theinfrastructural forces that shape what counts as legitimate knowledge. This paper argues thatapproaching AI as a neutral “tool” obscures the value regimes and power asymmetriesembedded in its very architecture. Drawing on critical & education technology studies, itproposes a reorientation from AI literacy to critical AI socio-technical practices. Suchpractices have informed the curricular design, pedagogical implementation, and teachingreflections of two core modules within an online MA distance-learning programme. Theseare pedagogical practices that aim to foreground situated accountability, epistemic plurality,and alternative imaginaries. By centring observations from curriculum design & learningengagements, this paper advocates for an approach to AI in educational research thatforegrounds critical AI literacies: pedagogies attentive to power asymmetries, and that inspirethe emergent ways learners may reimagine (and sometimes resist) AI’s role in academicinquiry. This allows for reframing ethics as a politics of value production and infras…

title: Risk-managed routes to space-based solar power
Pidgin as Resistance in Elif Batuman's The Idiot: The Psychology of Power and Acquisition in Selin's ESL Tutoring
abstract: This research examines the intersection of psychology and linguistics in Elif Batuman's The Idiot, concentrating on the protagonist Selin Karadag's experiences working as an ESL instructor in a housing complex. Through a detailed analysis of tutoring sessions with students Joaquín and Linda, this study examines the shortcomings of traditional English instruction in a repressive institutional setting. It specifically examines the evolution of language anomalies, such as the expression "Papel iss blonk." It claims that the "pidgin" that develops between the student and the tutor is a type of psycholinguistic resistance against the institutional force of authority, in addition to being a failure to learn. Grounded in critical pedagogy and a psycho-narratological perspective, this study examines how Selin's linguistic training conflicts with the reality of teaching, leading to a crisis of intimacy, authority, and self-perception. The findings suggest that learning one's own language is a defensive strategy that addresses the colonial relations present in the process of learning standard English and offers insight into Selin's overall existential crisis in terms of meaning and communication. In contrast to simple grammar, language acquisition is shown in this study to be a complex process of identity, negotiating power, and psychological safety.
venue: Theory and Practice in Language Studies

title: Plant‐derived compounds to improve soil inoculation for restoration
abstract: Abstract Restoring the soil microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important requirement for the success of ecosystem restoration. Soil inoculation can reintroduce the missing taxa, but its application is limited by the large amount of donor soil that is needed and by the poor persistence of the inoculants, because of habitat filtering, priority effects and the loss of plant–microbe feedbacks. Here we propose the metabolite‐inoculum approach, a framework that combines the chemical diversity of plants with soil inoculation, in order to improve the establishment, persistence and effectiveness of introduced microbial communities. In this framework, the chemical input is delivered as fresh and dead plant material, as extracts of this material or as purified compounds that are applied together with the inoculum, and not by adding or manipulating the living plant community. We first synthesize the evidence that plant metabolites, from both above‐ and below‐ground tissues, act as selective regulators of soil microbial composition and diversity. Building on this, we propose a framework for the selection of plant materials and metabolites at the species, tissue and compound levels, and we introduce the parallel concepts of core and keystone metabolites that are matched to their corresponding microbial groups. We then identify the main challenges of the approach, the mismatch in tim…

title: High-power tunable laser operation of Ho:YScO 3 crystal at 2.1 µm
abstract: We report the Czochralski growth, spectroscopic characterization, and laser performance at 2.1 µm of a Ho:YScO 3 mixed sesquioxide crystal with a doping concentration of 0.4 at.%. Spectroscopic evaluation was performed based on room-temperature absorption and fluorescence measurements. Intensity parameters, radiative lifetime of the 5 I 7 manifold, and spontaneous emission rates were calculated based on Judd–Ofelt theory. For the 5 I 7 → 5 I 8 transition near 2.1 µm, the emission cross-section was derived to be 4.06 × 10 −21 cm 2 , with an exceptionally broad full width at half maximum spectrum of 210.14 nm. In the laser experiment, the laser delivers a maximum continuous-wave output power of 12.1 W with a slope efficiency of 31%. Wavelength tuning over 85 nm (2074–2159 nm) is demonstrated using a Lyot filter. These results establish Ho:YScO 3 crystal as a promising gain medium for high-power, broadly tunable, and potentially ultrafast 2.1 µm lasers.

title: Lightweight Edge-Based Intrusion Detection for Power Monitoring Systems
abstract: The network security threats faced by the power monitoring system in the open network environment are becoming increasingly complex, and the attack forms are diversified and concealed. Undetected attacks may lead to abnormal monitoring data, control command failures, or even critical equipment shutdown, thereby threatening the security and stability of the power system. Therefore, network security protection methods that balance detection accuracy, response speed, and edge deployment efficiency have significant engineering application value. To improve the security protection capabilities and real-time response performance in a dynamic network environment, a network security protection method that integrates lightweight intelligent sensing and edge collaborative deployment is constructed. Through multi-source feature fusion and lightweight detection models, combined with the cloud-edge collaborative mechanism, efficient detection and low-latency response to complex attacks are achieved. Experiments showed that the Macro-averaged F1-score reached 0.93, which was 2.08–8.60% higher than that of baseline methods, respectively. The proportion of high-confidence samples of the proposed method was more than 77%, and it could still maintain an attack detection rate of more than 0.94 under different attack traffic proportions. The results show that the method achieves a good balance bet…

title: Leptogenesis without on-shell right-handed neutrinos
abstract: A bstract We propose a novel mechanism for generating the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through leptogenesis in a scenario where the right-handed neutrinos are heavier than the maximal temperature of the Universe, and are never produced on-shell, neither by thermal nor by non-thermal mechanisms. We introduce a new scalar field, ϕ , lighter than the right-handed neutrinos, that couples to the latter via a Yukawa coupling, so that it decays into two lepton doublets and two higgs doublets via off-shell right-handed neutrinos. Then, we derive the CP asymmetry arising from the interference between tree-level and loop diagrams in the four-body decay, and we show that the generated baryon asymmetry can reproduce the observed value both in a scenario where ϕ is responsible for the reheating of the Universe, and in a scenario where ϕ is a generic scalar that remains in thermal equilibrium with the plasma.

title: A Review of Pendulum Systems and Structures for Wave Energy Conversion
abstract: Wave energy has emerged as a promising renewable energy source due to its high energy density and consistency compared to solar and wind. This literature review explores the technological components and design considerations of wave energy converters (WECs), focusing on primary systems, power take-off (PTO) mechanisms, and innovative concepts utilizing enclosed-hull converters based on pendulum systems and structures. Various WEC designs are analyzed with respect to their operational principles, advantages and limitations. Special attention is given to recent advances in enclosed WEC systems utilizing pendulum-based inertial converters. These devices offer a flexible means for establishing resonant response of a PTO enclosed within the WEC buoy or hull, and as such, pendulum-based WECs have attracted significant interest within academia and relevant industry stakeholders. Through comprehensive comparison and evaluation, this review identifies key trends and challenges in the development, optimization and commercialization of pendulum-based wave energy technology.

title: Human Development, Industrialization, Renewable Energy, and Environmental Taxation as Determinants of CO2 Emissions: Evidence from Heterogeneous Panel and Quantile Analysis
abstract: Carbon dioxide emissions remain the principal driver of anthropogenic climate change, yet the socioeconomic forces that shape per capita emissions differ markedly across the distribution of emitting economies. This study examines the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions per capita using a balanced structure of 1189 country–year observations drawn from a panel of 41 countries over the period 1995–2023. Four explanatory variables are considered: the Human Development Index, the share of manufacturing value added in gross domestic product, the share of primary energy sourced from renewables, and environmentally related tax revenue expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product. Cross-sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity are formally tested and confirmed, motivating the use of second-generation panel techniques throughout. The Pesaran cross-sectionally augmented Dickey–Fuller test reveals a mixed order of integration, and the Westerlund error-correction-based cointegration test confirms a long-run equilibrium relationship among the series. Long-run marginal effects estimated through the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group and Augmented Mean Group estimators show that human development, manufacturing intensity, and environmentally related tax revenue raise per capita emissions on average, while renewable energy penetration lowers them. Method of Moments Quantile Re…

title: Sexualidade na infância e na adolescência: olhares em disputa entre família e Estado
abstract: Este ensaio aborda o debate sobre a sexualidade na infância e na adolescência, tema marcado por contradições e polêmicas na sociedade contemporânea. Partindo do princípio de que a integridade e a dignidade sexual de crianças e adolescentes demandam proteção absoluta, o estudo examina as profundas divergências conceituais e normativas que cercam o tema. A revisão evidencia uma disputa central de perspectivas: de um lado, a defesa da primazia da família na formação moral e na definição dos limites da educação sexual; de outro, a ênfase na responsabilidade pedagógica da escola e do Estado. O principal desafio, portanto, consiste em reconhecer a legitimidade dessas divergências e consolidar salvaguardas institucionais que delimitem, de forma clara, as responsabilidades complementares entre a família e o poder público.

title: Black holes and Abelian instantons
abstract: A bstract We argue that the electromagnetic θ -term is a physical parameter of the Standard Model coupled to gravity. Specifically, in the context of 4-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory we show that there exist Euclidean field configurations that have finite action, are asymptotically flat, and feature non-zero electromagnetic second Chern number. These “gravitational Abelian instantons” correspond to a dyonic extension of a Euclidean wormhole. We argue that these configurations should be included in the gravitational path integral, and that doing so generates a non-perturbative contribution to the vacuum energy density that is θ -dependent. We provide a Lorentzian interpretation of these instantons as capturing the effect of quantum fluctuations corresponding to pair production and annihilation of charged black holes. When θ is the expectation value of a dynamical axion field, the instantons presented here generate a potential for the axion, thereby breaking the axion shift symmetry. This provides yet another example of how quantum gravity violates global symmetries through the existence of black holes.

title: High-Temperature Corrosion in Biomass and Waste-to-Energy Boilers: Mechanisms, Materials and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Biomass and waste contain elevated concentrations of chlorine and alkali metals that promote the problem of high-temperature chlorine corrosion in power boilers. The results are rapid metal loss, increased maintenance costs, and reduced operational availability. This review paper provides a comprehensive overview of the high-temperature chlorine corrosion in biomass- and waste-fired boilers. The occurrence and chemical speciation of chlorine in these fuels are discussed together with its transformation during thermal conversion. Particular attention is devoted to the mechanisms of active oxidation, the role of ash deposits and their chemistry. The corrosion performance of conventional boiler steels, nickel-based alloys, and protective coatings is evaluated. Laboratory investigation methods, including gravimetric measurement and microstructural characterization are reviewed alongside recent advances in computational modelling, such as thermodynamic equilibrium calculations and computational fluid dynamics. The review shows that corrosion severity is governed by the coupled effects of chlorine speciation, alkali metals, deposit chemistry, temperature, combustion conditions, and material properties. Advanced alloys and protective coatings can substantially improve corrosion resistance, but cannot completely eliminate degradation under prolonged exposure. The analysis also indicate…

title: Amphiphilic MoS2 Nanosheet-Enhanced Salt-Tolerant Alkyl Polyether Sulfonate Surfactant Flooding System for Interfacial Regulation and Enhanced Oil Recovery Performance
abstract: Abstract The complex ionic environment in high-salinity reservoirs can weaken surfactant adsorption at oil–water interfaces and compromise interfacial film stability, limiting the effectiveness of chemical flooding systems for residual-oil mobilization. To improve the oil-displacement performance of salt-tolerant surfactant systems, two alkyl polyether sulfonate surfactants with different alkyl chains and polyether structures (CX1 and CX2) were used to construct a mixed surfactant system. Amphiphilically modified MoS2 nanosheets were introduced to investigate their synergistic effects on interfacial behavior, wettability alteration, emulsion stability, and enhanced oil recovery performance. The results showed that the CX1/CX2 = 5:5 mass ratio exhibited favorable interfacial activity in simulated formation water containing Ca2+ and Mg2+. The addition of 0.01 wt % MoS2 further reduced the interfacial tension to 1.49 × 10–3 mN/m and increased the interfacial storage modulus and loss modulus. Meanwhile, MoS2 addition reduced water separation, inhibited droplet coalescence, and improved droplet-size distribution stability. Contact-angle measurements demonstrated enhanced wettability alteration, with the contact angle decreasing from 38.87° to 28.76° after MoS2 addition. Core-flooding experiments showed that repeated surfactant injection produced only 1.19% incremental oil recovery, …

title: Pottery jar rainwater storage as living heritage: cultural adaptation to saline intrusion in coastal Thailand
abstract: ABSTRACT Decentralised rainwater systems are well established in Thailand but remain poorly understood in coastal settlements with brackish groundwater and canals. This study examines how pottery-jar rainwater storage was configured, maintained, and adapted in Ban Khao Yi San, an estuarine village in Samut Songkhram Province, and how living heritage can inform water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) planning. A qualitative case study combined four field rounds in March and October 2025 and 2026 with observation, photography, document review, and contextual conversations with adult residents. Evidence covered environmental setting, built form, storage infrastructure, and changing water practices. Salinity, rainfall, and water quality were not measured. Households used roof catchments, improvised conveyance, and ceramic or cement jars. Residents described first-flush diversion, selective use of rainwater for drinking, and historical boat transport from fresher upstream sources. The settlement is shifting from large reserves towards smaller hybrid systems storing rainwater or intermittent piped water. Comparison with freshwater areas of the Mae Klong basin and drought-prone Northeast Thailand suggests that salinity did not create jar use but increased its importance where alternatives were brackish. WASH planning should consider vessels, routines, spatial arrangements, and knowledge…
venue: Journal of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene for Development

title: Mecanismos de participación ciudadana, seguimiento e incidencia percibida en la gestión municipal: evidencia mixta de El Empalme, Ecuador
abstract: La existencia de mecanismos institucionales de participación ciudadana amplía las oportunidades de intervención social, pero su efectividad depende de que los aportes recibidos sean procesados, respondidos y vinculados con la gestión municipal. El objetivo fue analizar los mecanismos de participación ciudadana, las condiciones de acceso, el seguimiento institucional y la incidencia percibida en la gestión administrativa del Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Municipal del cantón El Empalme, Ecuador, durante 2023. Se desarrolló un estudio de caso con enfoque mixto, sustentado en una encuesta a 383 habitantes, una entrevista semiestructurada al jefe del Departamento de Participación Ciudadana y un grupo focal con ocho ciudadanos y líderes comunitarios. Los datos cuantitativos se analizaron mediante frecuencias y porcentajes, mientras la información cualitativa se examinó mediante análisis de contenido e integración temática. El 87,5 % declaró no haber participado en actividades organizadas por el GAD; el 56,9 % señaló que la información era clara y suficiente “casi nunca” o “nunca”; el 77,1 % indicó que las propuestas ciudadanas eran consideradas en la planificación con esa misma baja frecuencia y el 69,5 % reportó seguimiento insuficiente. En contraste, el 69,5 % valoró los mecanismos como bastante o totalmente inclusivos y el 85,9 % manifestó satisfacción con la transparencia en…

title: Rancang Bangun Sistem Identifikasi Biometrik dan Penyimpanan Data Bayi Baru Lahir Berbasis Fingerprint FPM10A dengan Mikrokontroler ATMega328P
abstract: Keselamatan bayi baru lahir sangat penting, namun metode identifikasi konvensional dengan menggunakan gelang identitas yang berisi informasi dasar pasien. Tetapi metode ini memiliki beberapa kelemahan diantaranya dapat terlepas, rusak, atau kesalahan dalam pemasangan yang dapat menyebabkan kesalahan identifikasi bayi. Penelitian ini merancang dan mengembangkan sistem identifikasi biometrik serta penyimpanan data bayi baru lahir berbasis mikrokontroler ATMega328P dengan sensor sidik jari FPM10A. Metode rancang bangun meliputi perancangan perangkat keras (sensor sidik jari FPM10A, mikrokontroler ATMega328P, LCD 20×4, modul SD Card) dan perangkat lunak. Data bayi (nama, tanggal lahir, jenis kelamin, berat badan, nomor rekam medis, dan nama ibu) dimasukkan melalui antarmuka komputer dan disimpan di SD Card dalam format CSV. Pengujian sistem melibatkan 5 subjek dengan total 10 percobaan identifikasi. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan 8 percobaan berhasil dan 2 gagal (tingkat keberhasilan 80%, False Rejection Rate 20%) dengan waktu respons rata-rata 2,8 detik (rentang 2–4 detik). Pengukuran kelistrikan menunjukkan persentase kesalahan tertinggi 1,2% pada rangkaian Step-Up MT3608. Sistem yang dikembangkan berhasil mengintegrasikan proses registrasi sidik jari dan penyimpanan data bayi, serta berpotensi meningkatkan akurasi dan keamanan identifikasi bayi baru lahir di fasilitas kesehatan.

title: Digital Revolution: How Chatbots Increase Revenue for MSMEs in Banten Province
abstract: Utilizing information technology is crucial for enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs. An emerging innovation is the utilization of chatbots, which facilitate automated communication between businesses and customers. The objective of this study is to assess the impact of ease perceptions, usefulness perceptions, information quality, and chatbot implementation on the revenue growth of MSMEs) in Banten Province. The objective of this study is to provide empirical evidence demonstrating the positive impact of chatbots on customer service, operational efficiency, and ultimately the income of MSMEs. The study’s sample consisted of 230 participants from eight cities within the Banten Province region. The data collection method involved sending G Forms to MSME business actors who utilize chatbots, using nonprobability sampling techniques. Based on the gathered MSMEs that used chatbots experienced a 24% increase in their revenue within one month. The findings indicate that perceived ease, perceived usefulness, and information quality significantly influence the adoption of chatbots, leading to a subsequent increase in income for MSMEs. This study is expected to enhance the growth of MSMEs in Banten Province, particularly in the utilization of AI chatbot digital technology.

title: Trade Liberalization, Public Governance, Foreign Direct Investment and Tax Revenue - Evidence from East Africa Community Member Countries
abstract: Tax revenue is a fundamental source of government financing and plays an important role in supporting economic development, provision of public services and fiscal sustainability. However, East African Community (EAC) member countries continue to experience challenges in mobilizing adequate domestic tax revenue amid increasing regional economic integration, trade liberalization and competition for foreign direct investment. This study examined the relationship between trade liberalization, public governance and foreign direct investment on tax revenue of EAC member countries. Trade liberalization was operationalized using trade openness ratio, public governance using the Corruption Perception Index, foreign direct investment using net foreign direct investment flows, and tax revenue using the tax-to-GDP ratio. The study adopted a longitudinal panel research design covering EAC member countries over the period 2000 to 2023. Panel data was employed to establish the joint relationships between the explanatory variables and tax revenue. The findings revealed a statistically significant relationship between trade liberalization, public governance, foreign direct investment and tax revenue. The findings demonstrated that economic openness, investment flows and institutional quality are important dimensions of domestic tax revenue mobilization in the EAC. As a result, this study recom…

title: Hysteresis of Suspension Shock Absorbers: Modeling and Effects on Vehicle Dynamic Performance
abstract: Hysteresis is widely observed in vehicle suspension shock absorbers and can significantly influence vehicle dynamic responses. Although various hysteresis models have been developed to reproduce experimentally observed force–velocity loops, the effects of damper hysteresis on the overall dynamic performance of passive and semi-active suspension systems remain insufficiently quantified. In this study, a parameterized physics-based damper model is developed by incorporating hydraulic-oil compressibility and pressure-dependent gas dissolution and release. The model is experimentally validated using the force–velocity characteristics of a commercial twin-tube hydraulic shock absorber and is subsequently integrated into passive and semi-active suspension systems. Suspension performance is evaluated under bump and random road excitations in terms of settling time, body acceleration (BA), suspension working space (SWS), and dynamic tire deflection (DTD). The results show that the influence of damper hysteresis depends on both the excitation condition and the suspension configuration. Under bump-road excitation, hysteresis reduces the peak BA and DTD while increasing the peak SWS for both passive and semi-active suspensions, and it shortens the corresponding settling times. The variations are more pronounced in the semi-active suspension. Under random road excitation, hysteresis increa…

title: Design and Simulation-Based Evaluation of ARTgriculture 2.0, an IoT-Enabled Unmanned Ground Vehicle for Artistic Landscaping
abstract: As cities densify, urban green infrastructure and artistic landscaping, the deliberate arrangement of plants into visual compositions, carry ecological and public-health weight, yet manual execution does not scale. This article presents ARTgriculture 2.0, a redesigned Internet-of-Things-enabled unmanned ground vehicle that automates the full seeding cycle of digging, sowing, backfilling, and spraying for artistic landscaping, extending our earlier conference prototype. The platform introduces iris-seeding, variable-gap, and depth-control mechanisms sized and fabricated for compositional planting, a layered control architecture, and a browser-based interface for autonomous and manual operation. The redesigned mechanisms were fabricated and exercised on the physical chassis in indoor bench tests, without soil engagement and with no seed lot loaded, and no field trial has been performed; the validation level reported here is therefore module-level bench actuation plus system-level simulation. Full-system seeding is evaluated with a simulation model: a robot model built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim supplies the geometry and scene, while an offline kinematic execution model plans and executes area-fill coverage over regular grids and artistic patterns such as circles, diamonds, and hearts. Under the undisturbed model at a conservative low cruise speed, the platform reaches 96 to 100 percent …

title: Quantifying Temperature-Dependent Fast-Charging Potential of NMC Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are considered a pivotal enabling technology for the advancement of transportation electrification, the development of stationary energy storage systems, and the integration of renewable energy sources. Despite continuous advances in energy density and cell design, the fast-charging capability of LIBs is still significantly constrained by temperature-dependent electrochemical and thermal processes, which are crucial to the overall performance of the battery. The objective is to quantify the temperature-dependent fast-charging potential and charging power capability. This is achieved by experimentally analyzing the internal resistance (IR) during the charging of three large-format prismatic state-of-the-art cells, in addition to extrapolating their charging power capability and constant-current constant-voltage charging behavior under varying thermal boundary conditions. Utilizing the IRs ascertained during the charging process, the fast-charging potential (FCP) is introduced as a dimensionless metric that expresses the temperature-induced increase in the maximum theoretically achievable charging current at a given SoC, relative to 25 °C. Elevated cell temperatures are found to reduce IR and thus increase the theoretically achievable charging power, with the FCP nearly independent of SoC but cell-specific, ranging from about 18% (CATL) to 40% (SVolt)…

title: Assessment and improvement of constructive safety of the Damas light passenger vehicle
abstract: The article is devoted to assessing and improving the constructive safety of the Damas light passenger vehicle widely used in Uzbekistan. The study analyzes the influence of geometric parameters, vehicle stability, braking performance, and active safety systems on overall operational safety. Vehicle stability was evaluated using the Static Stability Factor (SSF), rollover resistance indicators, and braking performance calculations. The obtained results showed that the vehicle’s constructive safety is significantly affected by its center of gravity position, track width, and the absence of modern active safety systems. The calculated stability indicators revealed an increased rollover risk during high-speed cornering maneuvers. A comparative analysis demonstrated that the implementation of Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS) and Electronic Stability Control (ESC) could significantly improve vehicle stability and controllability under critical driving conditions. Based on the findings, engineering recommendations aimed at enhancing vehicle safety, reducing accident risk, and improving operational reliability were developed. The proposed measures can contribute to improving road safety and increasing the efficiency of light passenger vehicle operation under the road and climatic conditions of Uzbekistan.

title: Optimized Modeling and Evolutionary Control of Three-Phase Magnetic Resonance Wireless Power Transfer Chargers with Artificial Neural Network–Based State of Charge Estimation for Heavy-Duty Electric Vehicles
abstract: Wireless chargers for electric vehicles have recently attracted considerable attention from researchers and scientists, particularly due to their promising applications for high-power transfer, such as in heavy-duty vehicles, which are the backbone of transportation. This paper presents an innovative method for controlling a threephase magnetic resonance wireless power transfer charger using genetic algorithm optimization of parameters to ensure efficient wireless energy transfer. This control method, which operates exclusively on the primary side, regulates the battery current in the case of charging using the constant current-constant voltage method and also in the case of charging using the multi-step current method, which preserves the state of health of the battery. The state of charge (SOC) of the battery is estimated by neural networks, which ensure SOC estimation despite communication loss. The proposed control method is tested under several scenarios for a wireless power transmission of 20 kW with a resonance frequency of 85 kHz and an efficiency of 90.15%. The results obtained demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method for transferring wireless power to heavyduty vehicles despite misalignment between the coils and variation in the air gap, two frequent and disruptive phenomena in real-world situations.

title: Frequency-Spatial Decoupled State-Space Modeling with Transformer Fusion: A Robust YOLOv11 Framework for Autonomous Vehicle Perception
abstract: Abstract Visual environmental perception is the safety cornerstone of autonomous driving, yet robust vehicle detection remains challenging under intense glare, occlusion, and adverse weather. Although YOLOv11 provides an efficient baseline, it suffers from coupled frequency-spatial extraction and inadequate long-range dependency modeling, leading to misdetections of occluded or distant targets. To circumvent these bottlenecks, we propose a collaborative enhanced YOLOv11 framework integrating three innovative modules: a Frequency-Spatial Decoupled Feature Pyramid Network (FSD-FPN), a Visual Recursive State-Space Module (VRSSM), and a Multi-scale Attention Convolution-Transformer Block (MACTB). Specifically, FSD-FPN segregates high-frequency structural details from low-frequency semantic components to attenuate spectral noise induced by extreme illumination . The Mamba-based VRSSM establishes global contextual dependencies with linear complexity to reconstruct feature integrity for occluded vehicles , while MACTB synergizes local convolutional biases with global Transformer refinement to enhance multi-scale discriminative power . Empirical evaluations on the BDD100K and a self-curated Chengdu urban dataset demonstrate that our framework achieves a superior mean Average Precision (mAP)@0.5:0.95 of 70.9\% and an mAP@0.5 of 93.0\%, consistently outperforming YOLOv7, YOLOv10, vanilla…

title: BAMBOO FOREST LAND MANAGEMENT STRATEGY IN PENGLIPURAN VILLAGE, BANGLI REGENCY, BALI
abstract: This study examines a sustainable management strategy for bamboo forest land in Penglipuran Village, Bangli Regency, Bali, an area known for a well-preserved bamboo forest of approximately 44.8 hectares that holds important ecological, socio-cultural, and economic value for the local community. A qualitative descriptive approach was combined with a SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis, supported by Internal and External Factor Analysis Summary (IFAS/EFAS) scoring derived from a five-point Likertscale questionnaire administered to six key respondents representing local government, the community, and tourism management, complemented by field observation, interviews, and documentation study. The results indicate that internal strengths obtained an average score of 4.23 (very high), largely driven by the customary regulation of awig awig and mutual cooperation (gotong royong), while weaknesses reached 3.56 (high), mainly related to declining craftsman regeneration and suboptimal bamboo utilization. External opportunities scored 4.56 (very high), dominated by the growing trend of sustainable, local wisdom based tourism, whereas threats scored 4.11 (high), primarily arising from tourism pressure and land use change. Since strengths exceeded weaknesses and opportunities exceeded threats, the management condition falls within the Strength-Opportunity (SO) quadr…

title: Validation Strategy Dominates Model Choice in Chronological QSAR Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models are commonly evaluated by random cross-validation or random train-test splits, but these retrospective procedures may overestimate performance when validation compounds are structurally or temporally close to the training data. In this study, we examined whether this optimism is primarily explained by structural redundancy, chronological data set evolution, or the choice of machine-learning model. Fourteen public ChEMBL bioactivity data sets were curated as binary classification tasks. Five validation conditions were compared: random validation, chronological validation by publication year, a size-matched randomly thinned control, structural filtering of the random validation set, and structural filtering of the chronological validation set. Model development was deliberately held fixed within the random-derived and year-derived comparisons, so that the effect of validation-set composition could be assessed without simultaneously changing the training cohort. Four standard QSAR model classes─random forest, support vector machine, XGBoost, and a feed-forward neural network─were evaluated under the same training-only model-selection workflow. Random validation produced closely aligned internal and external estimates, with mean MCC values of 0.75 and 0.72, respectively, while random thinning gave essentially uncha…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Oficina pedagógica como estratégia para educação de profissionais em segurança do paciente na Atenção Primária à Saúde: relato de experiência em um programa de residência de Medicina de Família e Comunidade do município do Rio de Janeiro
abstract: Problema: O modelo de ecologia dos sistemas de saúde postula que a maioria dos atendimentos em saúde acontece fora dos hospitais. Apesar disso, no Brasil, as discussões sobre segurança do paciente permaneceram predominantemente limitadas à atenção hospitalar até meados de 2013. Um estudo estimou que cerca de 1,11% das consultas e procedimentos realizados na Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) incluíram algum tipo de incidente, corroborando a necessidade de ampliar as discussões sobre o tema na APS. Método: Trata-se de um relato de experiência da elaboração e condução de uma oficina educacional sobre segurança do paciente na APS, proposta por médicos residentes e realizada como atividade teórico-prática de um programa de residência em Medicina de Família e Comunidade, em uma Clínica da Família da Zona Norte do município do Rio de Janeiro. Resultados: Durante a atividade, foi realizada uma breve apresentação teórica com o objetivo de promover a sensibilização inicial para o tema, em que foram introduzidos o pensamento sistêmico e a metáfora da “casa” para facilitar a compreensão das barreiras de segurança em um serviço e a visualização do processo de construção social da APS. Utilizando-se do conceito, os autores adaptaram e conduziram uma oficina que estimulou a identificação de questões de segurança do paciente nos oito macroprocessos da APS. Dessa forma, os participantes puderam co…
venue: Revista Brasileira de Medicina de Família e Comunidade

title: Developing a Dual-Targeting CD33/CD70 CAR T-Cell Strategy Against Acute Myeloid Leukemia to Overcome Tumor Heterogeneity
abstract: Background: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains the deadliest form of leukemia in children and adults despite therapeutic advances in recent decades. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is one such therapeutic approach that has been explored preclinically and clinically in AML; however, its efficacy is limited by antigen heterogeneity. To overcome this roadblock, we propose a dual-targeting CAR T-cell strategy, targeting the AML-associated antigens CD33 and CD70. Methods: To recapitulate tumor heterogeneity, we genetically edited the AML cell line Molm-13 using CRISPR-Cas9 to generate distinct sublines, namely CD33+/CD70−, CD33−/CD70+, and CD33+/CD70+. Two dual-targeting CAR T-cell approaches were developed: a “pooled” product, in which CAR T cells directed towards CD33 or CD70 are combined and co-administered, and a “co-transduced” product, wherein one population of T cells is transduced with both CD33-CAR- and CD70-CAR-encoding viral vectors. Results: Pooled and co-transduced products demonstrated potent cytotoxicity against all Molm-13 populations, whereas single-antigen CAR approaches were not as effective when their respective target antigen was absent. Mice engrafted with CD33/CD70 heterogeneous Molm-13 cells were treated with pooled or co-transduced CD33/CD70 CAR T cells. Both groups exhibited a significant survival advantage over the untreated group, with th…

title: СТРАТЕГІЯ ФОРМУВАННЯ ЦИФРОВОЇ ЕКОСИСТЕМИ МЕДИЧНОЇ ОРГАНІЗАЦІЇ
abstract: The article substantiates a strategy for building a digital ecosystem of a healthcare organization as a set of long-term managerial decisions that align clinical processes, digital services, data flows and partner interactions. The study addresses a persistent gap between the adoption of individual information systems and the continuity of care across the patient journey. Its purpose is to develop a conceptual ecosystem architecture, an implementation sequence and an assessment framework at the organizational level. The research draws on a critical review of scholarly publications, structural and functional analysis, process modelling and comparison of managerial alternatives. A digital ecosystem is defined by coordinated patient pathways, agreed rules for data exchange, clear allocation of responsibilities and feedback on service outcomes, rather than by the number of applications deployed. The proposed architecture brings together service delivery, interoperable information flows, partner coordination and management analytics under cross-cutting requirements for data protection and staff capability. An original decision matrix relates strategic priorities to organizational prerequisites and implementation risks. The evaluation framework includes access to care, continuity, completeness of records, processing time, patient experience and response to security incidents. The imp…

title: Essential Retail Pharmacies Under the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026
abstract: This cross-sectional study investigates the distribution and characteristics of essential retail pharmacies (ERPs) designated by the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 and considers policy amendments to ensure patient access to ERPs is protected.

title: Examining Critical Drivers of Customer Satisfaction and Retention in Contemporary Retail Stores in Padang, Indonesia
abstract: The rapid expansion of modern retail formats has reshaped competition in Indonesia, compelling retailers to strengthen service performance and refine their marketing strategies to maintain customer engagement. Within this context, the present study examines how key retail attributes shape customer satisfaction and, subsequently, customer retention. A survey of 230 shoppers at Budiman Swalayan in Padang, Indonesia, was analyzed using SEM-PLS. The findings reveal that service quality, price fairness, store atmosphere, and membership cards significantly enhance customer satisfaction. Furthermore, price fairness, store atmosphere, and satisfaction have a positive influence on customer retention, whereas service quality and membership cards do not directly predict retention. The analysis also reveals that customer satisfaction serves as a mediating mechanism, linking all four predictors to customer retention.

title: Strategic resource allocation through route optimization: Enhancing operational efficiency and competitive advantage in distribution operations
abstract: This research addresses the optimization of distribution routes to reduce transportation costs in an ice cream company in Chepén, Peru, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12 (Responsible Production and Consumption). The study employed an applied, quantitative, pre-experimental design with an explanatory scope. The population consisted of one year’s distribution records, with a sample of eight weeks. Data collection used documentary analysis through standardized forms. An Ishikawa diagram identified 13 root causes of high transportation costs, with the Pareto principle prioritizing nine causes representing 79.78 percent of the total impact. The main cause identified was non-optimized routes. Using the traveling salesman problem (TSP) model with Miller-Tucker-Zemlin (MTZ) restrictions implemented in Excel Solver, routes were optimized by merging and reconfiguring paths. Results showed an 18.14 percent reduction in average weekly transportation costs (from S/7,365.47 to S/6,029.51), with annual savings estimated at S/69,500. The Student’s t-test confirmed the statistical significance of this improvement (p < 0.05). This research demonstrates that route optimization through linear programming significantly contributes to reducing operational costs while promoting sustainable resource use by minimizing fuel consumption, tire wear, and carbon emissions. These findings a…

title: Pengaruh Preferensi Risiko Eksekutif, Kepemilikan Asing dan Transfer Pricing terhadap Tax Avoidance
abstract: This study aims to identify and present empirical evidence regarding the influence of executive risk preferences, foreign ownership, and transfer pricing on tax avoidance in basic materials sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2020-2024. This study involved 13 companies with a research period of 5 years resulting in 65 observational data, this data was selected using purposive sampling based on certain criteria. The data used is secondary data in the form of company annual reports obtained from the official IDX website. Using analysis including descriptive statistics, panel data regression models, panel regression model selection, hypothesis testing, coefficient of determination, partial t-tests, and simultaneous F-tests. The results of the study indicate that the three variables of executive risk preferences, foreign ownership, and transfer pricing have an effect on tax avoidance. However, partially, executive risk preferences have no effect on tax avoidance, foreign ownership has an effect on tax avoidance, and transfer pricing has no effect on tax avoidance.

title: Between public space and private living: social infrastructure as a demand-side strategy for compact living
abstract: Abstract Cities must balance the housing needs of growing populations with planetary boundaries. Technological improvements alone cannot meet climate targets, and demand-side strategies that reduce private dwelling size are critical for achieving absolute reductions in material and energy demand. However, the socio-spatial conditions that enable compact living remain poorly understood. Prior theoretical work suggests that social infrastructure, including cafés, parks, libraries, and community centres, can reduce demand for private residential space, but empirical evidence linking social infrastructure to dwelling size has been virtually absent. We address this gap through a large-scale, neighbourhood-level analysis across Vancouver, Toronto, and Montréal, Canada. Using Google Places data linked with census indicators, we estimated spatial error models to examine the association between social infrastructure and dwelling size. Across all three cities, greater access to social infrastructure was associated with smaller dwellings, independent of income, household size, and population density (β = −0.210 Toronto; −0.138 Vancouver; −0.091 Montréal). To account for differences in urban form, we further clustered neighbourhoods into built-form typologies, enabling comparisons among similar neighbourhoods. The relationship remained significant across most typologies within each ci…

title: Pengaruh Karakter Eksekutif dan Transfer Pricing terhadap Penghindaran Pajak Dimoderasi oleh Umur Perusahaan
abstract: Tax avoidance is a strategy frequently employed by companies to reduce their tax burden; however, the determinants of this practice remain inconclusive in the literature. This study aims to examine the effects of executive characteristics and transfer pricing on tax avoidance, with firm age serving as a moderating variable, in mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2021–2025 period. The study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data collected through purposive sampling, resulting in 90 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The findings indicate that executive characteristics and transfer pricing have no significant effect on tax avoidance, and firm age does not moderate the relationship between executive characteristics or transfer pricing and tax avoidance. However, firm age has a positive and significant effect on the Cash Effective Tax Rate (CETR), suggesting that older firms tend to exhibit lower levels of tax avoidance. These findings imply that firm age plays a more substantial role as a direct determinant of tax compliance than as a moderating variable. This study contributes to the empirical literature on the determinants of tax avoidance and provides insights for regulators in understanding the factors influencing tax avoidance practices in Indonesia'…

title: Cellulose-Based Wet Wipes Combining Essential Oils and Sodium Hypochlorite: A Sustainable Strategy for Bacterial Control
abstract: The development of antimicrobial formulations for biodegradable wet wipes is of increasing interest for more sustainable hygiene applications. Objectives: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a cellulose-based antimicrobial wipe formulation by combining sodium hypochlorite with essential oils from Cymbopogon citratus (lemongrass), Lavandula officinalis (lavender), and Syzygium aromaticum (clove). The formulation was designed to incorporate sodium hypochlorite and essential oils into a cellulose matrix and to evaluate whether their combination could enhance antibacterial efficacy through synergistic interactions. Methods: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy with attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR) was used as a complementary qualitative method to characterize the essential oils and to assess spectral changes following their incorporation into the cellulose-based wipe substrate. Antibacterial activity was evaluated against Gram-positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 and Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC 12228, and Gram-negative bacteria Escherichia coli ATCC 8739 and Salmonella enteritidis ATCC 13076 following CLSI guidelines, while combined interactions were assessed using the checkerboard assay. Results: FTIR-ATR analysis revealed characteristic spectral features of the investigated essential oils and detectable spectral changes following their incorporati…

title: A observação de aulas de Matemática como estratégia formativa na disciplina de Didática na formação inicial docente
abstract: Initial teacher education involves the articulation between theoretical knowledge and practical experiences that allow pre-service teachers to better understand the reality of the teaching profession. In this context, classroom observation plays an important role in professional development, as it enables future teachers to become familiar with the school environment, analyze pedagogical strategies, and reflect on the interactions that occur in the teaching and learning process. Thus, this study aimed to analyze the practice of a Mathematics teacher in basic education, seeking to understand how teaching strategies, content approach, and classroom interactions contribute to the development of the professional perspective of the pre-service teacher. To achieve this objective, a classroom observation was conducted in a 6th grade class of a public school located in the interior of the state of Ceará, Brazil, composed of approximately 30 students. The observation took place from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. and focused on the organization of the lesson, the teaching strategies adopted, the pedagogical resources used, and student participation. The topic addressed in the lesson was decimal numbers, initially introduced through everyday examples, followed by theoretical explanation and practical activities. During the class, the teacher used resources such as a whiteboard, a textbook, ruler…

A Microclimate Testing and Improvement Strategy for Transitional Spatial Forms of Traditional Dwellings in the Hot-Summer Regions of China: The Case of Ningbo
abstract: This study investigates climate adaptation for the transitional spatial forms of traditional dwellings in Ningbo, China, a region characterized by hot summers and cold winters. The study focuses on identifying and classifying different forms of transitional spaces in Ningbo’s traditional dwellings and analyzing their microclimatic adjustment capabilities. Four representative traditional dwellings were selected for on-site microclimate measurements, covering analyses of temperature, humidity and wind speed data for different transitional spaces. The study used ENVI-met 5.7.1 software to simulate and assess the thermal comfort of these spaces and proposed design-improvement strategies. The results show that cold alleys exhibit the most effective cooling due to their enclosed structure, followed by corridors and patios. Based on the simulation results, targeted design strategies are proposed, and their measures successfully improve the thermal comfort performance of the transitional spaces to better adapt the traditional dwellings to modern living needs, providing a useful reference for the conservation and modernization of traditional dwellings in Ningbo, and promoting sustainable building practices in hot-summer and cold-winter regions.

title: Intelligent Inversion and Calibration Parameter Uncertainty Quantification Method for Microwave Probe S Parameters
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of microwave and radio frequency technology, precise on-chip S-parameter measurement is constrained by non ideal standard components, probe crosstalk, and residual nonlinear errors in the millimeter wave frequency band. A intrinsic on-chip calibration process has been proposed. This process combines an open/short circuit de embedding model for crosstalk perception, a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) for residual error inversion, and a semi naive Bayesian network for probabilistic error compensation. The Bayesian stage generates a posterior distribution on the discretized residual error categories. The posterior mean is used for continuous compensation, while the posterior quantile provides the prediction interval. On the independent test set, the amplitude mean absolute error (MAE) of the complete process reached 0.061 ± 0.003 dB, and the phase root mean square error (RMSE) was 1.43 ± 0.07 °, while the traditional open/short circuit de embedding methods were 0.105 ± 0.005 dB and 3.46 ± 0.12 °, respectively. For the nominal 90% interval, the predicted interval coverage probability is 91.2%, and the expected calibration error is 0.024. In 500 engineering evaluations, the average end-to-end inference time was 0.91 ms per sample. The contribution lies in the system level integration of physically driven de embedding, nonlinear inversion, and…

title: Still in Place: Clinical Uncertainty in Intercostal Catheter Removal After Trauma
A Physics-Guided Statistical Framework for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Under Unit Variability and Rotational Speed Uncertainty
abstract: Reliable bearing fault diagnosis must differentiate between defects and normal-operation-condition variation. The predictor must remain accurate when shaft speed is uncertain. Conventional accuracy-driven models often ignore false-positive rates and fail to accurately locate faults on unseen bearings’ data. This study proposes a physics-guided statistical framework that integrates resolution-based order screening, envelope peak-to-floor evidence, search- and collision-matched empirical nulls, and conformal calibration against healthy reference data. A two-stage bearing-level rule detects abnormal operation before localizing the dominant fault order. Evaluation comprised controlled simulations, unit-disjoint Paderborn experiments, and a prospectively frozen external test using the University of Ottawa Rolling-Element Dataset: Vibration and Acoustic Faults under Constant Load and Speed Conditions (UORED-VAFCLS). In simulation, family-wise false-positive rates were 2.58% and 3.12% for the two bearing geometries; detection power reached 83.3–93.8% at −4 dB and 98.3–100% at 0 dB, satisfying all registered criteria. On Paderborn, the overall false-positive rate was 7.08%, but condition-specific false alarms reached 17.5%; inner- and outer-race detection reached only 49.8% and 71.5%, despite high localization accuracy. On UORED-VAFCLS, the healthy false-alarm rate remained 5% (1/20 be…

title: Reducing Alzheimer’s diagnostic uncertainty with a sequential plasma p-tau217 workflow in real-world memory clinic practice
abstract: Abstract Background Plasma p-tau217 and p-tau217/Aβ42 show high accuracy for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) amyloid pathology and are entering specialist clinical workflows, with standalone p-tau217 CE-IVDR marked in Europe and the p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio FDA-cleared in the United States. Their optimal integration into uncertainty-aware diagnostic pathways, particularly for patients near decision thresholds, remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 562 consecutive memory-clinic patients assessed between October 2023 and April 2026. Core1 amyloid status was defined using CSF biomarkers and/or amyloid-PET according to the 2024 Alzheimer’s Association Revised Criteria. Plasma biomarkers were measured on the Lumipulse G600II platform. We compared three two-threshold workflows: p-tau217 alone; p-tau217/Aβ42 as a universal upfront ratio; and a p-tau217-first sequential workflow in which p-tau217/Aβ42 was used only for patients with intermediate p-tau217 results. Rule-out and rule-in thresholds were selected to achieve ≥ 95% sensitivity and ≥ 95% specificity, respectively. A reverse sequential workflow and internal temporal validation were used as sensitivity analyses. Results Core1 + prevalence was 71.2% ( n = 400). P-tau217 achieved an AUC of 0.935 (95%CI 0.908–0.962), outperforming p-tau181 (0.826), Aβ42/Aβ40 (0.797), GFAP (0.789) and NfL (0.566; all p < 0.001). The p-tau217 two-…

title: Optimization of the Performance of Zirconia-Toughened and Mixed-Alumina Ceramic Tools in CNC Turning of 42CrMo4 Steel
abstract: This article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the performance of zirconia-toughened and mixed-alumina ceramic tools in CNC turning of 42CrMo4 steel with hardnesses of 35, 40, and 45 HRC. Empirical models have been developed for the cutting tool lifetime and the surface roughness of the machined surfaces as a function of cutting speed and hardness of the machined material. Through multi-objective compromise optimization via two approaches (the optimal compromise region and the generalized arithmetic mean utility function with weighting coefficients) and the application of a genetic algorithm, the optimal conditions for performing the CNC turning process were determined when using tools made of different mineral ceramics for steel with varying hardness. These conditions provide a tool lifetime exceeding 8 min and a high machined surface quality with a roughness below 1.7 µm.

title: Deepfake Image Detection Using Squeeze-and-Excitation Attention and Adaptive Threshold Optimization
abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has significantly improved the realism of manipulated facial images and videos, creating serious risks for social-network misinformation, content security, and digital trust. This study focuses on visual deepfake image detection rather than multimodal misinformation detection. Existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deepfake detectors commonly rely on a fixed decision threshold of 0.5, which may be unstable when facial images are affected by compression, cropping, noise, and distribution shifts in practical social-media environments. To improve detection reliability, this paper proposes a lightweight deepfake image detection framework that integrates a CNN backbone, a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention module, and an adaptive threshold optimization strategy. The key novelty of this work is not conventional threshold tuning alone, but a lightweight detection framework that jointly combines SE-based channel-wise feature recalibration, F1-score-driven adaptive threshold optimization, and leakage-aware group-level evaluation. Compared with post-hoc threshold tuning or calibration methods that mainly adjust the output boundary after training, the proposed framework improves both forgery-sensitive feature representation and the final classification decision mechanism. Specifically, the SE module enhances forgery-related fe…
