title: Machine learning guided optimization of water management options with a physical groundwater model for the Mid-County Basin optimization study
abstract: The Santa Cruz Mid-County Basin Groundwater Sustainability Agency conducted a Regional Water Optimization Study to support the selection of water supply projects and management actions within the critically overdrafted Santa Cruz Mid-County Groundwater Basin, for long-term operations and shared regional benefits including sustainable groundwater management and regional water supply needs. To support this objective, the Study utilized an integrated groundwater surface-water flow (GSFLOW) model of the Basin and surrounding areas to simulate water supply projects and management actions into the future (water year 2023 to 2075), covering the sustainability planning horizon under California’s Sustainable Groundwater Management Act. Water supply projects and management actions considered under this study include aquifer storage and recovery, indirect potable reuse, and interagency transfers. Many different implementations are possible for each type of project, such that the number of potential project configurations is practically endless. To facilitate optimization, we developed a novel workflow utilizing machine learning algorithms to conduct optimization by autonomously designing, preprocessing, post-processing, and evaluating physical model scenarios, which we call Machine Learning Guided Optimization (MLGO). MLGO improved project configurations within a complex system by generat…

title: Optimization of Biogenic Silver Nanoparticle Synthesis Using UV–Visible Spectroscopy from a Bacterial Strain Isolated from Coastal River Sediments
abstract: Abstract Microorganisms living in river sediments can reduce metal ions and produce nanoparticles through environmentally friendly processes. We aseptically collected sediment samples, serially diluted them, and cultured them to obtain morphologically diverse bacterial strains. The bacterial supernatants were then reacted with AgNo3, and the presence of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) was verified by observing a yellowish-brown colour and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) peaks in the range of 350-450 nm. 16S rRNA gene sequencing identified the most efficient strain, which was deposited in the NCBI GenBank database (PQ436520) as Bacillus altitudinis. The synthesis of AgNPs was optimized by changing the pH, temperature, agitation, nutrient sources, C:N ratio, salinity, and reaction time in a one factor at a time approach. Peak production occurred at 96 h, corresponding to peak biomass. Best reaction time was 24 hours, best pH 8, best temperature 35 °C, best rpm 150, best glucose concentration 1%, best yeast extract concentration 0.5%, best salinity 20 ppt, and best reaction time 24 hours. DLS analysis showed uniform AgNPs ranging from 23–72 nm and a low PDI (0.03–0.11), indicating that B. altitudinis can be used for sustainable green nanotechnology.
venue: Advances in Natural Sciences: Nanoscience and Nanotechnology

title: Penguin Species Classification using Backpropagation Neural Network : An Empirical Study of Learning Rate and Mini-Batch Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract: This paper presents an empirical study of a fullyconnectedfeedforward neural network, trained with the classicalbackpropagation algorithm, applied to the task of classifyingpenguin species from morphological measurements. Using thePalmer Archipelago (Antarctica) penguin dataset, a compact4–4–3 network is implemented from first principles in anobject-oriented MATLAB framework and trained with minibatchstochastic gradient descent (SGD). Rather than restatingthe results of the original design report, the present workre-implements the network and reproduces the experimentsindependently in Python on the same underlying data, so thatthe reported numbers are directly verifiable. Two questions areinvestigated in detail: (i) how the learning rate η affects testaccuracy over 10 and 50 training epochs, and (ii) whethermini-batch SGD offers a measurable advantage over full-batchgradient descent on a dataset of this size. The results show thatclassification accuracy exceeds 98% for a broad range of learningrates (1 ≤ η ≤ 20), that excessively small or large learningrates cause underfitting or divergence respectively, and that minibatchSGD yields a statistically clearer and more consistentconvergence at low epoch counts than full-batch descent, althoughthe two methods converge to comparable accuracy once trainingis allowed to proceed for 100 epochs. These findings are discussedin the context…

title: Integrated Ovarian circRNA, miRNA and mRNA Profiling Identifies Candidate ceRNA Relationships Associated with Late-Laying and Nesting Stages in Wanxi White Geese
abstract: Background: The pronounced broodiness of Wanxi white geese is associated with rapid ovarian regression and reduced egg production and reproductive efficiency. However, the extent to which circRNAs influence this physiological transition by coordinating ceRNA interactions is not yet well understood. Methods: Here, we generated ovarian microRNA (miRNA) and circRNA expression profiles by RNA sequencing in late-laying (LLG) and nesting (NG) Wanxi white geese and measured serum reproductive hormones. Results: Compared with the late-laying stage, the nesting stage was characterised by pronounced ovarian atrophy. Serum concentrations of oestradiol (E2), progesterone (P4) and luteinising hormone (LH) were lower, whereas the prolactin (PRL) concentration was higher. Transcriptome analysis identified 156 circRNAs and 64 miRNAs that met the nominal differential expressed (DE) criteria. Enrichment analysis associated genes giving rise to DE circRNAs with membrane and junctional structures, cell adhesion, small GTPase regulation, ECM–receptor interaction, adherens junction, focal adhesion and metabolic processes. Conversely, putative targets of DE miRNAs were linked to AMPK, mTOR, TGF-β and Hippo pathways, together with oocyte meiosis. The integration of the RNA datasets and Pearson correlation analysis highlighted several putative ceRNA relationships associated with ovarian functional tran…

title: Spatial variability of TEC perturbations and ROTI during the 3 october 2024 X9.0 solar flare: a multi-station GNSS analysis
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the spatially heterogeneous low-latitude ionospheric response to the 3 October 2024 X9.0 solar flare using GNSS observations from seven equatorial and low-latitude stations. TEC, quiet-time differential TEC ( $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ ), and ROTI were analyzed under relatively quiet geomagnetic conditions ( $$K_p=1$$ –3). The flare peaked at 12:18 UT, and comparison with quiet-time conditions revealed $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ perturbations of approximately 6–14% at several stations, with pronounced spatial differences. YKRO showed the largest positive perturbation at the flare peak, reaching 12.75 TECU (14.21%), whereas MBAR and CUSV exhibited negative perturbations of $$-10.98$$ TECU ( $$-10.77\%$$ ) and $$-6.14$$ TECU ( $$-9.29\%$$ ), respectively. However, substantial and sometimes larger $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ variations occurred outside the flare interval, indicating that their magnitude alone cannot establish a flare-driven response. ROTI remained generally below 0.04 TECU min $$^{-1}$$ during the flare, with stronger irregularity activity occurring predominantly after sunset. The results indicate a measurable and spatially heterogeneous ionospheric response temporally associated with the X9.0 flare, while highlighting the substantial contribution of intrinsic low-latitude variability. These findings emphasize the importance of multi-station…

title: Why East Asia's Financial Safety Net Remains Unused: From Reserve Adequacy to Liquidity Usability
abstract: ABSTRACT East Asia has built one of the world's largest regional financial safety nets, but the Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralisation (CMIM) has never been activated. This policy analysis argues that financial scale alone cannot explain this record. What matters is liquidity usability: Governments must be willing to request support, and the arrangement must be able to deliver it quickly and predictably. On the request side, the IMF link, the market signal associated with seeking assistance and access to bilateral swaps may make CMIM use politically costly. On the delivery side, contingent commitments, collective decision‐making, domestic authorisation requirements and untested procedures create uncertainty over timely disbursement. Reform must therefore address both sides. Confidential consultation, clearer communication, stronger AMRO capacity, legal preparedness, operational testing, coordination across safety‐net instruments and gradual resource pooling should proceed together. CMIM will become credible only when its liquidity is politically acceptable to request and operationally feasible to deliver during a crisis.

title: Reconceptualising the Right to Freedom of Expression in Nigeria's Digital Environment
abstract: The widespread emergence of digital technology has greatly changed the nature of freedom of expression by redefining how opinions are generated, disseminated, and contested within the public domain. Although freedom of expression is guaranteed under the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), the growth of social media platforms and State control practices have created a complex regulatory and constitutional conundrum. This article examines freedom of expression as it operates within Nigeria’s digitally mediated public sphere, assessing whether existing constitutional safeguards remain adequate to address the contemporary challenges posed by digital innovation. It explores the relationship between constitutional speech rights and regulatory measures such as the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act and other policy instruments regulating online expression. Through doctrinal and comparative legal analysis, the article posits that current regulatory approaches, if not properly applied, may decimate democratic engagement and frustrate legitimate expression. It therefore advocates a constitutionally grounded, proportionate, and rights-oriented framework for the regulation of speech, which reconciles the protection of fundamental freedoms with the State’s legitimate interests in security, public order, and the management of harmful online content…

title: Financial Effects of an Out-of-Pocket Cap in Traditional Medicare
abstract: Importance Traditional Medicare (TM) exposes beneficiaries to substantial financial risk because, unlike Medicare Advantage (MA), there is no out-of-pocket (OOP) maximum for medical spending. Policymakers have proposed introducing an OOP cap, but its fiscal and behavioral effects are uncertain. Objective To estimate the financial impacts of introducing OOP spending caps of $3000, $5000, or $10 000 annually in TM on beneficiary costs, enrollment patterns, and Centers for Medicare &amp; Medicaid Services expenditures between 2026 and 2034. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation using principles of microsimulation analysis projected enrollment, spending, and health care use outcomes under baseline (no OOP cap) and 3 alternative cap scenarios using publicly available national Medicare and insurance data from 2020 to 2024 with projections through 2034. The model incorporated elasticity-based behavioral responses, including beneficiary switching between TM and MA, changes in service use, and increases to MA benchmarks and spending. Sensitivity analyses varied model assumptions probabilistically. Exposure Introduction of annual OOP caps for Parts A and B in TM at $3000, $5000, or $10 000. Main Outcomes and Measures Projected changes in beneficiary enrollment by coverage type, mean annual beneficiary OOP and premium spending, and annual Medicare expenditures. Re…

title: Sostenibilidad ESG y rentabilidad financiera en cuatro grandes empresas de la minería del cobre chilena: evidencia correlacional desagregada por empresa y el modelo conceptual ISVM
abstract: Objetivo: analizar empíricamente la relación entre la madurez en criterios ambientales, sociales y de gobernanza (ESG), reportada bajo estándares SASB para el sector EM-MM, y la rentabilidad financiera, medida a través del ROE, el ROA y el margen EBITDA, en las cuatro principales empresas de la gran minería del cobre en Chile durante el periodo 2021-2025. Metodología: se empleó un enfoque cuantitativo, no experimental, longitudinal y descriptivo-correlacional, basado en estados financieros auditados bajo NIIF y reportes de sostenibilidad SASB. Se calculó la correlación de Pearson entre el score anual de madurez en ESG y los indicadores de rentabilidad, y se estimó una regresión múltiple del ROE en función de la madurez en ESG y el precio del cobre. La robustez se verificó mediante correlaciones de Spearman y Kendall y un análisis leave-one-out. Resultados: se identificaron relaciones positivas relevantes en Escondida (r ≈ 0,92) y Codelco (r ≈ 0,78), cuyos incrementos del ROE fueron de 13,7 y 21,1 puntos porcentuales, respectivamente. Anglo American Sur presentó correlaciones positivas débiles (r ≈ 0,28-0,45). Originalidad/valor: se propone el modelo de inversión sostenible y creación de valor en minería, sustentado en evidencia exploratoria. Implicancias prácticas: los hallazgos orientan a reguladores y gestores hacia la estandarización del reporte SASB, la incorporación de mét…

title: LIBRAS E DIREITO À EDUCAÇÃO DE ESTUDANTES SURDOS: ENTRE A EDUCAÇÃO INCLUSIVA E A EDUCAÇÃO BILÍNGUE
abstract: O presente artigo analisa o papel da Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) na garantia do direito à educação de estudantes surdos, distinguindo sua função de acessibilidade comunicacional de sua condição de língua de instrução na Educação Bilíngue de Surdos. Trata-se de revisão narrativa, de abordagem qualitativa, fundamentada em pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, com levantamento realizado nas bases SciELO, Portal de Periódicos da Capes e Google Acadêmico. O estudo parte da distinção introduzida pela Lei nº 14.191/2021, que reconhece a Educação Bilíngue de Surdos como modalidade escolar própria, ofertada em Libras como primeira língua e em português escrito como segunda língua, e analisa essa distinção à luz da Constituição Federal de 1988, da Convenção Internacional sobre os Direitos das Pessoas com Deficiência, da Lei Brasileira de Inclusão e do novo Plano Nacional de Educação, instituído pela Lei nº 15.388/2026. Os resultados indicam que a legislação brasileira oferece fundamentos consistentes para tratar a Libras como direito linguístico educacional, e não apenas como recurso de acessibilidade, mas que sua efetivação depende de condições institucionais, como a formação de professores bilíngues, a diferenciação entre a função do professor e a do tradutor intérprete, a produção de materiais didáticos e a participação da comunidade surda na formulação das políticas educacion…

title: Fair Learning Environment and Financial Well-Being as Resources for Students’ Academic Engagement: Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction as a Common Motivational Pathway
abstract: Academic engagement is associated with the resources available to students, yet it remains unclear through which psychological processes resources of different origins are related to academic engagement. Bringing together Basic Psychological Needs Theory and the Study Demands–Resources framework, this study examined whether autonomy, relatedness, and competence satisfaction mediate the associations of an institutional resource, a fair learning environment, and a resource rooted outside the academic environment, subjective financial well-being, with academic engagement. The measures were first evaluated using data from 278 university students. The structural model, specifying the three needs as parallel mediators, was then tested in a subsequent, non-overlapping sample of 741 students in Türkiye. Both resources positively predicted all three need satisfaction dimensions, whereas academic engagement was predicted only by autonomy (β = 0.43) and competence satisfaction (β = 0.36); relatedness satisfaction made no significant unique contribution. Neither resource was directly associated with academic engagement. The total indirect effects were β = 0.31 for a fair learning environment and β = 0.13 for subjective financial well-being. The model explained 47.4% of the variance in academic engagement. Resources of different origin were indirectly associated with academic engagement thr…

CEO Overconfidence, Debt Policy, and Financial Condition: The Moderating Role of Family Ownership in Indonesian Manufacturing Firms
abstract: Financial condition is central to corporate sustainability, yet evidence on whether family ownership conditions the relationships of CEO overconfidence and debt policy with financial condition remains limited, particularly in Indonesian manufacturing firms. This study addresses this gap by positioning family ownership as a boundary condition. From 850 firm-year observations of Indonesian listed manufacturing firms during 2020-2024, 822 observations remained after residual-based screening and were analyzed using multiple and moderated regressions. Financial condition was measured using the MFA Score, with the Altman Z-score as an alternative. CEO overconfidence and debt policy are negatively associated with financial condition, while family ownership attenuates both relationships. The former remains significant across ownership levels, whereas the latter becomes insignificant at high family ownership. Results remain consistent across the full sample, alternative outcome and CEO-overconfidence measures. Two-way fixed-effects estimates support H1-H3, while H4 shows limited robustness. The study identifies family ownership as a boundary condition in managerial-behavioural and financing pathways to financial condition.

title: ​Financial Feasibility of the Crispy Mushroom Business at CV FCK Corporation, Kediri Regency
abstract: This study analyzed the financial feasibility and sensitivity of the FCK Crispy Mushroom business at CV FCK Corporation, Kediri Regency, East Java. A quantitative case study used primary and secondary data from observation, interviews with four purposively selected key informants, and documentation during May–June 2026, feasibility was assessed using Net Present Value (NPV), Net Benefit-Cost Ratio (Net B/C), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and payback period, complemented by a switching-value sensitivity analysis on raw material cost and marketplace administration fees. Revenue fell 7.29% in 2025 after a 30% rise in oyster mushroom prices, yet the business remained feasible, with an NPV of IDR160,665,235, a Net B/C of 1.118, an IRR of 58%, and a payback period of 1.68 years, and stayed feasible up to a 29% rise in raw material cost and a 17% rise in marketplace fees. The business is financially feasible, though more sensitive to marketplace fees than to raw material cost. Findings rely on a single case company and four informants, therefore, they cannot be generalized. This study extends the feasibility literature on oyster mushroom agroindustry by incorporating marketplace administration fees into the switching-value sensitivity analysis.

TEMPERATURE FIELD ANALYSIS OF PLANETARY GEAR TRANSMISSION SYSTEM IN WIND TURBINES
abstract: Abstract To improve the prediction accuracy of thermal behavior in wind turbine planetary gear transmission systems, a dynamic thermal analysis method is proposed. Unlike existing studies that mainly consider gear meshing heat, the proposed approach simultaneously incorporates gear friction, bearing friction, heat dissipation, and surface roughness into a unified thermal model. A 21-degree-of-freedom dynamic model is established to calculate the frictional heat generation, and the transient temperature field is obtained using finite element analysis. Experimental validation on a gearbox test rig demonstrates good agreement between the numerical and measured temperatures. The results show that bearing friction has a significant influence on the system temperature distribution. In addition, the temperature rise increases logarithmically with surface roughness and approximately linearly with load under high-speed operating conditions. The proposed method provides a more comprehensive thermal analysis framework for planetary gear transmission systems.

title: Preliminary Synthesis and Basic Performance Characterization of Bio-Based Composite Materials Using Starch and Gelatin as Representative Matrix Phases: Exploratory Conceptual Design for Sustainable Toy Scenarios
abstract: The overconsumption of traditional plastic products causes serious white pollution and ecological pressure. Bio-based composites derived from natural polymers have emerged as promising sustainable alternatives. This work preliminarily fabricates starch- and gelatin-based composite films modified with natural fillers, and characterizes their basic physicochemical properties, dyeing performance, mechanical behavior, soil burial mass loss, and seed germination responses. On the basis of the tested baseline properties, tentative conceptual design schemes for eco-friendly toys were proposed. Notably, all experimental results in this work are preliminary and limited by insufficient experimental replicates. This study provides only basic experimental data and preliminary feasibility references for developing natural polymer composites for low-carbon consumer product scenarios.

title: Investigation on Hot-Carrier Injection Mechanisms and Reliability Design-Based Strategies in Cryogenically Operated CMOS ROICs for Infrared Focal Plane Arrays
abstract: Cryogenic operation of CMOS read-out integrated circuits (ROICs) is essential for high-performance infrared focal plane arrays but significantly affects carrier transport and device reliability. This work investigates hot-carrier injection (HCI) mechanisms in 180 nm NMOS transistors operating from room temperature down to 140 K. Electrical characterization and accelerated stress measurements reveal a strong impact of hot-carrier effects at low temperatures, resulting in increased degradation of device characteristics, particularly under channel hot-electron (CHE) and drain avalanche hot carrier (DAHC) stress conditions. Time-to-failure modeling confirms accelerated degradation kinetics while validating conventional substrate-current-based reliability methodologies at cryogenic temperatures. Geometry-based design strategies, notably gate-length optimization, are proposed to mitigate cryogenic HCI effects, enabling an improved performance–reliability trade-off. These results provide key guidelines for design reliability of cryogenic CMOS ROICs for infrared imaging applications.

Achieving Flexible Operation by Aggregating Structured Operating Protocols: An Electrolysis Case Study Using Real Market Data
abstract: Electrochemical devices can play a critical role in providing demand-side flexibility to the power grid, enabling greater integration of renewable power and enhancing system resilience. However, highly dynamic operation that tracks fluctuating market signals can accelerate degradation. To address this challenge, this work proposes a parallel aggregation framework in which multiple device modules operate under predefined structured protocols, defined as stable and periodic operating patterns assigned to individual units. Using a hydrogen electrolysis system participating in the real-time electricity market operated by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) as a case study, we develop an optimization framework that determines optimal mixing of predefined structured protocols that minimizes total electricity costs. Our results show that the cost of the protocol-based parallel setting closely approximates that of fully flexible operation. This trend is consistently observed across multiple protocol sets and different market days, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed concept. The proposed approach can also enhance predictability and practical implementation.

title: Application of Hedonic Regression Model and Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) in Land Price Assessment for Paddy Land in the Urbanization Area of Hue City
abstract: Urbanization causes rapid fluctuations in rice paddy land prices, leading to risks of inaccurate valuation in compensation, land-use conversion, and sustainable land management. This study compares the Hedonic model (OLS) and the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) in valuing rice paddy land in Thuy Thanh commune (Hue city) based on a survey of 454 land parcels. The results of the OLS model (adjusted R² = 0.796) show that significant influencing factors include: project information (strongest influence), enterprise compensation policies, soil fertility, and yield. Meanwhile, the SDM model (Pseudo R² = 0.8667) shows that in addition to the impact of factors within the land parcel, there is also a spillover effect from the surrounding area, confirming the role of spatial autocorrelation in land valuation in urbanizing areas. Overall, the SDM model yields more suitable results when it comes to reflecting spatial impacts, thereby providing a scientific basis for improving the valuation of rice land in a scientific and equitable manner.

title: Evaluating Trend Representation and Accuracy in Monthly Electricity Grey Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of monthly electricity consumption is important for energy planning, demand management, and policy making. This study evaluates five selected grey forecasting models for monthly electricity consumption in Australia, focusing on both trend representation and forecast accuracy. Data on monthly electricity consumption from January 2019 to December 2024 were used, with 80% of the observations covering 2019-2023 assigned to training and the remaining 20% covering January-December 2024 for testing. Five grey models were evaluated: GM(1,1), FGM(1,1), FHGM(1,1), NBGM(1,1), and WBGM(1,1), using MAPE and RMSE as performance criteria. The results show that GM, FGM, FHGM, and NBGM achieved similar training accuracy, with MAPE values of approximately 4.18-4.19%, while WBGM recorded a higher training MAPE of 4.80%. However, in the testing stage, WBGM achieved the best forecasting performance, with the lowest MAPE of 4.23%, and RMSE of 1063.06. In contrast, the other models recorded higher testing MAPE values ranging from 5.28% to 5.41%. These results highlight that while WBGM is less competitive in the training process, it performs better in testing performance forecasting and offers a better understanding of future monthly electricity consumption. The study highlights the importance of evaluating grey forecasting models not only by in-sample fitting accuracy but also by…

title: Scheduling and Dynamic Energy Optimization in Cement Mills
abstract: Background/Aim: This study aims to address energy consumption challenges in cement milling operations by developing an integrated framework that incorporates production uncertainties and inventory management efficiency. The main objective is to minimize energy costs while improving production planning and environmental sustainability.Methods: In this context, statistical and machine learning techniques, including Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), are employed for electricity price forecasting. Based on the forecasting results, a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is developed to optimize production scheduling and energy consumption. The proposed framework incorporates forecasted electricity-price fluctuations into production scheduling to generate cost-oriented production plans while satisfying operational constraints.Results: Among the forecasting methods, the LSTM model demonstrates superior performance with the lowest error rates. abstract: Introduction Player market value is a key indicator of a professional football player’s sporting and economic worth, yet how injury characteristics relate to the change in valuation after an injury remains poorly understood. Methods This retrospective cohort study examined the association between injury characteristics and the pre- to post-injury change in market value using Transfermarkt data. The cohort comprised the complete injury histories (July 2008 to August 2024) of the 2,624 players listed in the 2024 squads of the English, Spanish, Italian, German and French top divisions; 12,948 injury episodes from 2,061 players had a valuation in effect 120 days before the injury start and a valuation update after the 120 days following the injury end, and the outcome was the percentage change between these two valuations. Kruskal–Wallis tests with effect sizes, Dunn pairwise comparisons and linear regression models with player-clustered standard errors were used; age interactions were tested with joint Wald tests, and an exploratory matched-control comparison assessed differences in log-value change between injured players and injury-free player-periods matched on league, position group, age and baseline market value. Clearing the Air About Psychedelic Spirituality
abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapy occasions mystical experiences and their intensity often predicts therapeutic outcomes. Owing to their spiritual import, psychedelics have been linked to supernatural thinking, religions, and cults. Several authors within the psychedelic field argue these associations render the field scientifically and ethically questionable, with some calling for the ‘mystical framework’ of therapy to be replaced. This paper examines the controversy surrounding psychedelic spirituality to diagnose the issue and offer proposals for easing tensions. We argue that the question of the veracity of mystical insights is the primary source of controversy, but is a philosophical rather than scientific question and can, for now, be bracketed. We also argue that despite the charge of guruism and cultishness, researchers should be free to hold personal beliefs about the truth of these insights. Given their profession, however, they ought to remain agnostic about such insights and maintain values and views inherent to the ethos of science in their professional conduct.

abstract: This study presents the adaptive three-expert ensemble (A3E), a reproducible framework for joint one-hour-ahead solar and wind power forecasting. A3E combines temporal, physically informed, and high-generation Extra Trees experts through a causal local-error gate and is evaluated under a strictly chronological, leakage-free protocol. After timestamp reconciliation and causal feature construction, the primary source yielded 8,700 model-ready observations: 5,775 for training, 1,463 for validation, 719 for internal testing, and 743 for a same-source December holdout. The primary scale-neutral comparison used Macro train-SD normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) on 672 common forecast origins. A3E achieved 0.1978, compared with 0.2314 for the official photovoltaic (PV)-Client 2026 comparator and 0.2340 for TimeMixer. However, validation-optimized static weights achieved 0.2017 on the complete 719-origin internal test, compared with 0.2025 for adaptive A3E; the difference was not statistically significant under dependence-aware analysis. On the independent CISO and ERCO systems, TimeMixer outperformed A3E, demonstrating source-dependent model rankings. Event evaluation used 98 CISO and 320 ERCO high-generation events. The results support the value of heterogeneous expert integration, but not a universal accuracy advantage of adaptive weighting.

EXPERIMENTAL AND NUMERICAL MODAL ANALYSIS OF GASTRONORM FOOD-SERVICE CONTAINER
abstract: Stainless-steel gastronorm (GN) containers, commonly used in food-service operations, are widely employed for food storage, handling, and transportation. However, despite their extensive industrial utilization, scientific studies addressing their structural dynamics and modal behavior remain very limited. The aim of this study is to identify the modal parameters of the GN container in two distinct states: empty and filled with 10 liters of water. In parallel, a finite element model accounting for the thin-walled geometry of the container is developed to enable numerical simulation of its dynamic behavior. Numerical results are compared with experimental data, and the model is subsequently updated to achieve strong correlation between numerical and experimental modal parameters. The results show that the first natural frequency of the empty container is 133.2 Hz, corresponding to the torsion of the rim. Filling the container with 10 liters of water causes a significant decrease in this frequency to 54.1 Hz and leads to a modification of the mode shape. The obtained results provide deeper insight into the vibration behavior of GN containers and confirm the suitability of combining experimental and numerical approaches for the analysis of thin-walled structures used in food-service applications.

Reproducing and Predicting the Shear Band Characteristics of Geomaterials Using a Novel Multiscale Coupling Finite-Element Method
abstract: Abstract Soil is a multiphase and multiscale geomaterial. The failure of soil is a multiscale and hierarchical deformation process, and the onset and development of the shear band of soil is the pivotal factor for evaluating the strength and stability of soil. A multiscale coupling finite-element program based on the soil cell element model was developed to investigate the effects of solid is written to study the effect of the particle kinematics of solid particles on the onset and development of the shear band of soil. The results indicate that the multiscale FEM can relate the microscopic particle characteristics to the macroscopic mechanical response and resolve the pathological mesh dependence problem of the traditional FEM; the rotational displacement of soil particles concentrates within the shear band; the shear band width and normalized shear band width increase with increasing reinforcement particle diameter and have a linear dependence on the diameter of those particles. The evolution of plastic deformation that is induced and transmitted by the rotation of reinforcement particles is the microscopic physical mechanism of the trans-scale evolution of the shear band of soil.

The trials were conducted in a commercial grower’s field each year and managed the same way as their crop. Cultivar treatments were replicated three times and arranged in a randomized complete block design. Two harvests were conducted in 2024 and three in 2025. Fruit were separated into marketable and unmarketable categories and weighed. Stress Responses of Soft Ground under Vehicle and Temperature Loads Considering Pavement Thermal Sensitivity
abstract: Abstract An analytical multilayered road system is presented to evaluate stress responses of soft ground subjected to vehicle and temperature loads, and the temperature-dependent characteristics of the asphalt pavement are also considered. The soft ground is simulated as a coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical half-space, while a thermomechanical model is applied to represent the behaviors of other road layers. Key assumptions include linear poroelastic soil behavior and idealized drainage conditions at the ground surface. A circle impact vehicle load and a sinusoidal thermal load act on the top surface. The Laplace–Hankel transform is applied to solve the whole model, and an integration process is performed to obtain the final time-domain results. It is found that the vehicle and temperature loads, as well as pavement thermal sensitivity, can all induce obvious stress responses in the soft ground. Compared to the responses induced only by the vehicle load, pore pressure amplitude in the poroelastic half-space increases by 45.4% when the temperature load is also applied, and the increase reaches 75.2% when the thermal sensitivity of the asphalt pavement is further considered.

abstract: To balance NOX emissions and performance in ammonia-fueled marine engines, this study investigates exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) effects on combustion, performance, and emissions, and proposes a full-load EGR strategy. Based on a validated CFD model of a methanol/diesel dual-fuel engine and an ammonia spray model, an ammonia/diesel dual-fuel engine model was developed. Simulations at four typical loads were conducted with various EGR rates. Results show that higher EGR slows ammonia combustion, prolongs combustion duration, intensifies after-burning, and increases ammonia emissions. Heat release rate is load-dependent, with peaks regulated by EGR. Engine performance varies with load: the gross indicated mean effective pressure (IMEPg) increases with EGR at low-to-medium loads, but first rises then decreases at high loads. EGR effectively reduces NOX emissions at all loads, with maximum reduction ranging from 71.5 % to 90.2 %. Fuel NOX shows higher sensitivity to EGR than thermal NOX. However, EGR also increases ammonia and N2O emissions—marginal at low loads but significant at medium-to-high loads, with a distinct surge threshold. Recommended EGR rates are 50 %, 40 %, 30 %, and 10 % at 25 %, 50 %, 75 %, and 100 % loads, respectively. This strategy enables compliance with IMO Tier III NOX regulations, achieves low ammonia and N2O emissions, and improves IMEPg.

abstract: This research is a qualitative systematic review examining technology-enhanced Kazakh language teaching in multilingual educational environments through socio-pedagogical and neurolinguistic frameworks. The findings are presented around four research questions. First, it was determined that social media tools and digital platforms reinforce students' Kazakh language use practices and facilitate identity repositioning. abstract: Abstract The objective of this study was to determine the effect of full-scale experiential learning modules (ELMs) on student understanding of steel behavior in an undergraduate steel design course. Instructors at two universities taught an introductory steel design course with traditional teaching methods for 2 years. The following 2 years, the instructors taught the same course using the same methods with the addition of the full-scale ELMs to better visualize steel behavior and failure mechanisms. Three exam questions on the topics related to the ELMs were given at both universities. The responses to these problems were scored based on the number of correct statements made, awarding a point for each correct statement. How to Build the Right Coalition
abstract: Abstract: In competitive authoritarian and autocratic contexts, political parties win elections more frequently by running as public unity coalitions. However, in eroding democracies, voters are often highly polarized. The incumbent often won because the main opposition party was disliked by a plurality or majority of voters. Joining with such a tainted party can harm candidates’ chances. Where elected leaders are eroding once-strong democracies, opposition parties often do better with quiet coalitions in which parties remain fully independent but work together; choosing not to run against one another, or competing electorally to offer voters’ choice, but promising to caucus together post-election.

Transnational Gold Smuggling and the Making of Hong Kong’s Financial Hub, 1944–1973
abstract: Abstract: This article reinterprets Hong Kong’s postwar ascent by placing gold smuggling at the heart of its political economy. Challenging the narratives that credit only formal financial institutions, it shows how unregulated gold flows supplied the liquidity that propelled the colony from an entrepôt to a regional financial hub. Drawing on 1944–1968 court transcripts, police files, colonial correspondence, and newspapers, the study reconstructs the transnational corridors that ferried gold from Australia, Southeast Asia, and South Asia through Hong Kong to high-premium destinations such as Singapore and Calcutta. The Hong Kong colonial authorities’ policy of calculated underenforcement effectively transformed bullion into a stateless reserve asset. These shadow credit pools broadened Hong Kong’s foreign-exchange expertise and reshaped its postwar political economy. By foregrounding the networks that made this possible, the article offers a bottom-up perspective on state power, legality, and financial agency in Cold War Hong Kong.

title: Elementos normativos para el desarrollo de un mercado de combustibles renovables
abstract: La descarbonización para alcanzar la neutralidad climática en 2050 requiere diversas soluciones tecnológicas, donde los combustibles renovables constituyen una pieza necesaria, especialmente en sectores difícilmente electrificables directamente. La regulación y el desarrollo tecnológico son imprescindibles para reducir costes y fomentar el mercado de combustibles renovables. Sin embargo, la regulación puede incluir elementos que supongan barreras para las inversiones en combustibles renovables. Este artículo, a partir de un proceso de investigación cualitativa que combina la revisión de diversas fuentes bibliográficas y las aportaciones de un grupo de debate, presenta el contexto regulatorio en Europa y en España. A continuación, se presentan y analizan tres cuestiones genéricas (neutralidad tecnológica, flexibilidad normativa y cooperación regulatoria) y cuatro específicas de la regulación de los combustibles renovables (criterios de sostenibilidad, sunset clause del CO2 renovable, infraestructura e incentivos públicos), claves para su desarrollo. El documento concluye con una síntesis de las principales conclusiones.

title: Do workload and job stress always reduce employee performance? A study of employees in a state-owned electricity utility
abstract: Workload and job stress are commonly regarded as factors that undermine employee performance. However, their effects may differ across organizational and occupational settings. This study examines the effects of workload and job stress on employee performance at PT PLN (Persero) UP3 Lhokseumawe, a state-owned electricity distribution unit in Aceh, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory survey design was employed. Data were collected using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire from 55 employees selected through total sampling and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The findings reveal that workload and job stress each have a positive and statistically significant effect on employee performance. They also jointly contribute significantly to variations in employee performance. These results challenge the conventional assumption that work demands and occupational stress invariably reduce performance. Within the operational context of a public electricity utility, manageable work demands and performance pressure may encourage employees to maintain focus, discipline, responsibility, and responsiveness in delivering essential public services. Nevertheless, the findings should not be interpreted as justification for imposing excessive workloads or increasing employee stress. title: Forecast accuracy vs. Decision value in electricity price forecasting for power-to-X off-take agreements
abstract: Power-to-X (PtX) systems are emerging as key technologies in the transition to low-carbon fuels by converting renewable electricity into chemical energy carriers. Since electricity costs represent a major share of total production cost, accurate electricity price forecasts are essential for both the economic operation and contract design of PtX systems. However, forecasting models are typically evaluated using statistical error metrics that do not necessarily reflect their economic value in operational decision-making. This study proposes a decision-focused forecasting framework that integrates a Threshold-Aware Residual Network (TARN) with a Monte Carlo simulation based on a Mean-Reversion Jump-Diffusion (MRJD) process to improve the evaluation of PtX off-take agreements under electricity price uncertainty. The results demonstrate that superior statistical accuracy does not necessarily translate into superior economic performance, highlighting the importance of decision-focused forecasting for robust PtX contract assessment and investment decisions.

title: Quantification of Power Grid Frequency Regulation Capacity Demand Based on Deviation Prediction
abstract: Driven by global decarbonization goals, the rapid growth of renewable generation is increasing the frequency-regulation burden on power systems. Reliable estimates of regulation-capacity demand are therefore essential for coordinated energy and ancillary-services market clearing and secure grid operation. We develop a data-driven method that captures renewable variability while quantifying this demand accurately. The method uses renewable output, load fluctuations and meteorological conditions as predictors, with the maximum one-minute net-load deviation over each interval defining the target capacity. To address scale imbalance and redundant high-dimensional inputs, we introduce a dual screening procedure for training samples and features based on an improved weighted Euclidean distance. A deep neural network (DNN) then produces deterministic capacity forecasts, while adaptive-bandwidth kernel density estimation (ABKDE) models their residual errors. The upper confidence bound of the resulting prediction interval is used as the required regulation capacity. Tests on 2023 operating data from a provincial power grid yielded a spring-scenario mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.62% and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 98.31%. title: Physics-informed sparse deep neural networks for ultra-fast solar power forecasting and frequency response support in ancillary service markets
abstract: The rising penetration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into the current power grid leads to large variations and uncertainties, which are key challenges to frequency stability and reliable auxiliary services. In this research, a novel Physics-Informed Sparse Deep Neural Network (PI-SDNN) framework is proposed for quick and accurate solar power forecasting specially built to enable fast frequency response (FFR) in auxiliary service markets. The proposed approach incorporates domain-specific physical constraints such as irradiance-power correlations, inverter dynamics and ramp-rate limitations, in a sparsity-promoting deep learning framework, which facilitates superior generalization, lower computational complexity and improved interpretability. The PI-SDNN model exploits structured physics-informed regularization to capture rich spatiotemporal features from high-resolution meteorological and historical generation data. The approach ensures fast inference suitable for real-time grid operations while preserving the forecasting accuracy in highly dynamic environmental scenarios. Furthermore, the forecasting findings are strongly related to a frequency response support module for proactive deployment and reserve allocation of solar-integrated ancillary services. Extensive simulations on real solar datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms classical deep learnin…

title: Distributionally Robust Optimization-Based Dynamic Pricing Model and Solution Method for Multiple Virtual Power Plants in a Stackelberg Game
abstract: [Objective] To address the Stackelberg game between multiple virtual power plants （VPP） and a distribution system operator （DSO）， where existing dynamic pricing models fail to adequately account for the impact of renewable energy output uncertainty on game strategies， and conventional solution methods suffer from poor performance in high-dimensional decision spaces， this paper proposes a dynamic pricing model and solution method based on distributionally robust optimization （DRO） within a Stackelberg game framework. [Methods] A Stackelberg game dynamic pricing model is formulated with the DSO as the leader and multiple VPPs as followers. In the VPP optimization subproblem， a distributionally robust chance constraint is introduced to capture wind power output uncertainty. An ambiguity set is constructed using only the first and second moments of wind power， and the chance constraint is transformed into a deterministic equivalent via the Cantelli inequality. Moreover， a neural network-enhanced regional particle swarm optimization （NN‑RPSO） algorithm is proposed， which constructs a predictive model of VPP behavior to replace frequent calls to the lower‑level optimization， and incorporates a regional partitioning strategy to enable efficient search. title: E-Infinity Ecosystem: Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Using X-Changer and Energinx Smart Meters for Reverse Power Flow Prevention
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading in industrial settings is rarely validated with metered data. This paper studies the E-Infinity Ecosystem, coupling the X-Changer trading platform with Energinx IoT smart meters that limit reverse power flow (RPF) at the meter, deployed at a ceramic factory in Saraburi, Thailand. Contributions include (i) coupling meter-level export limitation with interval-level bilateral matching under conventional billing; (ii) an analytical bound on export above the admitted level; (iii) a proof that two-building allocation loses no energy relative to pooled metering; and (iv) metered evidence with uncertainty, economic, and benchmark analysis. Two PV buildings were metered at 10 min intervals over 118 days (January–April 2025): Building 1 generated 573,082 kWh (14.47% self-sufficiency) and Building 2 309,484 kWh (21.10%), with roles following the PV-to-load ratio. Estimated trading potential was 44,275 kWh (96.3% from Building 2 to Building 1), avoiding 185,953 THB at 4.2 THB/kWh. A 12-month dataset gave a 90.00 ± 0.33% matching rate and a ±7.8% seasonal interval on annual volume. Volumes are meter-based estimates; RPF suppression and control dynamics were not measured directly.

title: A low-carbon economic bidding strategy for power generators considering multi-market coupling: a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach
abstract: The coupling of electricity, carbon, and tradable green certificate markets is expected to reshape generation companies’ (GENCOs’) bidding strategies. To support power-sector decarbonization and improve strategic bidding decisions, this paper proposes a multi-layer electricity market clearing framework integrating carbon trading and tradable green certificates (TGC). A non-convex multi-segment bidding model is developed for GENCOs to capture the joint effects of generation costs and environmental compliance costs on bidding offers. In addition, a Beta-distribution-based multi-agent proximal policy optimization method (MAPPO-Beta) is adopted to solve the complex bidding problem under incomplete information and improve GENCOs’ market payoffs. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system show that MAPPO-Beta outperforms benchmark algorithms in reward performance and training stability, with an average reward improvement of 10.2%. Its effectiveness is further verified on the IEEE 118-bus system. Comparative analysis indicates that carbon trading is more effective in constraining high-emission thermal power generators, whereas TGC improves the bidding competitiveness of renewable energy generators. The results reveal clear strategy evolution after introducing carbon trading and TGC: low-emission thermal generators tend to submit more competitive bids with higher declared capacities and lo…

title: A distributional modelling approach with application to electricity price forecasting
abstract: The increasing volatility of electricity prices driven by renewable energy integration, market shocks, and regulatory changes has reinforced the need for forecasting methods that go beyond point predictions and accurately describe the full conditional price distribution. This paper applies the Generalised Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) framework to forecast Spanish day-ahead electricity prices using hourly data from 2020 to 2024. Alternative specifications based on Normal, Johnson's SU (JSU), and Sinh-Arcsinh (SHASH) distributions are considered, allowing the location, scale, and shape parameters to vary with market fundamentals, including electricity demand, renewable generation, seasonal effects, and regulatory and geopolitical risk factors. Forecasts are generated using a rolling-window approach and evaluated through the mean absolute error (MAE), pinball loss, and Diebold-Mariano tests. The results show that flexible distributional specifications improve forecasting performance relative to a naive benchmark and the standard normal specification. While SHASH and JSU specifications provide the lowest point forecasting errors, the hourly analysis reveals substantial intraday variation in relative performance across specifications. JSU specification with all four parameters driven by covariates achieves the best probabilistic forecasting performance, par…

title: Aggregated Bidirectional Wireless Charging Hubs as Virtual Power Plants: Coordinated Frequency Containment Reserve Provision and Reactive Power Dispatch in Distribution Networks
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) is creating new challenges for distribution networks, but the same batteries that increase charging demand can also provide valuable flexibility when coordinated as distributed energy resources. This paper investigates the use of aggregated bidirectional wireless charging hubs as a virtual power plant (VPP) capable of simultaneously providing frequency containment reserve (FCR), active-power balancing, and reactive-power support while preserving EV users’ mobility requirements. A coordinated control and optimization framework is developed in which multiple wireless charging hubs are aggregated at the supervisory level while local charging decisions account for vehicle availability, state of charge (SOC), departure requirements, converter limits, battery constraints, and distribution-network operating conditions. The VPP dynamically determines upward and downward FCR capacity and coordinates bidirectional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) active-power exchange with reactive-power dispatch to support both system frequency and local voltage conditions. The framework is evaluated using time-domain simulations of a modified distribution network under variations in EV availability, charging demand, renewable generation, load, and frequency disturbances. Compared with uncoordinated charging, the proposed strategy reduces peak grid demand by approximatel…

title: Robust benefit optimization for virtual power plants with incentive compatible control rights transfer for user-side storage
abstract: User-side battery storage often struggles to be profitable when revenue is restricted to time-of-use arbitrage, motivating business models that can unlock additional value through coordinated operation. This paper proposes a virtual power plant (VPP)–controlled framework in which users retain ownership of their energy storage systems while transferring charging and discharging control rights to the VPP under an incentive-compatible compensation mechanism that guarantees non-decreasing user net benefit. On this basis, a VPP profit-maximization model is developed to co-optimize thermal generation, wind and PV utilization, and aggregated user-side storage, subject to portfolio power balance, mode-dependent state-of-charge dynamics, rated power limits, and cycle-life-related degradation costs. Renewable curtailment penalties and settlement rules are explicitly embedded, enabling storage charging to be shifted toward renewable-rich periods and discharging to be scheduled in high-value periods while maintaining user participation constraints. Case studies demonstrate that coordinated control improves renewable-energy absorption, reduces wind/PV curtailment, and increases portfolio profitability, while a feasible compensation band is identified to support contract negotiation and tariff design. The proposed framework further provides implementable guidance on when to activate control …

title: Internet of Things (IOT)-Enabled Smart Microgrids for Off-Grid Electrification in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: This study explores the technical and economic potential of IoT-enabled smart microgrids as a sustainable solution for off-grid rural electrification in Sub-Saharan Africa. Using a thematic, literature-based approach, the research investigates how smart microgrids— integrating renewable energy sources such as solar with IoT technologies—can improve energy access, reliability, and cost-efficiency in underserved communities. Findings indicate that, unlike traditional diesel-based or non-smart off-grid systems, IoT-enabled microgrids offer significant advantages through real-time monitoring, automated control, predictive maintenance, and load optimization. These systems reduce operational costs, improve system lifespan, and enable responsive load management tailored to varying consumption patterns and environmental conditions. Case studies from Nigeria, Lesotho, Rwanda, and Namibia support these conclusions, showing improved energy performance, reduced fuel dependency, and enhanced user engagement through mobile platforms and peer-to-peer energy trading. The study also highlights the importance of scalability and community inclusion, noting that IoT features allow gradual system expansion based on real-time data and usage trends. Through conceptual illustrations and comparative diagrams, the study presents a clear contrast between smart and conventional microgrid models, reinforci…

Prioritization, patient selection, and multimodal perioperative management of colorectal cancer facing health-care system saturation
DIGITAL TWIN AND SOFTWARE OBSERVABILITY FRAMEWORK FOR PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT IN ENTERPRISE INFORMATION SYSTEMS
abstract: Enterprise information systems contain interconnected applications, APIs, databases, cloud resources, and infrastructure whose performance can change under varying workloads and service conditions. Conventional monitoring provides metrics, logs, traces, and events, but these signals often offer limited support for future performance prediction, dependency analysis, and operational response. This study presents a Digital Twin and Software Observability Framework for predictive performance management in enterprise information systems. The framework combines multimodal telemetry with a dynamic Digital Twin representation of service health, workload conditions, performance indicators, configuration information, and dependencies. Machine-learning models estimate abnormal behavior and service degradation risk, while a dependency-aware decision module evaluates potential downstream effects and recommends operational actions. Evaluation uses Train Ticket, Online Boutique, and Sock Shop microservice environments, public failure datasets, synthetic workloads, and controlled fault scenarios. The proposed framework achieved a Precision of 0.914, Recall of 0.902, F1-score of 0.908, and AC@k of 0.861, with an MTTD of 11.4 seconds. Results indicate that the integrated framework supports predictive diagnosis and operational decision making under incomplete trace coverage.

title: MULTI-OBJECTIVE PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE AND ENERGY-AWARE RESOURCE OPTIMIZATION FOR SMART INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS
abstract: Smart industrial systems must balance equipment reliability, energy use, maintenance cost, production continuity, and technical resources. This study proposes a multi-objective predictive maintenance and energy-aware resource optimization framework for industrial decision-making. The framework combines equipment health assessment, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, anomaly detection, failure probability, and maintenance prioritization. K-means clustering determines the Anomaly Level (AL), while Weibull survival analysis estimates Failure Probability (FP). These measures form a Hybrid Risk Index (HRI) for determining the Optimal Maintenance Point (OMP). NSGA-II evaluates maintenance timing, asset selection, and technician allocation under maintenance cost, energy, quality, and production objectives. Performance is compared with preventive maintenance, condition based maintenance, and reliability only optimization under changing industrial conditions.

abstract: Purpose: To investigate the moderating effect of Organizational factors on the relationship between occupational safety and health practises and performance of electricity distribution contracted firms in Western Kenya Methodology: The study employed a descriptive correlational research design and adopted positivism research philosophy. Data was presented through tables. Data analysis was based on descriptive and inferential statistics. Findings: organizational factors had a positive significant moderating effect on the relationship between occupational safety practices and Performance of electricity distribution contracted firms. Value: Organizational leadership should actively support safety initiatives through clear policies, communication and resource allocation.

title: Performance and Risk-Return Dynamics of Top Indian Mutual Fund Schemes across Market Capitalizations: An Empirical Evaluation
abstract: In a complex financial environment, investors face continuous trade-offs between risk, return, and portfolio volatility across asset management companies (AMCs). While traditional bank fixed deposits offer capital safety, equity-oriented mutual funds have emerged as the primary engine for long-term wealth creation in India due to active professional management and portfolio diversification. This empirical study evaluates the risk-return performance of top equity-oriented mutual fund schemes across Large-Cap, Mid-Cap, and Small-Cap categories offered by the top five Indian AMCs by Assets Under Management (AUM): SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund. Utilizing key quantitative risk metrics—Standard Deviation (sigma), Beta (beta), Sharpe Ratio, Treynor Ratio, and Jensen's Alpha—this paper measures risk-adjusted performance alongside expense ratios across market capitalizations. The findings provide actionable insights for retail and institutional investors constructing goal-aligned portfolios under the evolving regulatory framework governed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

title: Corporate Governance, Financial Policy, and Corporate Investment Efficiency: Rethinking the Role of Family Ownership in Emerging Market
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to determine the effect of corporate governance mechanisms and financial policy on the efficiency of corporate investment and to examine the moderating role of family ownership in the emerging market. Design/Methodology/Approach: Using panel regression techniques, the study tests the proposed relationships using balanced panel data from non-financial companies listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) for 2015 to 2022. Findings: The study shows that board independence, CEO duality, CEO qualifications enhance investment efficiency, while board gender diversity has a negative relationship with investment efficiency. Likewise, financial leverage reduces investment efficiency, while dividend policy improves it. Family ownership is an important boundary condition: it strengthens the positive relationship between CEO duality, CEO qualifications, and Corporate investment efficiency, and the negative relationship between financial leverage and investment efficiency. Practical implications: These insights will help regulators develop family business governance codes, remind boards of the advantages of CEO duality and qualifications for capital allocation, advise family businesses against over-leverage, and demonstrate an efficient way to invest by focusing on dividend policy. Originality/Value: It is the first study to consider governance mechanisms, financial…

title: Retail Investor Prediction in India’s Stock Market Using Complex-Value Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Neural Network for Demographic Analysis and Risk Assessment
abstract: Retail investor participation in India’s stock market has been increasing, driven by improved access to digital platforms and rising financial literacy. However, this surge leads to higher volatility and exposes investors to significant risks if they lack proper knowledge or experience in market dynamics. To overcome this problem, in this paper, retail investor prediction in India’s stock market for demographic analysis and risk assessment (RIP-ISM-CVSTGCNN) is proposed. The model utilizes financial time-series data from the Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) stock dataset, integrated with investor demographic and behavioral attributes to enable comprehensive analysis. The data are pre-processed utilizing implicit unscented particle filter (IUPF), which is employed to clean the data. Then the pre-processed data are fed into a complex-value spatio-temporal graph convolutional neural network (CVSTGCNN) to forecast demographic factors along with a quantitative risk score that reflects the investor’s financial risk level. The proposed model is evaluated using multiple performance metrics, including precision, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score and AUC. Results show that the RIP-ISM-CVSTGCNN method achieves an accuracy of 97.3%, precision of 96.3%, sensitivity of 96.3%, specificity of 96.3%, F1-score of 96.6% and an AUC of 0.97. Comparative analysis with existing methods, inc…

title: Pertumbuhan Aset dan Net Profit Margin terhadap Nilai Perusahaan Konstruksi di Bursa Efek Indonesia Berbasis Market Value Added 2020-2024
abstract: This study is driven by the tendency of several construction firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) to expand their assets rapidly without a corresponding rise in market-perceived firm value, with some even posting low or negative Net Profit Margins (NPM). The aim is to describe and analyze asset growth, NPM, and firm value proxied by Market Value Added (MVA) among IDX-listed construction sub-sector companies from 2020 to 2024. Using a quantitative descriptive approach, the study draws on secondary data from audited annual reports (idx.co.id) and share price data (finance.yahoo.com). Purposive sampling yielded 8 firms and 40 firm-year observations. Findings show a mean asset growth rate of 2.38%, mean NPM of -4.52%, and mean MVA of -Rp2,494.64 billion. Notably, 62.5% of observations combined positive NPM with negative MVA, and 50% combined positive asset growth with negative MVA—pointing to a pattern of growth unaccompanied by shareholder value creation in the IDX construction sector.

Market Overview of Lost Foam Metal Casting and Forecast of Its Growth Until 2033 with Prospects of Development and Technology Digitalization
abstract: The article presents a comprehensive analysis of the current state, macroeconomic trends, and technological prospects for the development of the Lost Foam Casting (LFC) process, dedicated to its 70th anniversary. Based on current monitoring data from global analytical agencies Grand View Research and Precedence Research, a stable expansion dynamics of the global LFC market is demonstrated, with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 7.2% up to 2033. This growth is driven by the modernization of industrial production lines and the global transition to Industry 4.0 standards. Particular attention is paid to the scientific and technological experience of the Physico-Technological Institute of Metals and Alloys of the NAS of Ukraine in the field of digital transformation of pattern production. The concept of introducing additive manufacturing methods, specifically 3D printing of porous polymer patterns, is considered, which allows eliminating the capital-intensive and time-consuming stage of designing and manufacturing traditional metal tooling (molds). A significant advantage of integrating 3D-printed patterns is justified in terms of the absence of the need to recertify existing foundry shop structures, since the metallurgical essence of the casting process and the certification criteria for the final castings remain unchanged. The unexploited potential of the physicoc…

title: HOW CAN A SMALL DESTINATION BECOME A “RISING STAR” IN THE MODERN COMPETITIVE TOURISM MARKET? EVIDENCE FROM THE PHILIPPINES
abstract: This review study aims to analyze how a small island destination, exemplified by Samal in the Davao Gulf (Philippines), can achieve rapid tourism growth and transition into a competitive regional destination. It seeks to identify key drivers and strategies behind its successful development. The research examines the pathways by which a small island destination can transform into a “rising star” in the contemporary tourism market. The research employed a review-based approach combining secondary tourism data from 2015 to 2024 with a detailed case study analysis of Samal Island. The study employed a destination development framework to evaluate the impact of institutional, environmental, and socio-economic factors on growth. The findings indicate that Samal’s tourism growth is driven by interconnected elements, including sustainable practices, the utilization of cultural and natural resources, and collaborative governance. These factors collectively enhanced the island’s visibility and competitiveness in Southeast Asia’s tourism landscape. The study concludes that even small, resource-limited destinations can reposition themselves successfully in regional tourism hierarchies through sustainable management, effective cooperation among stakeholders, and strategic leveraging of local assets. The contribution of this research lies in providing review evidence from the emerging island…

title: Time to First Job after College Graduation: Associations with Career Support Participation and Job-Market Credentials
abstract: This study examined how participation in university career support activities and job-market credentials are associated with the speed of the school-to-work transition among Korean college graduates after excluding those continuously employed in main or concurrent wage jobs through the month of graduation. Using waves 1-8 of the KEEP II, this study reconstructed job histories to identify and exclude graduates continuously employed in main or concurrent wage jobs through graduation, and analyzed monthly event-history data for 2,590 graduates with Kaplan-Meier estimates and discrete-time hazard models using a complementary log-log link. Four findings emerged. First, the median time to first job was seven months, and the employment hazard peaked one to two months after graduation before declining. Second, the number of certificates obtained before graduation was consistently associated with faster transition across all model specifications and sensitivity analyses, whereas the breadth of career support participation, measured as counts of activities ever experienced, showed no significant association and the association of overseas study experience was unstable across event definitions. Third, stratified models suggested gendered patterns, but none of the gender interactions were statistically significant, so these contrasts are interpreted as exploratory heterogeneity. Fourth, fo…

Market Stability as a Boundary Condition for Smallholder Spice Production: Evidence from Zanzibar, Tanzania
abstract: Purpose: To assess the effects of capital sufficiency, labour competence, and entrepreneurial skills on the spice production of smallholder farmers in Zanzibar, as well as to assess if and how market stability conditions the strength of these associations. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employed a cross-sectional survey with a quantitative explanatory design grounded in the positivist philosophy. Out of a total population of 763 smallholder spice farmers in five regions of Unguja and Pemba, a sample of 256 farmers was selected through stratified and simple random sampling, respectively. The sample size was determined using the Krejcie and Morgan (1970) table at a confidence level of 95% and a margin of Error of 5%. A total of 214 valid responses (83.6%) were analysed using Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA)-based Structural Equation Modelling in IBM SPSS AMOS 28. Findings: Capital sufficiency, labour competence, and the entrepreneur’s skill are each positively and significantly related to spice production, with the entrepreneur’s skill having the strongest standardised effect. Keeping the above in mind, a multi-group moderation analysis sought to evaluate the role of market conditions in moderating. Meanwhile, in normal or stable market conditions, the relationship between farm resource allocation and farm output was insignificant. Implications/Originality/Value: The st…

Value Proposition, Differentiation, and Target Market Orientation in New Product Evaluation: Evidence From a Focus Group Study of the Television Program Shark Tank.
What Holds Its Value Price Determinants in Indias Used Motorcycle Market and the Absence of the Yamaha RX100
abstract: The Yamaha RX100 retains a strong reputation among Indian motorcycle enthusiasts, yet it does not appear once in 7,324 listings of used motorcycles offered for sale online in India. This paper starts from that absence and asks a broader question: what determines the asking price of a used two-wheeler in India? The data are a public, CC0-licensed file of listings scraped from the marketplace droom.in. The file holds 32,648 rows, but 25,324 of them are exact duplicates, leaving 7,324 distinct listings; the duplication is not disclosed by the publisher and is documented here. A hedonic regression explains 84.7 per cent of the variation in log asking price. Engine displacement, age and brand each carry a large partial effect, and asking price falls by about 7.1 per cent for each year of age. Ownership history matters much less than its place in every listing suggests: holding other attributes constant, a second-owner machine is listed 4.1 per cent below a comparable first-owner one (95 per cent confidence interval 1.4 to 6.7 per cent), and ownership has a partial η² of 0.002. A deliberate check for Simpson’s paradox found none: the negative relationship between age and price holds within every brand and every displacement band examined. Depreciation slows with age, and the fitted curve turns upward at about 25 years (bootstrap 95 per cent interval 19.7 to 30.0 years), but that uptu…

title: Innovation, Perceived Value, and Customer Satisfaction as Antecedents of Behavioural Intention: Evidence from the Terrarium Market in Bangkok, Thailand
abstract: Although increasing interest with respect to green products, little is known about how innovation affects perceived value, satisfaction, and behavioural intention within niche green product markets. This gap is particularly evident in the terrarium sector, where empirical evidence remains scarce, especially in the Thai context. To address this gap, this empirical study, which focused on the interrelation among innovation, perceived value, satisfaction, and behavioural intention determinants was carried out in Thailand’s terrarium market. A quantitative approach using an online survey was conducted with 400 sample participants. The study implemented a probability sampling method applying systematic random sampling to select the participants. A path analysis with latent variables employed structural equation modelling (SEM) to analyze the data via AMOS version 24. The findings indicate that perceived value is the most influential factor significantly affecting customers' behavioural intention. Among its dimensions, perceived emotional value and perceived functional value emerged as the strongest indicators. Innovation was identified as the second most influential factor, with marketing, service, and cultural innovation serving as its strongest indicators. Satisfaction ranked as the third most influential factor, with meaningfulness and affordability identified as its most importa…

title: Aligning education with labour market needs: a scoping review of strategies to address the employment skills gap
abstract: Purpose This scoping review systematically identifies strategies reported between 2015 and 2025 to align post-secondary education and training with labour market demands to address employment skills gaps and mismatches. Design/methodology/approach This study follows the Arksey and O'Malley model for conducting a scoping review, as extended by Levac et al., and is presented in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR protocol. The study uses a three-stage approach to database and grey literature searches, drawing on prominent databases (e.g. Scopus, Web of Science and ERIC) and grey literature sources (e.g. ILO, UNESCO, OECD and World Bank). The data are charted using a standardised form and synthesised descriptively. Theoretical coding is grounded in human capital theory and signalling theory. Findings From 60 studies, this review highlights two different yet overlapping logics through which education realises employability. One logic involves capability building through curriculum and pedagogical innovations, workplace-based learning, reskilling and the development of employability capitals. The other logic involves signalling through co-constructed assessment approaches, portfolios, artefacts, validated learning and quality assurance that make the capabilities credible and intelligible to employers. Although the research involved multiple geographic locations, it is uneven and dominate…

title: Effect of Health and Safety awareness on Performance of Electricity Distribution Contracted Firms in Western Region, Kenya
abstract: Purpose: To determine the effect of health and safety awareness on performance of electricity distribution contracted firms in Western region, Kenya. Methodology: The study employed a descriptive correlational research design and adopted positivism research philosophy. The study targeted 546 stakeholders comprising 48 CEOs and 498 technicians. The study sampled 270 stakeholders consisting of 222 technicians and 48 CEOs. The 48 CEOs were purposively selected for interviews to triangulate vital information, while systematic random sampling was used for technicians. The study area included the four counties in the Western Region of Kenya and targeted all CEOs or directors and technicians of registered electricity distribution contracted firms in the region. Open and closed-ended questionnaires were applied from technicians, while interviews with CEOs were conducted to obtain additional information for triangulation. A pilot study was conducted in Trans-Nzoia County. Quantitative data were analyzed using both descriptive and inferential statistics. Descriptive statistics included frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations, while inferential statistics included simple regression, multiple regression, and hierarchical regression models. The data were presented using figures and tables. Findings: The study found that health and safety awareness significantly influenced t…
